Handler ordering means a tool removed by one extension can still be advertised to the model if another handler forces a system prompt. This is an extension-composition correctness bug with real security-adjacent implications (capability leakage).
  3. #11317 [OPEN] Let SDK users customize the identity preamble without replacing default sections — 5 comments. Requests systemPromptOptions.sections.preamble so personas can be set without hand-rebuilding Pi's tools/rules/docs. Paired with PR #11904 (already closed).
  4. #11869 [OPEN] [bug, inprogress, prio:p0] New StringEnum in Pi 1.5.0 breaks compile-time typing — 2 👍, the only p0 still open. registerTool derives TParam via typebox's TSchema, but the new StringEnum no longer does, so enum fields become unknown. Type safety in the tool-authoring surface is a headline regression.
  5. #10585 [OPEN] bash temp-file stream errors still crash the whole process on 1.0.4 — 4 comments. An ENOSPC on a full /tmp produces an uncaught exception and loses the in-flight session, with no tool error surfaced. Durability concern for long agent runs.
  6. #10650 [OPEN] codemode: preserve nested Error messages in allSettled output — 4 comments. Rejections serialize to reason: {}, so the model reasons over missing information. Directly degrades codemode's self-correction loop.
  7. #9817 [CLOSED] [no-action] Extensions can't resolve npm packages declared via package.json main/exports — 5 comments, 1 👍. Only packages with a root index.js resolve; yaml and similar fail at runtime. Closed without action, which leaves a sharp edge for the extension ecosystem.
  8. #11858 [CLOSED] [no-action] codemode script repeated an identical tool call 24,018 times — 3 comments. ~680 calls/s for 35 s, each reading a 28 KB file, stopped only by the wall-clock abort. No per-script repetition guard; a strong signal that sandbox guardrails are thin.
  9. #11876 [CLOSED] edit and read tools are bypassed by shell commands — 3 comments. On Windows 11 / 1.5.0 the model reached for sed, sidestepping tool instrumentation and rewriting line endings. Underscores the need for tool-preference steering.
  10. #8544 [CLOSED] edit rewrites line endings of untouched lines in mixed CRLF/LF files — 3 comments. Editing one character silently mutates bytes on other lines. Fixed by PR #11751; the related non-UTF-8 case is split out.

Also notable: #11676 (open, inprogress) Harness.close() retains provider WebSocket + idle timer; #11863 asks for context-management guidance for long-running embedded agents and was closed no-action.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11751 fix(coding-agent): edit keeps line endings of untouched lines — Rewrites only around the actual change and avoids the post-write diff OOM. The highest-impact data-integrity fix of the day.
  2. #11896 fix(coding-agent): wait for image resize worker to terminate — void worker.terminate() in finally let the next worker start mid-teardown; awaiting it stops the macOS arm64 / Node 24 process aborts.
  3. #11891 fix(ai): omit empty tools array for tool history on openai-completions — Unblocks vLLM 0.20+ and LiteLLM gateways that 400 on "tools": [].
  4. #11890 fix(tui): draw fullscreen Kitty images after the rows they cover — Fixes Orca/WezTerm xterm.js tile rendering, where only the first row of a fullscreen image appeared.
  5. #11888 fix(coding-agent): record the live thinking level on the branch before each prompt — Closes the stale-level-after-/tree-rewind resume bug (#11451).
  6. #11882 openai-completions: split tool-call blocks when stream index and id disagree — Prevents two distinct tool calls from being concatenated into one malformed argument blob by non-conforming providers.
  7. #11895 fix(coding-agent): match grep globs relative to path — Glob with a folder component now works when path isn't the cwd, instead of returning a false "No matches found".
  8. #11873 fix(coding-agent): keep apostrophes in prompt template arguments — /ask why doesn't the user's cache work no longer becomes why doesnt the users cache work.
  9. #11885 fix(ai): retry streams cut short after the reply had begun — Adds the Magpie/Anthropic mid-reply truncation message to RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN.
  10. #11894 [OPEN] fix(coding-agent): edit refuses files that are not valid UTF-8 — Currently the tool silently substitutes U+FFFD and reports success on UTF-16/GBK/Windows-1252 files. Still open; worth watching as the companion to #11751.

Also merged/closed: #11904 custom system prompt preamble, #11887 fullscreen stderr corruption, #11893 reasoning_effort now routed through thinkingLevelMap, #11874 Windows Bun virtual entry path, #11900 CONTRIBUTING RFC link. Still open: #11889 Windows console-close shutdown cleanup, #11878 codemode local tools/console declarations.

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11870 How do you keep skills organized across Pi and other agents? (1 👍, 0 comments) — Duplicate skills across Pi, Claude Code, and OpenCode directories drift apart; the author built a macOS app + CLI, AgentKeeper, to catalog them. No replies yet — an open invitation for the community to compare approaches to cross-agent skill/package management.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • SDK/embedding control surfaces. The clearest cluster: replaceable identity preamble without losing default sections (#11317, PR #11904), correct handler ordering for forced prompts vs. active tools (#9932), per-conversation compaction policy in pi-durable (#11771), queue-intent disposition reporting (#11872), and documented patterns for long, tool-heavy multimodal sessions (#11863). Users are past "can I embed Pi" and into "can I govern it."
  • Model catalog currency. Three separate requests to add models: k3.1-pro / video modality for kimi-coding (#11883), glm-5.3-flashx for zai (#11884), and deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 for qw (#11877). All closed no-action — suggesting a maintained catalog-update path is still missing.
  • Codemode robustness and sandboxing. Error fidelity in serialization (#10650), correct NaN/Infinity printing (#11901), repetition guardrails (#11858), and shadowed parameter names (#11878).
  • Accessibility and terminal fidelity. Screen-reader-safe rendering (#1188), fullscreen inline images across Kitty-capable terminals (#11835), and out-of-band stderr isolation (PR #11887).
  • Windows parity. SIGHUP-only shutdown handling (PR #11889) and the Bun SEA B:/~BUN/root/ entry path leaking into subagent argv (#11865).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent file corruption from edit. Mixed line endings (#8544) and non-UTF-8 encodings (#11894) both produce "success" while mutating bytes the user never touched. Trust in the edit tool is the recurring theme.
  • Unhandled errors that kill the process, not the tool call. ENOSPC on a full /tmp (#10585) and the worker teardown race (#10695) both lose the in-flight run. Users expect per-tool error boundaries; they're getting process aborts.
  • Model-hostile output from codemode. reason: {}, avg null, and 24k unguarded repeated calls all feed the model bad state or burn tokens with no guardrail (#10650, #11901, #11858).
  • Provider non-conformance leaking into Pi. Empty tools: [] (#11843), duplicate stream index (#11881), expired Copilot tokens returning 401/403 (#10238), and Kimi K2.7 printing thinking as the reply (#10237) — all closed, several no-action.
  • Extension ecosystem friction. npm packages using main/exports fail to resolve (#9817), and before_agent_start handler ordering is unspecified (#9932). Extension authors are absorbing platform gaps.
  • Resource and state lifecycle bugs in embedded use. Harness.close() leaving provider sessions and WebSockets alive (#11676) and stale thinking levels after /tree (#11451) are the kind of defects that only surface in long-lived host processes.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.26.9, headlined by a full skill installation and activation pipeline (ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections), alongside a same-day nightly. Issue traffic remains dominated by session/transcript durability problems — a P1 unopenable-session bug from quadratic snapshot growth (#13113) and a P1 headless auto-memory write denial (#15597) are both still open. Meanwhile the managed-agent surface is expanding fast, with two large PRs adding Skills/MCP self-service (#16500) and execution diagnostics plus an agent graph (#16498).

2. Releases

v0.26.9 — Release

  • No known breaking changes.
  • Skill installation and activation: skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing skills a first-class workflow rather than a manual file operation.

v0.26.9-nightly.20261106.80fd7c3353 — Release

  • Nightly cut from release/v0.26.9-nightly.20261106.80fd7c3353.
  • Test-infrastructure work: interactive tests now poll the foreground-shell frame instead of snapshotting it (#16455), plus managed-agent test adjustments.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #13113 — Session becomes unopenable: "Transcript snapshot is too large to index" (P1, 11 comments) file_history_snapshot grows quadratically and the 256 MiB index limit is hardcoded, so long sessions with many file touches become permanently unloadable — every POST /session/:id/load fails. This is the highest-severity durability bug in the tracker: it is silent, unrecoverable from the user's side, and blocks the core value proposition of long-running agent sessions.

  2. #15597 — Headless -p auto-memory can never save (P1, 8 comments) In non-interactive mode with default/Auto approval, the implicit edit/write_file deny overrides the memory agents' scoped allow. Memory runs after every prompt, writes nothing, and the user still pays for the tokens. A permission-precedence bug with a direct cost impact.

  3. #16418 — Repeated auto-compaction turns a review-only skill into unauthorized implementation (P1, 4 comments) A long-running session invoked /ce-doc-review (review + limited safe fixes only) and ended up implementing the plan in application source. Filed as Critical: this is a scope-adherence failure that surfaces only under compaction, which makes it a trust and safety concern rather than a routine bug.

  4. #16508 — Idle-time auto-compaction (P2, 3 comments) Proposal to run the summarizer while the user is away instead of mid-turn, so compaction latency never lands inside a user-visible turn and the next turn starts from an already-compacted, cacheable prefix. Filed 2026-11-07 and already paired with a design doc PR (#16509) — the fastest-moving idea in the tracker.

  5. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (218 comments) The single highest-traffic issue in the repo, open since 2026-10-19 and still accumulating bot comments. Symptomatically, the CI failure reporter cannot attribute a failing test, so the issue can never self-close. The comment count is a signal about bot noise and CI triage debt, not community interest.

  6. #15412 — Long project paths prevent chat recording and break the sessions list (P2, 7 comments) The per-project session directory is derived from the full absolute working directory and flattened into a single path component, which can exceed filesystem limits on macOS. Deeply nested monorepos silently lose chat history.

  7. #15310 — Tell the model which shell it uses instead of letting it assume bash (P3, 6 comments) On Windows, commands run through cmd.exe but nothing in the system prompt says so, so the model emits POSIX commands that cannot work. The reporter observed two wasted turns in a single unattended run — a cheap prompt fix with outsized reliability payoff.

  8. #16417 — Reject an oversized write_file before generating it (P2, 3 comments) A write_file larger than the remaining output budget is generated in full and only then rejected with Response truncated due to token limit. Nothing is written and the whole turn is lost; the reporter hit it three times on the same file. Clear argument for a pre-flight check against the output budget.

  9. #15800 — Background shell status file stays "running" forever after abrupt session end (P2, 3 comments) The background process completes, but its persisted status file never updates, leaving stale state that later sessions and tooling read as live. Part of a cluster of background-automation lifecycle gaps.

  10. #16444 — CLI background-view auto-surface UX edges (P3, 4 comments) Deferred from #16432: an auto-opened dialog becomes the Ctrl+C target, so the first interrupt dismisses the dialog instead of reaching the composer. Representative of the repo's disciplined "defer, don't drop" review culture — non-blocking findings are filed rather than lost.

Also worth noting: #15675 (sed simulation diverges from real sed — . doesn't match \r, emoji handling differs) closed after 5 comments; #15833 closed — cancelling a shell command used to tell the model "the tool had already completed."

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16500 — feat(managed-agent): Skills and MCP self-service Lets managed-agent operators manage Skills and MCP servers themselves rather than through maintainer intervention. The largest surface expansion in this window and the natural follow-on to the v0.26.9 skill pipeline.

  2. #16498 — feat(managed-agent): execution diagnostics and agent graph Adds persisted, session-owned tool/Skill usage, native file-operation and line-change measurements, and an authorized agent-relationship view. Notably keeps conversation outcomes separate from physical execution evidence, so a successful write stays visible after cancellation.

  3. #16432 — fix(cli): surface workflow agent approvals in the interactive TUI (#16425) Fixes a deadlock: a background workflow agent hitting a tool-approval gate parked the approval with nothing able to answer it, so the run never progressed. The registry now requires a real responder before parking.

  4. #16404 — fix(cli): surface stacked-skill overflow in non-interactive and ACP runs Warns when a prompt stacks more than five skills. Headless runs write to stderr (including under JSON/stream-JSON), ACP clients get a live notice before the model response, and channel bridges preserve it across tool round-trips.

  5. #16439 — fix(core): replay the persisted startup prelude on resume Resumed sessions now replay the exact startup prelude originally sent instead of rebuilding it from the current date, directory tree, git snapshot, MCP instructions, skills, and deferred-tool list. Directly improves prefix-cache reuse and resume determinism.

  6. #16509 — docs(core): design the idle-time auto-compaction pass Bilingual design doc for #16508, fixing the reviewable contract: dual-condition trigger (idle duration + soft watermark). Landed the same day as the issue — an unusually fast issue-to-design loop.

  7. #16507 — perf(core): compare a grown local journal prefix in chunks Follow-up to #16483: a file that grew during the read is now compared in 64 KiB chunks instead of re-reading wholesale. Journal-path performance hardening that matters for large managed sessions.

  8. #16352 — fix(managed-agent): mask digit-led passwords and refuse empty Harness user info Closes review items from #16110/#16175 in the upgrade command's start/verify phases: a refusal previously hid everything up to a URL's last @, including when the URL parsed without user info. Credential-leak hardening.

  9. #16461 — feat(cli): add ui.startExpanded Boolean (default false) that starts the TUI with thinking blocks and tool output expanded. Fills the gap left by retiring ui.compactMode, which removed any way to say "I always want the reasoning visible."

  10. #15852 — ci(release): only file issues on failure and reconcile stale ones Both fan-out release notifiers treated a cancelled run as a failure and filed an issue, and neither could close it after a later attempt shipped. Directly targets the stale-issue accumulation visible in #14724.

Also merged/active: #16489 closed — a late snapshot publication now waits for the in-flight claim instead of being rolled back as a deadlock victim per page; #16492 adds the deferred-acquire-vs-close acceptance test requested by #14674; #16482 routes the @qwen-code /review and /resolve permission gate to the self-hosted ECS pool; #14353 honors configured loading phrases in the Web Shell.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Skills as a managed product surface. v0.26.9's ZIP upload / bulk activation / SDK support, plus #16500 (Skills and MCP self-service) and #16404 (stacked-skill overflow warnings), show skills moving from a prompt convention to a governed, quota-aware platform feature. Expect pressure next on skill permissions and provenance.
  • Context and compaction performance. #16508/#16509 (idle-time compaction), #16439 (prelude replay for cache reuse), and #16417 (pre-flight output-budget checks) all attack the same cost center: wasted tokens and latency inside a turn. Idle-time compaction is the clearest emerging architectural direction.
  • Managed-agent observability. #16498 (execution diagnostics, agent graph), #14629 (OpenRouter routing provider and generation ID as span attributes), and #15414 (dropped cache-write token counts) form a consistent ask for richer, more truthful telemetry.
  • Session durability at scale. #13113, #15412, #15800, and #14674 all concern state that must survive long sessions, deep paths, and abrupt termination.
  • Shell correctness across platforms. #15310 (declare the shell in the system prompt), #15675 (sed simulation fidelity), and #16449 (amend-guard recognizer coverage) point at the shell tool being the most common source of silent divergence from real-world behavior.
  • Web Shell / UI ergonomics. #16474 (selection-anchored inline branch threads), #13911 (auto-recap ignores the setting), #16471 (managed-host review deferrals), and #14353 (custom loading phrases) show the companion UI maturing from prototype to configurable product.
  • Provider breadth. #16506 requests a Wally (RunAnywhere) OpenAI-compatible provider preset, continuing steady demand for first-class presets rather than manual endpoint config.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI noise is drowning the issue tracker. #14724 has 218 comments from an automated reporter that cannot identify a failing test, and #16191 and #13953 show the same pattern at smaller scale. Several PRs (#15852, #16319, #16482) are explicitly about making CI reporting quieter and self-reconciling — maintainers are treating this as a real tax on triage.
  • Permission semantics contradict each other. #15597 (implicit deny overriding a scoped allow in headless mode) and #16418 (a review-only skill escalating to source implementation after repeated compaction) are the same underlying complaint: the model's effective permissions are not predictable from the configuration the user wrote.
  • Silent, unrecoverable session loss. #13113 (unopenable transcript), #15412 (path length breaks recording), and #15800 (stale "running" status) all fail without a clear error at the moment of damage. Users discover the loss later, which is the worst failure mode for a coding agent.
  • Wasted turns from avoidable mistakes. #15310 (wrong shell assumed), #16417 (oversized write generated then discarded), and #16418 (compaction-induced drift) each burn a full model round-trip. In unattended runs these compound quickly and are the most common motivation cited in feature requests.
  • Latency landing inside the user's turn. Compaction fires mid-turn today, so users feel summarization as a stall. This is the single most consistently cited performance complaint and the reason #16508 moved from issue to design doc in one day.
  • Background execution lacks a lifecycle. #15800 (status never clears) and #16444 (auto-opened dialog steals Ctrl+C) show background shells and background agents working in the happy path but leaving stale or hijacked state at the edges.

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-11-07

Issues: 365 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-11-07 02:20 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-07

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 仍处于高频、高竞争的维护阶段：过去 24 小时内有 365 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 被更新，其中 160 个 issue 已关闭（占被触及 issue 的 43.8%），123 个 PR 已合并/关闭（约占被触及 PR 的 24.6%）。今日没有发布新版本，跟踪器中评论最多的 issue 是一个 P0 崩溃循环回归（#160959，80 条评论），自 9 月下旬起一直处于开启状态，这表明部分阻碍发布的缺陷已经跨越了多个发布周期仍未解决。PR 队列是当前主要的健康隐患：377 个 PR 仍处于开启状态，而今日关闭的只有 123 个；在评论最多的 PR 中，有相当一部分是草稿、占位符或“需要补充证明”的候选，而非可合并的工作。活跃度很强，但吞吐量偏向于接收与分诊，而不是落地修复——这与一个承受高用户负载、并依赖激进自动化分诊的项目相符（几乎每个 issue 都带有 clawsweeper:* 标签）。

2. 发布情况

今日无新版本发布。 Latest Releases 区块为空。

从 issue 流量中可以看出：当前稳定线似乎是 2026.10.10，预发布版 2026.11.5-beta.1 在 #141474 和 #193962 中被提及。值得注意的是，#193962 报告称，2026.10.10 上的受影响用户无法通过 openclaw update 获取 2026.11.5-beta.1 中的修复，因为已安装的更新器的 10 秒 SQLite 头部探测会超时——这是一个分发渠道层面的阻塞问题，值得在下一次稳定版发布前优先处理。

3. 项目进展

今日合并/关闭的 PR（部分）：

PR 变更
#194384 fix(cron)：一次性任务的收尾以及启用/禁用状态切换现在可在 PostgreSQL 16 上正常工作（function json(unknown) does not exist）；同时修复了 PostgreSQL 18 缓存一致性断言
#194399 fix(media)：被中断的附件下载现在会被取消，而不是一直运行到进程退出
#194407 fix(ci)：在 Vitest 元数据增长时保留编译 worker 的复用
#194405 test(ui)：修复不稳定的已配置 provider 图标测试（定时运行 42319656353）
#194411 fix(plugins)：恢复缺失的 OpenClaw ID Access 素材（解除素材检查阻塞）
#194190 fix(ui)：在紧凑行中，当日时间戳仅显示时间
#194152 ui：对话框关闭与幽灵图标操作统一改用 IconButton

今日关闭的 issue（部分）： #166017（MCP 会话空闲 TTL 默认值未生效 → 256 子进程 spawn-broker 耗尽）、#178291（P0：2026.10.4→10.5 聊天更新在激活后 Doctor 检查中失败）、#164923（某工作区短期记忆晋升 0/512）、#155457（Anthropic 流式 JSON 参数格式错误）、#168794（Codex 中继 >32 MiB 图片 → 502）、#165433（重连信封被拒绝）、#164690（claude-cli 下 stdio MCP 重复生成）。

评估： 当日落地的工作主要是正确性与 CI/测试卫生，而非面向用户的功能。影响最大的关闭项是 #166017——一个导致所有 exec/read/MCP 启动瘫痪的硬上限耗尽缺陷——但该修复尚未确认已在稳定版中发布。

4. 社区热点

#160959 — [P0] Gateway 在捕获大型外部插件时阻塞数分钟（2026.9.6 回归） · 80 条评论 · 链接 这是项目中讨论最热烈的线程。自插件生成捕获功能落地（#144252）以来，拥有大型外部/工作区插件依赖树的 Gateway 会在启动时以及每次重新发布 prepared-runtime 时阻塞其事件循环数分钟。被标记为 impact:crash-loop、P0、clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr。其根本需求是架构性的：插件捕获必须移出 V8 主线程，或改为增量/缓存方式。相关的活性证据见 #166641（web_fetch 回退路径同步捕获插件）。

#164294 — Gateway 状态数据库的 WAL 自动检查点永不完成 · 39 条评论 · 链接 一个 PASSIVE 检查点被进程内的读取器钉住（checkpointedFrames=866、logFrames=17091、consecutiveBlocked 持续攀升）。用户实际上只能眼看着 WAL 无界增长而无任何补救途径。需要对 state/openclaw.sqlite 进行长生命周期读取器审计。

#177656 — [P1] 原生主机 exec 返回共享状态完整性准入错误 · 30 条评论 · 链接 在稳定版 2026.10.5 上出现 ≥28 次失败，子进程副作用未证实，无修复。错误信息：Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission。这是没有关联修复 PR 的最高严重度 issue。

#150635 — Dreaming 深度阶段永不晋升（短期回忆被驱逐） · 25 条评论 · 链接 在 512 条目上限处，夜间摄取会暂存数百条零召回条目，将真正被召回的条目驱逐出去，因此晋升永远不会发生。结合今日关闭的 #164923，这指向一个系统性的记忆层级容量/驱逐策略问题，而非两个孤立的 bug。

#191944 — gateway stop / stop --force 在 macOS 上失败 · 23 条评论 · 链接 ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected。一个基础的生命周期操作在一流桌面平台上失效——实现复杂度低，但 UX 影响面大。

PR 侧： 最值得关注的开放候选是 #194376（feat(gateway)：为 sessions_send 唤醒启动添加准入边界——解决并发发送者绕过批处理/速率限制的问题）、#182383（feat(plugin-sdk)：访问策略修订缓存，安全敏感）以及 #194133（UI 菜单行结构规范化）。队列中还包含明确的非工作项——#191509（“空的 iOS 交接占位符——请勿使用”）和 #188726（调查占位符）——它们抬高了开放 PR 的计数。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重度排序。“修复 PR”表示数据中存在已关联/已合并的候选修复。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点，按信号频次排序：

  1. 启动/升级脆弱。 从 2026.9.6→2026.10.10 的用户报告 Gateway 阻塞数分钟、迁移在大型归档上失败、以及无法通过更新摆脱问题版本（#160959、#185656、#193962、#178291）。这是不满情绪的最大单一来源。
  2. 记忆功能令人失望。 “dreaming”/短期回忆系统被广泛报告为未按宣传方式工作——某个工作区晋升 0/512，而同类工作区达到 50–90%（#164923、#150635）。用户自己在做细致的对比调试，这说明文档/可观测性存在缺口。
  3. 成本不透明。 多位用户量化了无法归因的大额支出（#143017：2130 万缓存写入 token；#130257：父子成本相差 100 倍）。提示缓存被报告为从未复用（#182891），直接转化为计费 token。
  4. 平台相关的生命周期故障。 macOS 的 gateway stop（#191944）、Kubernetes fsGroup 重启（#192959）、Android 每 0.8 秒轮询一个未知智能体（#167316，已关闭）。桌面/容器用户感觉相对于 Linux systemd 路径是二等公民。
  5. 多智能体复杂度。 运行时发布被取代错误、Codex 启动超时、重复的 MCP 生成、每个 stdio 子进程 145 MB 的包装器开销（#158127、#164690、#164017 系列）。运行大量智能体的运维者报告资源增长不可预测。

满意信号： 报告始终详细、可复现，并标明版本——用户群体技术素养高且投入度高。今日的若干关闭项（#166017、#164923、#178291）都源自持续数周的实质性讨论，说明用户确实会跟踪修复直至解决。主要不满在于 P0/P1 项的修复时间，而非对报告的响应速度。

按严重程度排序。“修复 PR”指今日样本中可见的 PR。

P0 — 数据完整性

高 — 数据丢失 / 安全边界

  • #147720 （开启，P3 安全） — 按配置文件路由的子代理会继承父级的工具集，而不是目标配置文件的工具集；禁用了终端的目标配置文件在被委派时仍可运行 shell 命令。这是权限边界违规；标签低估了影响。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点，按强烈程度排序：

  1. 更新安全性主导了焦虑。 用户不是在要求功能；他们在报告更新可能让 macOS 构建搁浅（#149861、#150146）、把活跃数据库锁误诊为损坏并回滚到陈旧数据（#147938），或静默丢弃用户配置（#150436）。alt-glitch 的更新路径系列读起来像是对累积信任侵蚀的直接回应。
  2. 重启后的会话持久性。 #139818 的 42 条评论和 #146643 的超时都描述了同一种真实体验：当网关/serve 进程轮转时，对话会“消失”或变得不可达。远程后端和多配置文件自托管用户是受影响最大的群体。
  3. 规模。 几千个会话就足以打满核心并破坏 Desktop 用户体验（#146643）。重度用户正在触及 SQLite 后端设计的实际上限。
  4. 多配置文件 / 多租户运营。 #150397（一个网关中有 11 个配置文件）、#147720（配置文件工具集泄漏）、#150431（管理员锁定）都来自将 Hermes 作为共享基础设施而非单用户助手来运行的运营者。
  5. 客户端功能对等差距。 Desktop 侧边栏遗漏已启用平台（#79836）、iPhone Safari 需要双击（#150369）、移动通知重复 Desktop 活动（#148307），以及发送内容可能被复制到输入框（#148277）。

满意信号： 深思熟虑、可复现的报告附带版本/提交固定信息，甚至包含自我纠正（#150056 在重放失败后明确撤回自己的假设），表明用户群参与度高且技术成熟。最热议题上的 3 个 👍 以及 #139347/#148307 各 1 个，绝对数字很低——这个社区通过详细评论而非表情反应来表达认同。

不满信号： 反复出现的“代理侧没有补救办法”（#148329）、“原因未确定”（#150056）以及“成功恢复被报告为未完成”（#147938）等措辞，指向一种认知：故障模式不透明，自我诊断不可靠。

7. User Feedback Summary

GBK/CP936 files silently byte-stripped by errors="ignore" (#8234); \\?\ path canonicalization breaking SQLite URIs (#8585); hanging cancellation tests (#8604). Use cases evidenced: multi-workspace Matrix bridging, cross-agent collaboration and delegation, Creator (image/video generation) pipelines, offline/air-gapped deployment, third-party backend routing (Codex/Qoder/Kimi), scheduled agent tasks over IM, and long-term memory recall.

  5. PR #11846 — OpenRouter balance reporting; explicitly depends on unmerged #11845, so it is stalled in a chain.
  6. PR #12065 / PR #12116 — Discord approval and peer-delivery fixes open since 2026-10-27 / 2026-10-30. Small (XS/S) but risk:high on #12065; both relate directly to the still-open #10926 peer-resolution theme and could be batched into one peer-routing decision.

Health verdict: strong triage velocity and clear release discipline, with risk concentrated in (a) the three multi-month XL PRs and (b) inconsistent identity/trust primitives across gateway, RPC and peer-resolution code paths.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-07

Issues: 365 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-07 02:20 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity, high-contention maintenance phase: 365 issues and 500 pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours, with 160 issues closed (43.8% of touched issues) and 123 PRs merged/closed (~24.6% of touched PRs). No new release shipped today, and the most-commented issue in the tracker is a P0 crash-loop regression (#160959, 80 comments) that has been open since late September, signaling that some release-blocking defects are outliving multiple release cycles. The PR queue is the main health concern: 377 PRs remain open versus 123 closed today, and a visible share of the top-commented PRs are drafts, placeholders, or "needs proof" candidates rather than merge-ready work. Activity is strong, but throughput is skewed toward intake and triage rather than landing fixes — consistent with a project under heavy user load and aggressive automated triage (clawsweeper:* labels on nearly every issue).

2. Releases

No new releases today. The Latest Releases section is empty.

Context from issue traffic: the current stable line appears to be 2026.10.10, with a prerelease 2026.11.5-beta.1 referenced in #141474 and #193962. Notably, #193962 reports that affected users on 2026.10.10 cannot reach the fix in 2026.11.5-beta.1 via openclaw update because the installed updater's 10-second SQLite header probe times out — a distribution-channel blocker worth prioritizing before the next stable cut.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (selected):

PR Change
#194384 fix(cron): one-shot finalization and enable/disable transitions now work on PostgreSQL 16 (function json(unknown) does not exist); also repairs PostgreSQL 18 cache conformance assertion
#194399 fix(media): interrupted attachment downloads are now cancelled instead of running until process exit
#194407 fix(ci): preserves compiled-worker reuse when Vitest metadata grows
#194405 test(ui): fixes flaky configured-provider icon test (scheduled run 42319656353)
#194411 fix(plugins): restores missing OpenClaw ID Access artwork (unblocks artwork check)
#194190 fix(ui): same-day timestamps show time only in tight rows
#194152 ui: dialog closes and ghost icon actions unified onto IconButton

Issues closed today (selected): #166017 (MCP session idle-TTL default not applied → 256-child spawn-broker exhaustion), #178291 (P0: 2026.10.4→10.5 chat update fails post-activation Doctor), #164923 (short-term promotion 0/512 in one workspace), #155457 (Anthropic malformed streamed JSON args), #168794 (Codex relay >32 MiB image → 502), #165433 (reconnect envelope rejection), #164690 (duplicate stdio MCP spawn under claude-cli).

Assessment: the day's landed work is predominantly correctness and CI/test-hygiene, not user-facing features. The most consequential closure is #166017 — a hard-cap exhaustion bug that bricked all exec/read/MCP starts — but the fix is not yet confirmed shipped in a stable release.

4. Community Hot Topics

#160959 — [P0] Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) · 80 comments · link The single hottest thread in the project. Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252), a Gateway with a large external/workspace plugin dependency tree blocks its event loop for minutes at startup and on every prepared-runtime republish. Labeled impact:crash-loop, P0, clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr. The underlying need is architectural: plugin capture must move off the main V8 thread or become incremental/cached. Related liveness evidence appears in #166641 (web_fetch fallback synchronously capturing plugins).

#164294 — Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes · 39 comments · link A PASSIVE checkpoint is pinned by an in-process reader (checkpointedFrames=866, logFrames=17091, consecutiveBlocked climbing). Users are effectively watching unbounded WAL growth with no remediation path. Needs a long-lived-reader audit of state/openclaw.sqlite.

#177656 — [P1] Native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error · 30 comments · link ≥28 failures on stable 2026.10.5, child effects unproved, no fix. Error: Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission. This is the highest-severity issue without a linked fix PR.

#150635 — Dreaming deep phase never promotes (short-term recall eviction) · 25 comments · link At the 512-entry cap, nightly ingestion stages hundreds of zero-recall entries that evict genuinely recalled ones, so promotion never occurs. Coupled with #164923 (closed today), this points to a systemic memory-tier capacity/eviction policy problem rather than two isolated bugs.

#191944 — gateway stop / stop --force fail on macOS · 23 comments · link ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected. A basic lifecycle operation is broken on a first-class desktop platform — high UX blast radius for low implementation complexity.

PR-side: the most notable open candidates are #194376 (feat(gateway): admission boundary for sessions_send wake starts — addresses concurrent-sender bypass of batching/rate limits), #182383 (feat(plugin-sdk): access-policy revision caching, security-sensitive), and #194133 (UI menu-row anatomy normalization). The queue also contains explicit non-work — #191509 ("empty iOS handoff placeholder — do not use") and #188726 (investigation placeholder) — which inflates the open count.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity. "Fix PR" indicates a linked/merged candidate exists in the data.

Sev Issue Symptom Fix PR?
P0 #160959 Gateway event-loop blocked for minutes by plugin capture; crash-loop No
P1 #177656 Native host exec: shared-state integrity-admission error, 28+ occurrences No
P1 #191847 2026.10.10 regression: large session repeatedly OOMs the 512 MB SQLite worker; every turn fails with "admission is closed" No
P1 #192959 Gateway refuses to start after K8s pod restart (fsGroup remount invalidates client credential dir) No
P1 #185656 Large zstd transcript archive exceeds Node string limit in media-persistence migration — regression of #170847 despite merged fix #170853; blocks updates Merged but ineffective
P1 #182647 Cloud-worker turns fail pre-inference: "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" queueable-fix
P1 #166641 web_fetch cold fallback synchronously captures plugins on Gateway main thread → liveness stalls (V8 profile captured) No
P1 #155563 2026.9.5 regression: service-child-relay/group-anchor/MCP groups retained after successful turn No
P1 #126950 Telegram tgcb1: opaque callback payloads silently dropped for non-plugin callers (message loss) Linked PR open
P1 #157182 Control UI forces /chat/main and retries forever when ambient main session isn't visible (security-flagged) No
P1 #162087 9.7: scheduled announce fails for pre-9.7 account-mode cron jobs (missing ownerOrigin) No
P2 #164294 WAL checkpoint permanently blocked No
P2 #141474 sessions_yield strands agents_wait forever; outputSchema inert on claude-cli — fix only in 2026.11.5-beta.1, not stable In prerelease
P2 #193962 SQLite header-probe timeout fix (#187197) unreachable from 2026.10.10 via openclaw update Fix exists, distribution blocked
P2 #182891 Prompt cache never reused — cache read dropped N -> 0 on every request No
P2 #191944 macOS gateway stop fails (process ancestry inspection) No
P2 #158127 2026.9.6 multi-agent runtime publication failures + Codex startup timeouts No
P2 #167609 Code Mode reports guest TypeErrors as internal_error (live repro on main e29577b7d7d) fix-shape-clear
P2 #123792 Assistant turns persisted/rendered twice with claude-cli backend No

Stability read: the dominant failure cluster is Gateway main-thread blocking and SQLite worker pressure (#160959, #166641, #191847, #164294, #185656). A second cluster is runtime lifecycle leakage (#155563, #166017 now closed, #164690 closed). A third is update/installation integrity (#185656, #193962, #178291) — worrying because it can trap users on known-bad versions. Two P1 regressions (#185656, #191847) are confirmed present in the current stable line.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Cost & observability

  • #13219 — Per-model usage logging for cost tracking (open since Feb 2026, 10 comments, 👍1). Repeatedly reinforced by #143017 (21.3M cache-write tokens measured) and #130257 (delegated ACP child run $14.14 vs parent $0.04, unattributable). Strong candidate for near-term roadmap: three independent cost-visibility issues with production numbers attached.
  • #178373 — No run-level turn/token budget; tool-loop detection opt-in (defaults off); retained history re-billed every turn.

Agent/session management

  • #166678 — Hide agents from pickers while keeping them spawnable (WebUI/macOS/iOS), 👍1.
  • #158800 — Browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after /new in Control UI.
  • #103067 — Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime & cross-channel persistence.

Channels & integrations

  • #136271 — msteams: dynamically resolve team SharePoint site for channel uploads.
  • #162087 — cron announce account-mode ownership (bug, but drives a delivery-model decision).

UX & configuration

  • #163739 — Make Ctrl+Shift+A (Archive) configurable; collides with browser shortcuts, 👍1. Low effort, clear win.
  • #79223 — Configurable Dream Diary language (hardcoded English prompt in memory-core), 👍2 — a recurring complaint from non-English workspaces.
  • #164620 — Setting to disable the hosted plugin catalog feed (clawhub.ai hardcoded).
  • #130247 — Cron jobs cannot end: no --until/--max-runs, no cumulative run counter.

Prediction: the highest-probability next-cycle items are cost/usage aggregation (#13219 family), cron lifecycle bounds (#130247), and keybinding configurability (#163739) — all are narrow, well-specified, and backed by repeated reports. The memory/dreaming work (#150635, #79223) likely needs a design decision (clawsweeper:needs-product-decision) before implementation.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points, by frequency of signal:

  1. Startup/upgrade fragility. Users on 2026.9.6→2026.10.10 report Gateways that block for minutes, migrations that fail on large archives, and updates that cannot be applied to escape the broken version (#160959, #185656, #193962, #178291). This is the single largest source of dissatisfaction.
  2. Memory feature disappointment. The "dreaming"/short-term-recall system is widely reported as not working as advertised — 0/512 promotion in one workspace while siblings hit 50–90% (#164923, #150635). Users are doing careful comparative debugging themselves, which suggests documentation/observability gaps.
  3. Cost opacity. Multiple users quantify large, unattributable spend (#143017: 21.3M cache-write tokens; #130257: 100× parent/child cost asymmetry). The prompt cache is reported as never reused (#182891), directly converting into billed tokens.
  4. Platform-specific lifecycle breakage. macOS gateway stop (#191944), Kubernetes fsGroup restarts (#192959), Android polling an unknown agent every 0.8 s (#167316, closed). Desktop/container users feel like second-class citizens relative to the Linux systemd path.
  5. Multi-agent complexity. Runtime publication superseded errors, Codex startup timeouts, duplicate MCP spawns, 145 MB wrapper overhead per stdio child (#158127, #164690, #164017-family). Operators running many agents report unpredictable resource growth.

Satisfaction signals: reports are consistently detailed, reproducible, and version-pinned — the user base is technically sophisticated and invested. Several closures today (#166017, #164923, #178291) drew substantive multi-week threads, indicating users do track fixes through to resolution. The main dissatisfaction is time-to-fix on P0/P1 items, not responsiveness to reports.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered, high-value issues:

Age Item Why it matters
~9 months #13219 Per-model usage logging (Feb 2026) Cheapest possible answer to the loudest cost complaints; still needs-product-decision
~6 months #79223 Dream Diary language (May 2026) Hardcoded prompt in memory-core; trivial fix, international users blocked
~4 months #112638 session.maintenance enforce mode doesn't bound the store Silent unbounded disk growth; maxEntries/maxDiskBytes are effectively advisory
~4 months #103067 Centralize chat-session naming / subagent lifetime Foundational for multi-agent UX; keeps generating duplicate reports
~3 months #126950 Telegram opaque callbacks dropped Message loss on a primary channel; linked PR open but stalled
~3 months #130247 / #130257 Cron has no end condition; ACP run cost unattributable Both filed by the same operator; scheduler lacks basic lifecycle semantics
~2.5 months #123792 Double-rendered assistant turns (claude-cli) Visible data-integrity/UX defect on Control UI + Android

Stale PRs needing maintainer attention:

  • #75225 — feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list. Open since 2026-04-30, proof: sufficient, status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer. Over six months with a sufficient proof packet is a process failure, not a technical one.
  • #125969 — fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery. Open since 2026-08-18, ready for maintainer look.
  • #130231 — ci(i18n): non-publishing locale refresh. Open since 2026-08-26, flagged merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary, needs proof.
  • #182383 — feat(plugin-sdk): access-policy revision caching (XL, security-sensitive). Needs a security reviewer, not more author iteration.
  • #161362 — fix(agents): stop warning that documented core tool groups need a plugin. security-review-required, waiting on author since 2026-09-29.

Recommendation: the open-PR backlog (377) is now large enough to obscure real work — several top-listed PRs are explicitly non-mergeable placeholders (#191509, #188726). Closing or converting those to draft issues, and prioritizing the two P0/P1 regressions with no fix PR (#160959, #177656), would materially improve both perceived and actual project health.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

⚠️ Comparative analysis generation failed.

Peer Project Reports

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest, 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

Activity is high and heavily maintenance-weighted: 50 issues and 50 PRs were touched in the last 24 hours, with 5 issues closed and 13 PRs merged/closed, but no new release was cut. The day's work clusters into three streams: cleanup and follow-ups from the npm→pnpm workspace switch (#149746 lineage), a large stack of update-path hardening PRs from alt-glitch (tracked under #150383), and continued pressure on gateway/session-store scalability and the "session authority" cutover (#145171). The most-discussed item, #139818 (42 comments), closed today after a long thread on remote-backend Desktop sessions being unresumable — a sign that session-state correctness is the project's dominant pain point. Health reads as active but regression-heavy: recent infrastructure changes (pnpm, state-store relocation, update swap mechanics) are generating a visible tail of follow-up bugs, including one open P0 data-integrity issue on Windows (#147938).

3. Project Progress

The 20 most-commented PRs shown are all still open; the 13 merged/closed PRs are not itemized in this sample, so merged-feature attribution is limited to what is visibly in flight.

In-flight, high-impact work:

Area PR Status
Platform extraction #150210 — Yuanbao moves out of core into a Hermes Labs plugin, with automatic migration for existing users Open, CI-reviewed
Session read API #150102 — session.transcript: read a stored session without attaching (picker fields, transcript pages, compactions, subagent transcripts) Open
State backend #150421 — optional PostgreSQL backend for conversation state (stage B), stacked on #150332 Open
Update path #150385, #150386, #150387, #150405, #150406, #150407, #150408 Open
Test/CI hardening #150411 (upgrade suites start from real releases), #150418 (upgrade E2E shards on update-path PRs), #150195 (de-flake refusal-stamp test) Open
pnpm follow-ups #150430 (cache inputs, undeclared deps, lock attributes), #150419 (android-arm64 pin for linux-arm64-bionic/Termux) Open
Refactor #150388 — removes the CJK FTS5 tokenizer from core; #150401 — package-qualified logger routing Open

Closed today (issue-side): #139818 (remote-backend Desktop resume), #106960 (systemd dashboard inventoried as manual-serve), #149861 (macOS Desktop build failure after pnpm switch), #150035 and #150036 (pnpm npmrc reader / pin consolidation).

Notable direction: several PRs explicitly require shipping before the state-store directory move (#150407: "must reach a stable release before the move"), indicating a coordinated, staged migration rather than ad-hoc patching.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Signal Underlying need
#139818 — remote-backend Desktop sessions unresumable (session.resume → not_found) 42 comments, 3 👍, CLOSED Users run hermes serve on a remote host and expect Desktop conversations to survive process restarts. The long thread reflects confusion about where sessions are persisted and who owns them.
#146643 — gateway re-reads full session history on every change; CPU and Desktop timeouts scale with store size 17 comments, P2 perf Scalability ceiling: on a few-thousand-session store the gateway burns 1.5–2.5 cores and Desktop requests hit 30 s timeouts. This is the top structural risk to power users.
#106960 — systemd dashboard inventoried as manual serve after update 14 comments, CLOSED Self-hosters using systemd units want first-class service discovery, not fallback heuristics.
#139347 — bounded hosted-room transcript drops users still referenced by settlements 9 comments, 1 👍 Multi-participant/hosted-room correctness: eviction logic conflicts with validation invariants.
#147938 — state.db verify mistakes a live lock for corruption 7 comments, P0 Trust in the updater. Users need "don't touch my data" guarantees.
#105163 — English-only stall-guard intent detector 7 comments Non-English operators are silently losing anti-stall protection.

Read: the community's center of gravity has shifted from feature requests to operational trust — session durability, update safety, and performance at scale. The 42-comment #139818 thread is the clearest signal that session authority (#145171) is the right architectural bet.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity. "Fix PR" = a PR visible in today's sample.

P0 — data integrity

  • #147938 (open, Windows) — state.db verification cannot distinguish a live lock from corruption during the update pause window; it restores a months-stale snapshot over healthy data and then reports the successful restore as "did not complete." Highest-risk open issue today. No linked fix PR in sample.

High — data loss / security boundary

  • #150436 (open, v0.23.0 Docker) — any config save (e.g. an "always allow" approval) deletes user values for keys also set in the managed /etc/hermes/config.yaml scope. Silent, user-invisible config loss. No fix PR.
  • #147720 (open, P3 security) — profile-routed subagents inherit the parent's toolsets instead of the target profile's; a profile with terminal disabled can still run shell commands when delegated to. Privilege-boundary violation; label understates impact.
  • #137723 (open, P2) — Codex quota recovery marks a credential ok in memory but persists exhausted, so pool reloads resurrect stale quota errors. No fix PR.

Medium — functional breakage

  • #148329 (open, P2) — locking a skill inside a git working tree blocks all git writes in that repo, with no agent-side remedy. Protection feature becoming a work blocker.
  • #146643 (open, P2 perf) — see hot topics; CPU/timeouts grow with store size.
  • #133006 (open, P2, macOS) — Desktop form-filling: stale/empty browser targets plus unverified agent recovery loops.
  • #146280 (open, P2) — Anthropic usage: utilization <= 1% reported as 100% due to fraction scaling on a percent field. Cosmetic but erodes billing trust.
  • #148277 (open, P2) — Desktop message that landed is also restored into the composer; re-sending runs it twice under a new submission id.
  • #150397 (open) — multiplexed gateway (11 profiles) has the local terminal backend overwrite the routed profile's explicit terminal.cwd with the process cwd.
  • #150056 (open) — message_agent deliveries refused with admission_conflict for hours after compression; cause not identified, prior hypothesis disproven by replay.

Regression cluster from the pnpm switch (#149746)

  • #149861 (CLOSED) — pnpm 12.15.0 silently drops the get-windows optional dependency; every macOS Desktop build fails.
  • #150146 (open) — same failure, still reproducible on main (v0.23.0+209). Two files disagree on whether a missing optional dep is fatal. Fix PRs: #150430, #150419.

Update-path correctness (open, with fix PRs)

  • #150398 → #150408
  • #150399 → #150407
  • #150403 → #150406
  • #150402 → #150405

Low

  • #105163 (i18n stall guard), #79836 (Desktop sidebar missing platform sections), #150369 (iPhone Safari mic requires double-tap; AudioContext gesture gating), #150439 (re-authorization path after an explicit "Deny" on a Dangerous Command prompt is unclear).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

User-requested:

  • #150431 — managed scope should be able to lock mcp_servers (mapping-level lock, not leaf-merge). Enterprise/admin deployment signal.
  • #148307 — suppress routine mobile push notifications while the user is active on Desktop. Cross-device presence awareness.
  • #145171 — tracking issue: cut serve, remote Desktop, and web over to the gateway session authority.

Likely in the next release (high confidence):

  1. pnpm stabilization — macOS Desktop build fix plus lock/pin consolidation (#150146, #150430, #150419, #150041 tracking).
  2. Update-path hardening bundle — the #150383 stack (#150385–#150408, #150411, #150418) is explicitly sequenced and partly gated on landing before the state-store move.
  3. session.transcript read API (#150102) — unblocks third-party frontends (hermes-tern cited) and is a prerequisite for scalable session pickers.

Plausible but not imminent: PostgreSQL state backend stage B (#150421, stacked and opt-in); Yuanbao core→plugin extraction (#150210); catalog additions for wally (#150438) and Yandex Mail (#150433).

Structural bet worth flagging: the state-store relocation (src/hermes_agent/) plus #150388's FTS5 CJK removal and #150421's Postgres seam together suggest a session-storage rearchitecture in progress. Expect migration notes and a minor-version bump when it lands.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points, in order of intensity:

  1. Update safety dominates anxiety. Users are not asking for features; they are reporting that updates can strand a macOS build (#149861, #150146), misdiagnose a live DB lock as corruption and roll back to stale data (#147938), or silently drop user config (#150436). The alt-glitch update-path stack reads as a direct response to accumulated trust erosion.
  2. Session durability across restarts. #139818's 42 comments and #146643's timeouts both describe the same lived experience: conversations that "disappear" or become unreachable when a gateway/serve process cycles. Remote-backend and multi-profile self-hosters are the most affected cohort.
  3. Scale. A few thousand sessions is enough to saturate cores and break Desktop UX (#146643). Power users are hitting the SQLite-backed design's practical ceiling.
  4. Multi-profile / multi-tenant operations. #150397 (11 profiles in one gateway), #147720 (profile toolset leakage), #150431 (admin locking) all come from operators running Hermes as shared infrastructure, not a single-user assistant.
  5. Client parity gaps. Desktop sidebar omits enabled platforms (#79836), iPhone Safari needs double-taps (#150369), mobile notifications duplicate Desktop activity (#148307), and a send can be duplicated into the composer (#148277).

Satisfaction signals: thoughtful, reproducible reports with version/commit pins and even self-corrections (#150056 explicitly retracts its own hypothesis after a failed replay) indicate an engaged, technically sophisticated user base. Three 👍 on the top issue and one each on #139347/#148307 are low absolute numbers — this community signals agreement through detailed comments rather than reactions.

Dissatisfaction signals: repeated "no agent-side remedy" (#148329), "cause not identified" (#150056), and "successful restore reported as did not complete" (#147938) phrasing point to a perception that failure modes are opaque and self-diagnosis is unreliable.

8. Backlog Watch

Issues with meaningful age and no visible fix PR:

Issue Age (as of 2026-11-07) Why it matters
#79836 — Desktop messaging sidebar missing raft and other enabled platforms ~93 days Platform adapters ship but are invisible in the UI; a persistent feature-parity gap for multi-platform users. 6 comments, no fix PR.
#105163 — English-only stall-guard intent detector ~61 days Silently disables anti-stall for every non-English agent run. Small, well-scoped fix (_TRAILING_CONTINUE_INTENT_RE) with clear ROI.
#133006 — macOS Desktop form-filling failure, stale browser targets ~33 days Tagged needs-repro; blocks the flagship computer-use use case on macOS.
#139347 — bounded transcript eviction breaks settlement references ~23 days DiscussionValidationError leaves rooms stuck; correctness bug in hosted rooms with 1 👍 and no fix PR.
#145171 — entry-point cutover tracking issue ~12 days Meta-issue; needs sequencing clarity so #139818-class bugs stop recurring.

PRs needing maintainer attention: #150418 is an explicit draft awaiting a CI-owner cost decision (adds runner cost to update-path PRs) and is stacked behind #150411. #150421 (Postgres stage B) is stacked on #150332 and will stall if stage A is not reviewed. #150210 (Yuanbao extraction) is a cross-repo migration and carries the highest coordination cost of any open PR.

Data basis: 50 issues and 50 PRs updated 2026-11-07; issue/PR lists truncated to top 30 and top 20 by comment count respectively, so merged-PR attribution and zero-comment items are under-represented. All links point to github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.

IronClaw — nearai/ironclaw

No activity in the last 24 hours.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

Repository: agentscope-ai/QwenPaw Data window: last 24 hours (through 2026-11-06)

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw had a high-velocity, triage-heavy day with no release: 35 PRs and 23 Issues were updated in 24 hours, of which 18 PRs were merged/closed and 11 Issues were closed. The dominant pattern is same-day issue→fix conversion — at least five Issues updated today already have a matching open PR from the same day (#8576→#8608, #8596→#8600, #5110→#8609, #7436→#8610, #8549→#8550), indicating an engaged contributor base and responsive maintainer triage. Activity clusters around four subsystems: Console/UI ergonomics, memory & reranker, IM channel plugins (Matrix), and Windows compatibility. Notably, every Issue and PR in this window has 0 👍, so engagement is comment-driven rather than reaction-driven — a signal worth watching for a project of this size. Overall health: strong throughput, but a growing long-tail of "under review" large PRs and a recurring pattern of Chinese-Windows edge cases.

2. Releases

None. No new versions were published in the last 24 hours, and the "Latest Releases" feed is empty. No breaking changes or migration notes to report.

Context from Issues: the newest line in circulation appears to be 2.3.0b2 / 2.3.0-beta.1 (Desktop), with 2.2.2.post1 as the latest stable referenced by reporters. Several fixes merged today target 2.3.0b2 regressions (e.g., Matrix plugin conversion in #8538), which suggests a 2.3.0 release is the near-term target — see §6.

3. Project Progress

18 PRs merged/closed in the window (top-20 sample shows 8). Highlights:

PR What advanced Linked Issue
#8550 Model config write-path validation — enforces thinking_budget >= 1 and max_input_length >= 1000, preventing persisted bad values that silently dropped a provider after restart #8549
#8411 Matrix channel hardening — restores cached sessions instead of re-login on every start; re-uploads E2EE device keys after server-side key loss #8365
#8457 Memory recall semantics — automatic recall now injected as transient untrusted TextBlock reference context instead of a synthetic assistant tool-call trajectory, stopping models from imitating it and re-calling memory_search —
#8535 Third-party backend cron fix — converts dict requests to AgentRequest before backend selection, fixing Third-party agent requests require text or attachments for Codex/Qoder #8533
#8600 Console /clear cache hygiene — reset chats stay empty after reopen/refresh, empty-state greeting restored #8596
#8598 Plugin dependency check refactor (size/XXXL) — rework of the install-time dependency validation path —
#8604 CI stability — stops Windows shell-cancellation tests from hanging —
#373 Dynamic MCP tool persistence — per-session persistence of dynamically loaded MCP connections; closed after ~8 months open —

Theme: the day's merged work is predominantly correctness and lifecycle fixes (config validation, session/crypto recovery, cache state, async test hygiene) rather than net-new capability — a maturing-project signature.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume (all items show 0 👍):

  1. #2420 — [CLOSED] Cross-agent collaboration UX feedback · 4 comments · open since 2026-03-27 Reports four distinct problems in v0.2.0.post1: onboarding for cross-agent collaboration, triggering of cross-agent communication, collaboration coherence, and identity confusion between agents. Closed today after ~7.5 months. Underlying need: users are attempting multi-agent compositions the product does not yet guide them through; "identity confusion" points at a real agent identity/attribution model gap rather than a UI bug.

  2. #8580 — [OPEN] Memory tag index never rebuilds, /memory/tags → 503 · 4 comments auto_memory_generate_tags = true is accepted and persisted, tags are generated, but the index never rebuilds so the read API is permanently unavailable. Config read-back verified; on-disk diff confirmed. Underlying need: memory is being sold as a first-class capability, but write path and read path are decoupled with no reconciliation/rebuild trigger. This is the highest-impact open bug in the window.

  3. #8596 — [CLOSED] /clear message reappears on chat reopen · 4 comments · fixed same day by #8600

  4. #1453 — [CLOSED] CoPaw offline install can't reach offline Qwen3/3.5 but works with DeepSeek R1 · 4 comments · open since 2026-03-13 Underlying need: air-gapped / on-prem deployment is a real use case; provider-specific offline behavior is inconsistent.

  5. #8276 — [CLOSED] ReMe reranker accepts empty api_key, surfaces only "unexpected error" · 4 comments Underlying need: configuration validation and actionable error messages — the same root complaint as #8549.

  6. #7436 — [OPEN] tool_call_format for compact tool display in IM channels · 3 comments · open since 2026-08-31 → addressed by #8610

  7. #5110 — [OPEN] Quote/reference response text for follow-up (Perplexity-style) · 3 comments · open since 2026-06-11 → addressed by #8609

Read: the comment distribution shows users are not arguing about direction — they are filing precise, code-located defect reports and feature asks, and the maintainers are converting them to PRs. The friction is in validation and observability (silent failures, empty-state errors), not in product vision.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity. "Fix PR" = a PR exists in this window.

Critical

  • #8580 — Memory tag index permanently unavailable (503) · OPEN · no fix PR Tags generate but never index; /memory/tags is dead for any user who enables the feature. Feature is effectively non-functional, with no self-healing path.

  • #8592 — Creator review round becomes permanently undecidable · OPEN · no fix PR REJECT always returns 422 "visual artifact reference references missing id" — a hard blocker: a review round can never be resolved. Bundles two further defects (expired provider source_url → 502; frame_stats ignores CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH). Reporter explicitly offers to split into three Issues.

  • #8517 — Hub Docker runtime fails to start: Permission denied on working/config.json · OPEN · no fix PR Blocks any non-root Docker deployment of the Hub. Deployment-class blocker for self-hosted/enterprise users.

High

  • #8585 — recall_history broken on Windows · OPEN · no fix PR workspace_dir canonicalized to \\?\ extended-length path, breaking the SQLite read-only URI. Cross-version (also on 2.2.x, earliest log 20xx) — a long-standing, unaddressed platform bug affecting Desktop users' memory recall.

  • #8538 — Matrix plugin fails to activate with multiple workspaces · OPEN · related fix #8411 closed but this specific 10s-window defect is not covered A 10s shared startup window only covers the first workspace; with three Matrix-enabled workspaces, none come online. Regression introduced by the 2.3.0b2 Matrix→plugin conversion.

  • #8595 — Plugin install fails: "No package metadata was found" for qwenpaw-creator v2.0.4 · OPEN Fails via both extension UI and CLI hot-install path. Blocks the flagship Creator plugin. Possibly related to the dependency-check refactor in #8598.

  • #8603 — run_code invoked with empty {} arguments on custom OpenAI-compatible providers · OPEN Every run_code call on user-defined providers (kimi, kimi-codingplan / k3.1-pro) fails validation: 'code' is a required property. Breaks tool use entirely on custom providers — a tool-schema serialization issue, same family as #8607.

Medium

  • #8576 — Default agent edit button disabled although PUT API allows it · OPEN · fix PR #8608 Restriction compiled into the served React bundle; single-agent installs cannot edit their only agent.

  • #8276 — Reranker enablement without credential, opaque error · CLOSED Silent misconfiguration; error surfaces only as "unexpected error."

  • #8590 — Plugin-registered settings route loses the settings sidebar · CLOSED Navigating to a plugin page under primary.settings drops back to the conversation list; built-in settings pages are unaffected. Plugin-navigation state bug.

Low / Resolved

  • #8596 /clear bubble resurrected on reopen — fixed (#8600)
  • #8549 Invalid thinking_budget/max_input_length persisted → provider vanishes after restart — fixed (#8550)
  • #8365 Matrix re-login every start / no E2EE key re-upload — fixed (#8411)
  • #8533 Cron tasks misjudged as empty on Codex/Qoder — fixed (#8535)
  • #8516 SSE missing X-Accel-Buffering: no → first event buffered behind nginx — CLOSED
  • #7857 ACP shutdown fallback skips session cleanup, leaks event loop — CLOSED
  • #7858 Unawaited-coroutine warnings from test mocks — CLOSED (test hygiene)

Stability read: 11 of 23 Issues closed today is a strong burn-down, but the open critical set has zero fix PRs attached (#8580, #8592, #8517, #8585) — that is the main health risk this week.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Issue Status Likelihood for next version
Quote/reference response text for follow-up (Perplexity-style) #5110 Open 5 months; PR #8609 opened today High — implementation already drafted (multiline/code support, repeat quotes, draft preservation)
Compact tool-call display for IM channels (tool_call_format: full/name_only/compact) #7436 Open 2 months; PR #8610 opened today High — backward-compatible default full
Model deletion in Console model pool #8195 → #8410 / #8611 Two competing PRs High, but PR duplication needs maintainer arbitration
Tab title reflects current session name #8605 New, 1 comment Medium — small, well-localized (KB component, route-name-only title source)
Creator UI overhaul (button contrast, model-start state desync, forced shared API key across image/video/LLM models) #8591 New, 1 comment Medium — #3 (per-modality credentials) is a config-model change, not just UI
Reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history, auto-verify PR #8472 Open, size/XXL, under review since 2026-10-28 Medium — large surface, mirrors existing Embedding model center
Cross-agent collaboration guidance & identity model #2420 Closed after 7.5 months, no linked PR Low near-term — closed as feedback, but the need is structural

Prediction: the 2.3.x line likely ships Console polish (#8608, #8609, #8611, tab titles), IM channel display control (#8610), and provider/model config validation hardening (#8550, #8607). The memory subsystem (reranker center #8472, tag index #8580) is the most likely 2.4 headline feature area.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points, in order of frequency:

  1. Silent failures with useless error messages. The single most repeated complaint: reranker enabled with empty key → "unexpected error" (#8276); out-of-range config accepted → provider silently disappears (#8549); tags generated → index never built → 503 (#8580). Users are doing the debugging work themselves and locating exact file/line — a sign the project is under-instrumented, not under-documented.

  2. Windows is a second-class platform. GBK/CP936 files silently byte-stripped by errors="ignore" (#8234); \\?\ path canonicalization breaking SQLite URIs (#8585); hanging cancellation tests (#8604). Chinese Windows users are a **core, vocal constituency** — the GBK report describes Notepad/legacy .txt/.csv/.md notes losing data with no log line.

  3. Deployment friction in constrained environments. Air-gapped/offline installs where Qwen3/3.5 are unreachable but DeepSeek R1 works (#1453); non-root Docker Hub startup failure (#8517); nginx reverse-proxy SSE buffering (#8516). Self-hosted enterprise users are hitting first-run blockers.

  4. Plugin ecosystem immaturity. Install fails with a bare "No package metadata was found" (#8595); plugin routes break sidebar state (#8590). The extension API is being used, but the loading/registration contract is still leaky.

Use cases evidenced: multi-workspace Matrix bridging, cross-agent collaboration and delegation, Creator (image/video generation) pipelines, offline/air-gapped deployment, third-party backend routing (Codex/Qoder/Kimi), scheduled agent tasks over IM, and long-term memory recall.

Satisfaction signals: reporters are precise, reproducible, and cooperative ("Happy to split this into three issues"); first-time contributors are filing docs fixes (#8606) and validation patches (#8550). Dissatisfaction signals: zero 👍 across the entire window, repeated "permanently broken / never rebuilds / cannot be decided" phrasing, and a 7.5-month-old collaboration-feedback thread closed without a linked fix.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ranked by risk:

  1. #8580 — Memory tag index 503 · OPEN, 4 comments, no fix PR, no assignee signal Highest-severity open bug with no owner. Every user who enables auto_memory_generate_tags is silently broken.

  2. #8592 — Creator REJECT permanently 422 · OPEN, 3 defects bundled Needs a maintainer decision on splitting into three Issues so defect 1 (the blocker) isn't buried under defects 2–3.

  3. #8517 — Hub Docker non-root Permission denied · OPEN since 2026-10-31 Blocks a whole deployment class; reporter could not even capture a version tag, which itself hints at packaging/tagging gaps.

  4. #8410 vs #8611 — duplicate "remove models from pool" work Two contributors solving the same Issue (#8195). Needs immediate arbitration to avoid contributor burnout — this is the clearest process risk in today's data.

  5. #8234 & #8236 — size/XXL & XL, open since 2026-10-14, "Under Review" GBK/CP936 decoding fix (data-loss class) and Ollama num_ctx context-window fix have been sitting 3+ weeks without merge. Both are high user impact; #8234 in particular silently destroys user file content.

  6. #8472 — reranker model center, size/XXL · open since 2026-10-28 Large feature PR with no review comments recorded; at risk of bit-rot.

  7. #8100 — resolved media capabilities at runtime · open since 2026-10-03 (5+ weeks) A one-line-class correctness fix (image-capable models rejected and image content stripped) stuck in review. Also #8274 (chat-switch state loss, since 2026-10-16).

  8. #5110 — Quote/reference for follow-up · open since 2026-06-11 Now unblocked by #8609; the Issue should be linked to the PR so it closes on merge.

  9. #2420 — cross-agent identity confusion · CLOSED with no linked fix Closed as feedback, but "identity confusion between agents" and "collaboration coherence" are architectural, not cosmetic. Recommend a follow-up design Issue so the closure doesn't read as dismissal.

Bottom line: QwenPaw is in a productive, contributor-driven consolidation phase — high fix throughput, fast issue-to-PR turnaround, and a clear focus on validation, lifecycle correctness, and Console ergonomics. The risks are concentrated in (a) four critical open bugs with no fix PR, (b) duplicate/competing PRs on the model-management path, and (c) a review queue of large PRs aging 3–5 weeks. A 2.3.x patch release closing #8549, #8533, #8596 and #8365 would be a well-supported next step.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a high-throughput hardening phase: 17 issues were touched in the last 24h (10 closed, 7 open/active) and 50 PRs were updated (14 merged/closed, 36 still open), with no new release. The closed-issue set is dominated by security and identity-access fixes — OIDC bearer verification limits (#12047), X-Forwarded-For spoofing (#12052), RPC session exhaustion (#11962) and a RUSTSEC-blocking dependency (#12272) — indicating the maintainers are clearing a release-gate backlog rather than shipping features. At the same time, several new S1/S2 defects landed today, including a permanently poisoned provider session (#12263) and a boot-time transcript overwrite that risks message loss (#12279). Overall project health looks strong on responsiveness (fast close rate, multiple follow-up PRs filed within hours), but the open security-adjacent bugs in approval and peer-resolution paths deserve attention.

Data note: only 2 of the 14 merged/closed PRs and the top 20 of 50 updated PRs were included in the supplied dataset; PR comment counts were unavailable.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h, and none listed in the latest-release feed. No changelog, breaking-change or migration notes to report. Several open PRs carry the release:v0.9.0 label (#9746, #12239, #12270, #12282), suggesting the next version is being staged but is not yet cut.

3. Project Progress

Closed issues (10) — fixes landed or resolved:

Issue Area Outcome
#12047 Gateway / OIDC Attempt limiter + outbound cap added via PR #12233
#12052 Gateway / XFF spoofing Rate-limit keying moved to proxy-appended hop via PR #12114
#11962 Runtime / daemon Idle RPC sessions now releasable (64-session cap)
#12176 Tools / MCP Deferred tool list ordering stabilized — restores prompt caching
#12272 Dependencies vodozemac RUSTSEC-2026-0445 / -0451 unblocked; Security gate green again
#12248 Runtime / approval No approval prompt for tool names absent from the turn
#12178 Tools deliver_file description no longer instructs URI citation in reply text
#12155 Onboarding Quickstart cancel message now matches actual config state
#12217 Docs Email tools-only setup clarified re: IMAP listener
#12249 Gateway / web Config pages hidden from accounts lacking config grant

Notable open PRs advancing work: PR #12281 (forwarded-loopback SOP cancel fix, follow-up to #12114), PR #12239 (holding authority through session effects, p1/release-gate), PR #12276 (streaming Telegram voice synthesis), PR #12275 (MCP local config controls), PR #12270 (daemon dashboard via relay, #10315 phase 2).

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. Issue #10926 — Matrix send_via treats peer user identities as room destinations — 9 comments, open since 2026-09-17, labeled status:accepted, priority:p2, risk:medium. The most-discussed item in the window. Underlying need: a coherent distinction between peer identity and channel destination in the outbound routing model — the same conceptual gap appears in today's #12283 (peer-group ignore handling) and in PR #12116 (Discord peer rejection). Three separate reports point to peer-resolution semantics being the project's most fragile abstraction.
  2. Issue #12047 (3 comments, closed) and Issue #12052 (2 comments, closed) — both identity-access gateway bugs reported by the same author and fixed within days. Underlying need: operators deploying behind reverse proxies and external IdPs want consistent trust-boundary rules across pairing, webhook, enrollment and config routes.
  3. Long-running high-risk PRs — #9809 (multi-model provider profiles, open since 2026-08-07, needs-author-action), #9746 (per-agent ownership scoping, priority:p1, release-gate), #11076 (agy_cli tool, size:XL). These carry the widest label sets and touch many subsystems; they are the de facto centers of design debate even without visible comment counts.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity as reported:

Severity Issue Status Fix PR?
S1 — workflow blocked #12263 Strict provider rejects a long tool-heavy session forever (422 missing field tool_call_id); conversation permanently unusable after ~38 messages / ~10 tool rounds OPEN None visible
S1 — workflow blocked #12272 vodozemac 0.11.0 RUSTSEC advisories fail cargo deny on every PR CLOSED Resolved same day
S2 (possibly S0) #12279 Channel startup caps a long transcript without a lock, overwriting a message appended in between — data loss in a boot window; reporter notes triage may prefer S0 OPEN None visible
S2 — security #12260 RPC cron/add and cron/patch pass approved = true for shell commands, treating any RPC caller as an operator approval OPEN None visible
S2 — security #12283 resolve_peer_set applies peer-group ignore per group over a HashMap, so outbound sends can reach ignored peers OPEN (filed today) None visible
S2 #10926 Matrix send_via misroutes to peer user identity as a room OPEN, accepted None visible
S2 #11962 64 live RPC sessions never released when idle CLOSED Fixed
S2 #12176 Non-deterministic MCP tool ordering busts prompt caching every session CLOSED Fixed
S2 — security #12047 OIDC bearer verification had no attempt limiter / outbound cap CLOSED PR #12233
S2 — security #12052 First-XFF-entry keying let clients claim the loopback exemption CLOSED PR #12114
S3 #12155 "No config written" shown while config.toml was written CLOSED Fixed

Assessment: the closed set shows good regression hygiene, but two patterns recur: (a) loopback/forwarded-header trust decisions implemented inconsistently per call site (#12052 → #12280 → #12261), and (b) approval semantics leaking across layers (#12260, #12248). A shared "is this request local / is this approved" helper would likely retire several of these at once.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

No new enhancement-labeled issues appeared in this window; feature direction is driven by open PRs:

  • Provider flexibility — #9809 multi-model profiles, [providers.connections] / [providers.model_presets] / [providers.fallback]; #11846 OpenRouter balance reporting with per-alias opt-in; #12277 SSE [DONE] sentinel tolerance at EOF; #12073 Codex stream retry fix.
  • Channel depth — #12276 Telegram voice replies synthesized during generation; #12065 Discord bot approval hardening.
  • Extensibility — #11076 Antigravity CLI (agy) delegation tool; #12216 multiple plugin registry origins; #12275 MCP-exposed local config.
  • Web/UX — #12269 paired-device voice settings; #12270 daemon dashboard served through ZeroRelay.

Prediction for v0.9.0: the release:v0.9.0 label clusters tightly around identity/access correctness — #9746 (per-agent ownership scoping), #12239 (authority held through session effects), #12282 (placement-exception doc), plus #12270 (relay dashboard). Expect v0.9.0 to be framed as a multi-tenant isolation and access-control release, not a feature release.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Configuration trust is a recurring sore point. #12155 ("cancelled, no config written" — but it was written) and #12249 (config pages visible to accounts without a config grant) show users do not trust the config layer's stated state or its visibility rules.
  • Long-running sessions are the biggest reliability complaint. #12263 (permanently rejected conversation after a tool-heavy session), #11962 (RPC session slots never freed), and #12279 (transcript overwrite at boot) all cluster around session lifecycle. This is the clearest signal of where real-world usage outgrows the current design.
  • Cost/efficiency awareness is explicit. #12176 was filed specifically because non-deterministic system prompts bust provider prompt caching — a user-visible cost regression, not just a cosmetic one.
  • Onboarding friction is low-severity but frequent. Quickstart messaging and email tools-only docs both needed correction.
  • Satisfaction indicators: 10 issues closed in 24h, with fixes often landing within 1–3 days of filing (#12047 → #12233 in ~11 days; #12280 → #12281 in under a day). Contributors are actively self-filing follow-ups (#12280, #12282, #12261), which suggests a healthy review culture rather than user frustration.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  1. PR #9809 — multi-model provider profiles. Open since 2026-08-07 (~3 months), size:XL, risk:high, risk:manual, needs-author-action. Touches nearly every subsystem label in the repo. Highest-risk merge in the backlog; needs a decision or a split plan.
  2. PR #9746 — per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search. Open since 2026-08-04, priority:p1, release-gate, release:v0.9.0, topic:identity-access. This is a release blocker that has been open for three months.
  3. PR #11076 — agy_cli Antigravity CLI tool. Open since 2026-09-23, size:XL; its placement-exception doc (PR #12229) is still open too, so it is blocked on process, not code.
  4. Issue #10926 — Matrix send_via misrouting. Accepted, priority:p2, 9 comments, open since 2026-09-17, no linked fix PR. Highest-discussion bug with no visible remediation path.
  5. PR #11846 — OpenRouter balance reporting; explicitly depends on unmerged #11845, so it is stalled in a chain.
  6. PR #12065 / PR #12116 — Discord approval and peer-delivery fixes open since 2026-10-27 / 2026-10-30. Small (XS/S) but risk:high on #12065; both relate directly to the still-open #10926 peer-resolution theme and could be batched into one peer-routing decision.

Health verdict: strong triage velocity and clear release discipline, with risk concentrated in (a) the three multi-month XL PRs and (b) inconsistent identity/trust primitives across gateway, RPC and peer-resolution code paths.
