item.content:encoded:
AI 开源趋势日报 2026-11-07

数据来源: GitHub Trending + GitHub Search API | 生成时间: 2026-11-07 02:20 UTC

AI Open Source Trends Report — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Agent "skills" packaging is the single loudest signal today: cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+2,548), mattpocock/skills (+2,070) and google/skills (+534) pulled in over 5,100 new stars combined, turning portable capability bundles for coding agents into a first-class distribution format. NVIDIA's auto-ontology (+2,015) marks a major vendor betting on semantic graph layers over raw vector retrieval, promising deterministic query generation and explainable context for agent workflows. Meanwhile the context/memory tier keeps compounding — graphify (143,582), claude-mem (114,050), headroom (79,031) and mem0 (68,531) all sit in the top tier of the topic search, evidence that "cheaper, structured context" has replaced "bigger context window" as the engineering battleground. Coding-agent harnesses and terminals (ECC at 298,619, Codewhale, DeepSeek-Reasonix, oh-my-pi) continue to expand, and vertical agents in finance and career search are producing some of the fastest-growing application repos.

2. Top Projects by Category

🔧 AI Infrastructure

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
ollama/ollama Go 186,153 Local model runtime serving Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen and Gemma behind one CLI/API. It remains the default on-ramp for self-hosted inference, which keeps it central every time a new open-weight family ships.
huggingface/transformers Python 168,607 The reference model-definition framework for text, vision, audio and multimodal models across inference and training. Its breadth makes it the layer most new open-weight releases target first.
pytorch/pytorch Python 105,219 Tensors and dynamic neural networks with strong GPU acceleration. Still the substrate underneath nearly every training and fine-tuning stack in this report.
tensorflow/tensorflow C++ 201,367 The long-standing ML framework, now primarily a production-serving and legacy-ecosystem anchor. Its star count keeps it atop the topic search even as new development concentrates in PyTorch and Rust tooling.
langchain4j/langchain4j Java 13,367 Idiomatic Java library for LLM apps on the JVM with a unified provider API, tool calling/MCP, agents and RAG. It matters because Spring Boot and Quarkus backends are where a large share of enterprise production still lives.
0xPlaygrounds/rig Rust 9,081 Modular Rust toolkit for building scalable LLM applications. It represents the steady Rust migration of agent and inference plumbing where latency and memory footprint dominate.
skyzh/tiny-llm Python 5,680 A build-your-own tiny vLLM + Qwen inference system for systems engineers, running on Apple Silicon. Educational in framing but directly useful for understanding KV cache, batching and serving internals.
FonaTech/Project_Chronos Python 207 Zero-stall MoE inference via lookahead prediction and async DMA prefetching, tuned for SSD I/O with hybrid MLA + sliding-window attention. Small project, but a concrete signal that MoE serving and storage-bound inference are the new optimization frontier.

🤖 AI Agents / Workflows

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
affaan-m/ECC JavaScript 298,619 An agent-harness performance optimization system spanning skills, instincts, memory, security and research-first development across Claude Code, Codex, Opencode and Cursor. At nearly 300k stars it is the clearest evidence that harness-level tuning, not just model choice, is where agent quality is now decided.
NousResearch/hermes-agent Python 261,224 "The agent that grows with you" — a persistent, self-extending personal agent. Its scale signals strong appetite for long-running agents that accumulate capability rather than reset each session.
cloudflare/security-audit-skill JavaScript 0 (+2,548) A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings. It is today's top trending repo overall, showing vendors shipping official agent skills as a product surface.
mattpocock/skills Shell 0 (+2,070) "Skills for Real Engineers," published straight from an .agents directory. Its second-place trending finish confirms skills are now a personal-brand and knowledge-sharing format, not just vendor tooling.
google/skills Python 0 (+534) Official Agent Skills for Google products and technologies. A hyperscaler formally packaging its APIs for coding agents is a notable shift in how developer platforms are being distributed.
langgenius/dify Python 160,579 Collaborative workspace for building agentic workflows and RAG pipelines with broad model and tool support, deployable cloud, VPC or self-hosted. It is the de-facto open alternative to managed agent platforms for teams moving from prototype to production.
browser-use/browser-use Python 120,218 Python library for AI browser agents plus a hosted cloud with stealth browsers and an agent API. Browser control remains the most commercially legible agent capability, and this repo owns that niche.
Panniantong/Agent-Reach Python 109,705 One CLI giving agents read/search access to Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili and XiaoHongShu with zero API fees. It addresses the practical bottleneck of agent data access without per-source integration work.

📦 AI Applications

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
open-webui/open-webui Svelte 157,955 User-friendly self-hosted AI interface supporting Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs. It remains the most-starred front end in the ecosystem and the standard UI layer for local deployments.
f/prompts.chat MDX 176,079 The community prompt library formerly known as Awesome ChatGPT Prompts, self-hostable for private organizational use. It shows prompt assets still command enormous attention as reusable organizational IP.
Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps Python 144,049 A collection of 100+ AI agents, agent skills and RAG apps, all free and open source. It functions as the practical reference catalogue developers copy from when starting new agent products.
harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo Python 140,278 Generates HD short videos from a topic or keyword via an automated LLM workflow. It is a durable example of a single-vertical generative pipeline reaching massive consumer demand.
hugohe3/ppt-master Python 74,278 Turns documents or topics into native PowerPoint decks with real shapes, transitions, charts and narration from speaker notes. Native-format output rather than image slides is what distinguishes it from earlier deck generators.
openbq-org/OpenBB Python 75,171 Open data platform for analysts, quants and AI agents. It is becoming the standard data layer that financial agent projects build on top of.
HKUDS/DeepTutor Python 55,972 Lifelong personalized tutoring system from the HKU data science lab. Education remains one of the strongest product-market fits for persistent-memory agents.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm JavaScript 68,015 Local-first agent workspace bundling document chat, agents and model management in one owned deployment. Its "stop renting your intelligence" positioning captures the self-hosting mood of the moment.

🧠 LLMs / Training

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch Jupyter Notebook 107,935 Step-by-step PyTorch implementation of a ChatGPT-like LLM. It is the most-cited hands-on path from transformer theory to working training loop.
rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch Python 77,166 A "learn it, build it, ship it" curriculum for AI engineering. Its 77k stars show demand shifting from ML theory toward end-to-end production skills.
labmlai/annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations Python 67,716 60+ deep-learning paper implementations with side-by-side notes, covering transformer variants, optimizers, GANs, RL and distillation. It stays relevant because it explains the mechanisms that newer architectures recombine.
open-compass/opencompass Python 7,570 LLM evaluation platform spanning 100+ datasets across knowledge, reasoning, coding, science, long-context and safety, with support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, GLM and DeepSeek. Evaluation breadth is increasingly the real moat when choosing models.
EgoAlpha/prompt-in-context-learning Jupyter Notebook 2,250 Curated resources for in-context learning and prompt engineering across ChatGPT-era and later models. It tracks a technique layer that survives model churn.
AkaliKong/MiniOneRec Python 1,955 A minimal reproduction of OneRec, the generative recommendation approach. Small but indicative of recommender systems converging on LLM-style generative formulations.
thinkwee/AgentsMeetRL HTML 1,877 An awesome list for agentic reinforcement learning. It marks RL-for-agents as a distinct, rapidly consolidating research area.
datamllab/OpenEBFM Python 282 Open-source code for training and scaling energy-based foundation models. A niche but notable non-autoregressive alternative worth watching.

🔍 RAG / Knowledge

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
Graphify-Labs/graphify Python 143,582 Turns a codebase with docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph via local deterministic AST parsing, with no vector store. Its 143k stars make it the flagship of the "graph over embeddings" wave.
thedotmack/claude-mem TypeScript 114,050 Captures everything an agent does per session, compresses it with AI and reinjects relevant context into future sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot and more. Cross-agent portability is what makes it strategically interesting.
infiniflow/ragflow Go 93,699 A RAG engine that has grown into agent-native context infrastructure and a database in its own right. It is one of the few RAG projects that has successfully repositioned rather than stagnated.
NVIDIA/auto-ontology Python 0 (+2,015) A Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data, enabling deterministic query generation, better context retrieval and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows. Its +2,015 star day makes it the strongest single-day signal in the retrieval space today.
unclecode/crawl4ai Python 87,017 Apache-2.0 crawler powering a hosted scraping, extraction and search API for AI agents, with a free tier of 1,000 credits monthly. It is the practical ingestion layer most RAG stacks still start from.
mem0ai/mem0 Python 68,531 Drop-in memory infrastructure giving agents persistent, production-grade context. Memory has become a separate purchasable layer rather than a feature inside agent frameworks.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom Python 79,031 Compresses tool outputs, logs, files and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM — 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60–95% fewer for JSON — as a library, proxy and MCP server. It quantifies the token-economics turn in retrieval design.
milvus-io/milvus Go 46,608 Cloud-native vector database built for scalable ANN search. It remains the reference production-grade option even as vectorless and hybrid approaches gain mindshare.

3. Trend Signal Analysis

Three signals stand out. First, agent skills are becoming a distribution format. Cloudflare, Google and an individual engineer all shipped skills repos that trended simultaneously — a pattern that looks like the npm-ification of agent capability. Skills are small, composable and provider-agnostic, and they let vendors expose APIs to agents without building a full framework.

Second, context engineering is displacing context expansion. The retrieval tier is splitting into four distinct bets: knowledge graphs (graphify, NVIDIA auto-ontology), session memory (claude-mem, mem0), token compression (headroom, caveman at 65% reduction), and vectorless reasoning-based indexing (PageIndex, LEANN). Vector databases like milvus, qdrant, weaviate and Alibaba's in-process zvec still matter, but they are no longer the default answer. Determinism and explainability — every edge explained, deterministic query generation — are now explicit selling points, which suggests enterprises are hitting the reliability ceiling of pure embedding similarity.

Third, the agent harness is the new IDE. ECC at 298k stars, Codewhale in Rust, DeepSeek-Reasonix, oh-my-pi and openclaude all compete on harness quality, multi-provider routing and terminal ergonomics rather than model weights. Notably, Rust appears repeatedly (rig, Codewhale, zvec, qdrant, caveman), and Project_Chronos points at MoE serving and SSD-bound inference as the next performance frontier. Verticals — finance (TradingAgents, Vibe-Trading, daily_stock_analysis, OpenBB), career search, tutoring, slide generation — are consolidating fast, which is exactly what you expect once the harness layer stabilizes.

4. Community Hot Spots

  • Agent skills as a package format — cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+2,548), mattpocock/skills (+2,070), google/skills (+534). Worth studying the file layout and invocation conventions now; this is likely how agent capabilities get distributed over the next year.
  • Graph and ontology layers over RAG — NVIDIA/auto-ontology (+2,015) and graphify (143,582) both argue that structured semantics beat similarity search for code and enterprise data. High-value area for anyone building retrieval for agents.
  • Token-economics tooling — headroom (79,031) and caveman (118,024) sell measurable token reduction rather than capability. As agent loops lengthen, cost compression becomes a first-class infrastructure category.
  • Agent harness optimization — affaan-m/ECC at 298,619 stars shows harness-level work (memory, instincts, security, research loops) draws more attention than any single model release.
  • Vertical agent products with native output — ppt-master (74,278, real .pptx shapes and animations), career-ops (80,736), TradingAgents (121,029). Native-format output and human-in-the-loop submission are the differentiators separating these from demo-grade wrappers.

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

datamllab/OpenEBFM Python 282 Open-source code for training and scaling energy-based foundation models. A niche but notable non-autoregressive alternative worth watching.

🔍 RAG / Knowledge

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
Graphify-Labs/graphify Python 143,582 Turns a codebase with docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph via local deterministic AST parsing, with no vector store. Its 143k stars make it the flagship of the "graph over embeddings" wave.
thedotmack/claude-mem TypeScript 114,050 Captures everything an agent does per session, compresses it with AI and reinjects relevant context into future sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot and more. Cross-agent portability is what makes it strategically interesting.
infiniflow/ragflow Go 93,699 A RAG engine that has grown into agent-native context infrastructure and a database in its own right. It is one of the few RAG projects that has successfully repositioned rather than stagnated.
NVIDIA/auto-ontology Python 0 (+2,015) A Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data, enabling deterministic query generation, better context retrieval and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows. Its +2,015 star day makes it the strongest single-day signal in the retrieval space today.
unclecode/crawl4ai Python 87,017 Apache-2.0 crawler powering a hosted scraping, extraction and search API for AI agents, with a free tier of 1,000 credits monthly. It is the practical ingestion layer most RAG stacks still start from.
mem0ai/mem0 Python 68,531 Drop-in memory infrastructure giving agents persistent, production-grade context. Memory has become a separate purchasable layer rather than a feature inside agent frameworks.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom Python 79,031 Compresses tool outputs, logs, files and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM — 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60–95% fewer for JSON — as a library, proxy and MCP server. It quantifies the token-economics turn in retrieval design.
milvus-io/milvus Go 46,608 Cloud-native vector database built for scalable ANN search. It remains the reference production-grade option even as vectorless and hybrid approaches gain mindshare.

3. Trend Signal Analysis

Three signals stand out. First, agent skills are becoming a distribution format. Cloudflare, Google and an individual engineer all shipped skills repos that trended simultaneously — a pattern that looks like the npm-ification of agent capability. Skills are small, composable and provider-agnostic, and they let vendors expose APIs to agents without building a full framework.

Second, context engineering is displacing context expansion. The retrieval tier is splitting into four distinct bets: knowledge graphs (graphify, NVIDIA auto-ontology), session memory (claude-mem, mem0), token compression (headroom, caveman at 65% reduction), and vectorless reasoning-based indexing (PageIndex, LEANN). Vector databases like milvus, qdrant, weaviate and Alibaba's in-process zvec still matter, but they are no longer the default answer. Determinism and explainability — every edge explained, deterministic query generation — are now explicit selling points, which suggests enterprises are hitting the reliability ceiling of pure embedding similarity.

Third, the agent harness is the new IDE. ECC at 298k stars, Codewhale in Rust, DeepSeek-Reasonix, oh-my-pi and openclaude all compete on harness quality, multi-provider routing and terminal ergonomics rather than model weights. Notably, Rust appears repeatedly (rig, Codewhale, zvec, qdrant, caveman), and Project_Chronos points at MoE serving and SSD-bound inference as the next performance frontier. Verticals — finance (TradingAgents, Vibe-Trading, daily_stock_analysis, OpenBB), career search, tutoring, slide generation — are consolidating fast, which is exactly what you expect once the harness layer stabilizes.

4. Community Hot Spots

  • Agent skills as a package format — cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+2,548), mattpocock/skills (+2,070), google/skills (+534). Worth studying the file layout and invocation conventions now; this is likely how agent capabilities get distributed over the next year.
  • Graph and ontology layers over RAG — NVIDIA/auto-ontology (+2,015) and graphify (143,582) both argue that structured semantics beat similarity search for code and enterprise data. High-value area for anyone building retrieval for agents.
  • Token-economics tooling — headroom (79,031) and caveman (118,024) sell measurable token reduction rather than capability. As agent loops lengthen, cost compression becomes a first-class infrastructure category.
  • Agent harness optimization — affaan-m/ECC at 298,619 stars shows harness-level work (memory, instincts, security, research loops) draws more attention than any single model release.
  • Vertical agent products with native output — ppt-master (74,278, real .pptx shapes and animations), career-ops (80,736), TradingAgents (121,029). Native-format output and human-in-the-loop submission are the differentiators separating these from demo-grade wrappers.

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
AI CLI 工具社区动态日报 2026-11-06

生成时间: 2026-11-06 02:48 UTC | 覆盖工具: 7 个

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

横向对比

跨工具对比报告 — AI CLI 开发者工具生态

日期： 2026-11-06 · 覆盖工具： Claude Code、OpenAI Codex、Gemini CLI、GitHub Copilot CLI、OpenCode、Pi、Qwen Code

1. 生态概览

AI CLI 工具领域正围绕三个共同的工程问题逐步收敛：上下文经济学（缓存 TTL、剪枝、节省 token 的导航方式）、智能体可靠性信号（子智能体谎报成功、挂起、流式工具调用中途损坏）、MCP 运维成熟度（OAuth 生命周期、TLS 信任、会话恢复后的 schema 漂移）。与此同时，工具之间的成熟度差距正在扩大：Gemini CLI 和 Copilot CLI 正在交付深层次的平台级修复（路径遍历补丁、ACP 策略强制执行、重试正确性），而 Claude Code 今天的主导事件是一场信任事故而非功能竞赛——这表明隐私与安全默认值如今已成为竞争差异化因素，而不再只是合规勾选项。Windows 与跨平台正确性（路径语义、进程树、libc/原生插件兼容性）在几乎所有社区中都是被过度反映的痛点。此外，多个项目（Codex、Qwen Code）今天没有社区信号，而两个工具（OpenCode、Codex）只表现出 PR 或发布层面的动能、零 issue 活动——这说明社区健康度在整个生态中已不再均匀一致。

2. 活跃度对比

工具 Issue（已更新） PR（已更新） Discussions 发布状态（24 小时）
Claude Code 约 10 个热门 + 荣誉提名（1 个主导：#107757，172 👍） 1 N/A（未提供） 无发布
OpenAI Codex ⚠️ N/A（摘要生成失败） ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ 未知
Gemini CLI 约 10 个热门 + 窗口期内 50 个更新 10+（以安全 + 正确性为主） N/A（未提供） 无发布
GitHub Copilot CLI 22 个更新（列出 10 个热门） 0 N/A（未提供） 2 个发布（v1.0.106 + 预发布）
OpenCode 0 个更新（已标记为报告缺口） 10+ N/A（未提供） 1 个发布（process-daemon v0.5.0）
Pi 列出 10 个热门，跟踪器"异常活跃" 10+ 1 个 Ideas + 1 个 Q&A + 2 个 Show-and-tell 无发布
Qwen Code ⚠️ N/A（摘要生成失败） ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ 未知

数据质量说明：

  • OpenAI Codex 和 Qwen Code 的摘要生成失败——它们被标记为 N/A，而非"不活跃"。不应从其缺失中推断任何结论。
  • OpenCode 报告的字面 issue 更新数为零；摘要本身将其标记为"报告缺口而非代码库沉寂"，并以 PR 描述作为替代信号。应视为 issue 活跃度 N/A。
  • 任何来源均未提供 Discussions 数据；在 GitHub Discussions 似乎是主要渠道的地方（Pi、OpenCode），不应将其解读为社区沉默。
  • Claude Code、Gemini CLI 和 Pi 在窗口期内无发布；Copilot CLI 和 OpenCode 是今天仅有的发布方。

3. 共性功能方向

在两个或以上工具社区中出现需求的方向：

方向 工具 具体需求
上下文 / 缓存经济学 Claude Code、Copilot CLI、Pi、Gemini CLI 更长的 Anthropic prompt-cache TTL（Copilot #5220）、缓存预热以阻止 5 分钟过期（Pi #11857 — 占 p2 支出的 26%）、模型判定的垃圾工具输出剪枝（Copilot #5362）、节省 token 的上下文管理与"Tactful Extraction"（Gemini #19561）、自动记忆越界损害用户控制（Claude #107555）
MCP 可靠性与生命周期 Claude Code、Copilot CLI、OpenCode、Pi 预热会话中 MCP 服务器在第一轮后被杀（Claude #107179/#107060）、工具 schema 在会话中途丢失（Copilot #5367）、OAuth"已连接"状态陈旧（Copilot #5366）、回调关闭时 OAuth 挂起（Pi #11855）、私有 CA 的按服务器 TLS 信任（OpenCode #60039/#60041）
无头 / 自动化与终端宿主集成 Copilot CLI、Claude Code、Pi、Gemini CLI remote-control --headless（Claude #30447）、面向终端宿主的 OSC 7501 智能体状态上报（Copilot #5320；Pi #11670/#11816）、无浏览器副作用的设备码登录（Copilot #5358）、Workers 运行时进程注入（Pi #10846）
沙箱化 + 不安全命令防护 Gemini CLI、Claude Code、Copilot CLI 零依赖 OS 沙箱以解锁原生 bash（Gemini #19873）、阻止破坏性 git reset --force/数据库写入（Gemini #22672）、pkill -f 'cat' 误向 macOS 应用发送 SIGTERM（Claude #106029）、Tab 执行 /clear 导致数据丢失（Claude #106074）、不透明的沙箱策略上报（Copilot #5365/#5360）
会话持久化与多路复用 Claude Code、Copilot CLI、Pi 跨界面共享会话列表（Claude #107611）、可信赖的会话恢复（Copilot #5359/#5361）、切换时会话分离而非拆除（Pi #11829/#11830）、多设备会话同步（Pi #11696）
子智能体/技能可靠性与可观测性 Gemini CLI、Claude Code MAX_TURNS 后误报 GOAL 成功（Gemini #22323/#21983）、技能/子智能体触发不足（Gemini #21968）、Browser Agent 忽略 settings.json 覆盖（Gemini #22267）、永久记忆越界（Claude #107555）
Windows / 跨平台正确性 OpenCode、Pi、Copilot CLI、Gemini CLI Git Bash PWD 规范化（OpenCode #61619）、孤儿进程树（Pi #11854）、.cmd 执行失败（Pi #10616）、Windows 上多分钟级轮次卡顿（Copilot #5356）、Termux/Bionic 已损坏 6 个月（Copilot #3333）、Windows dev: 0 stat 修复（Gemini #30033）
隐私与数据卫生默认值 Claude Code、（Copilot 隐含） 彻底移除 User-Agent 中的邮箱暴露，而非使其可配置（Claude #107757）；开源隐私模块（Claude #107768）
AST 感知 / 语义化代码导航 Gemini CLI、Claude Code（隐含） 关于 AST grep/映射的三 issue EPIC，以减少错位读取和 token 噪声（Gemini #22745/#22746/#22747）

最强的跨领域主题： MCP 是新的集成税。 六个活跃社区中有四个独立提交了 MCP 故障——这如今已是"能用，然后停止工作"类报告的最大单一来源。

4. 差异化分析

功能侧重

  • Claude Code — 智能体自主性深度（自动记忆、远程控制、守护进程模式），并在行为正确性上投入最重：记忆越界、破坏性操作防护、桌面/会话统一。今天的议程以信任为中心（隐私泄露、数据丢失的 Tab bug）。
  • Gemini CLI — 深层次平台工程：安全加固（路径遍历）、流式/重试语义的正确性，以及在 AST 感知导航 + 原生 bash 沙箱上的战略性押注。其待办列表在架构上最具前瞻性。
  • GitHub Copilot CLI — 终端环境集成与编辑器交接（/code、内联 Kitty 图像、/settings 仪表盘）以及模型路由透明度（基于 ACP 的 Fusion）。明确瞄准 VS Code / 终端原生的企业开发者。
  • OpenCode — 基础设施与自托管：站点/worker 整合、按服务器 MCP 网络、会话人体工学（--all）。定位为可配置、部署灵活的 CLI，而非托管优先的产品。
  • Pi — SDK/嵌入与可扩展性：Workers 运行时支持、自定义身份前导、会话同步、扩展沙箱。是这一组中最类库化的——在构建平台，而不仅仅是一个 CLI。
  • Copilot CLI vs. Claude Code — Copilot 偏向编辑器/终端宿主嵌入与企业策略可见性；Claude 偏向智能体自主性与桌面人体工学。

目标用户

工具 主要用户
Claude Code 运行长时间、自主桌面/守护进程会话的高级用户
Gemini CLI 在模型 + 智能体平台上构建的工程团队；编辑器集成（--acp）
Copilot CLI 企业 VS Code / 终端开发者；以 GitHub 为中心的工作流
OpenCode 自托管者、基础设施导向的团队、私有网络 MCP 用户
Pi SDK 集成者、扩展作者、多设备高级用户
Codex / Qwen Code ⚠️ 今日数据不足

技术路径

  • Gemini CLI 最具防御性：p1 安全补丁、流式工具调用的重试/丢弃正确性、ACP 中的 hook 策略强制执行。
  • Copilot CLI 最具发布驱动性：无可见 PR 活动直接发布，围绕 ACP 界面和认证人体工学迭代。
  • OpenCode 最具基础设施优先性：PTY 协议升级、构建时 Worker 冒烟测试、部署门禁。
  • Pi 最具SDK/扩展导向性：prompt 段落定制、运行时无关的进程注入、持久会话同步。
  • Claude Code 最具桌面应用重量级，同时伴随当天最强的隐私/信任事件。

5. 社区动能与成熟度

最活跃的社区（今日）：

  1. Gemini CLI — 实质性工程量最高（50 个 issue 更新、10+ PR、多个 p1 安全/正确性修复）。动能高且有方向。
  2. Pi — 跟踪器"异常活跃"，10+ PR、完整的编辑待办（Windows 进程树、文件编码、缓存预热、OAuth），以及自发的社区工具（Slack 机器人、CaseClip）。强烈的生态建设信号。
  3. GitHub Copilot CLI — 22 个 issue 更新 + 2 个发布；暴露出高强度的日常摩擦（MCP 状态漂移、会话恢复、Windows 卡顿），但也在积极发布。动能高，成熟度中等——可靠性问题是主导主题。
  4. Claude Code — 由单个高参与度的信任事件（172 👍）和一波桌面应用分诊主导。情绪参与度高，今日功能速度较低（无发布，1 个 PR）。
  5. OpenCode — 今日仅有 PR 动能；基础设施整合与 MCP 网络。社区反馈信号缺失（0 issue）——成熟度评估为暂定。
  6. OpenAI Codex / Qwen Code — ⚠️ 数据不足。 不参与排名。

快速迭代者： Gemini CLI 和 Copilot CLI（Gemini 通过安全/正确性补丁，Copilot 通过发布）。走向平台稳定成熟： OpenCode 和 Pi（协议升级、冒烟测试、SDK 接口）。信任修复模式： Claude Code（隐私争议）和 Copilot CLI（MCP/OAuth/会话恢复可靠性集群）。

成熟度解读： Copilot CLI 展现出最高的发布节奏但最低的可靠性一致性（脆弱的 MCP/OAuth/会话状态）。Gemini CLI 展现出最强的修复纪律，但有一批误报成功信号的 bug 会侵蚀自动化信任。Codex 和 Qwen Code 今日因数据缺口均无法评估。

6. 趋势信号

  1. MCP 运维成熟度是首要可靠性前沿。 在 Claude Code、Copilot CLI、OpenCode 和 Pi 中，反复出现的故障模式是状态漂移：连接状态、工具注册表和认证令牌不同步，且无自动协调。预计"MCP 生命周期管理"（健康检查、自动重启、schema 协调）将成为一等功能类别。给开发者的行动建议： 为 MCP 监管预留工程时间；不要假设"已连接"就等于"可用"。

  2. 上下文经济学正成为一项预算科目。 Pi 将 Anthropic 缓存过期量化在三周内约 $1,430 / 占 p2 支出的 26%；Copilot 正在请求更长的缓存 TTL 和模型判定的剪枝；Gemini 正在设计 AST 工具以减少 token 噪声。行动： 将 prompt-cache 配置和上下文剪枝视为成本工程，而不仅仅是 UX。

  3. 智能体误报成功正成为新兴的信任危机。 Gemini 的子智能体在达到 MAX_TURNS 或在 Wayland 上失败后仍上报 GOAL/success；Claude 的自动记忆将一次性纠正提升为永久规则。行动： 围绕智能体的声明构建外部验证（测试、diff、退出码）——不要信任智能体自己的状态字段。

  4. 自动化与无头操作在各处都被需求。 remote-control --headless、Workers 运行时支持、OSC 7501 状态上报、设备码登录和多设备会话同步都指向同一方向：AI CLI 正在成为后台服务，而非交互式玩具。行动： 现在就为无 TTY、守护进程化、可嵌入的运行方式做设计。

  5. Windows 与跨平台正确性是一项持续税负。 七个工具中有六个暴露出 Windows 特有的缺陷（路径语义、进程树、.cmd 执行、多分钟级卡顿、glibc/Bionic 不兼容）。行动： 如果你的团队重度使用 Windows，在工具选型时应高度重视平台修复速度——它在各处都滞后。

  6. 隐私与安全默认值如今具有竞争力。 Claude Code 的 User-Agent/邮箱泄露（172 👍，要求移除而非可配置）以及隐私模块的开源表明，用户将数据卫生视为不可谈判。行动： 审计你的 CLI 在网络边界发送的内容（请求头、遥测、查询参数）——这如今是一项采购标准。

  7. 沙箱化 + 原生 bash 是一种刻意的设计张力。 Gemini 的零依赖沙箱提案旨在在不丢失安全性的前提下解锁 grep/sed/awk 链式调用。行动： 关注这一领域——"智能体化 bash"的胜出方案很可能定义下一代工具执行方式。

  8. 编辑器/终端宿主嵌入是下一个集成层。 ACP Fusion 广告、/code 交接、OSC 状态协议和内联图像渲染表明，CLI 正被吸收进编辑器和终端复用器，而非独立使用。行动： 如果你构建编辑器或终端工具，优先支持 ACP/状态协议。

方法论说明： 本报告仅基于所提供的社区摘要综合而成。OpenAI Codex 和 Qwen Code 因摘要生成失败被标记为 N/A，并被排除在动能排名之外，而非视为不活跃。Issue/PR 计数反映报告窗口期，未跨仓库归一化。

各工具详细报告

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills 社区热点

数据来源: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Data source: github.com/anthropics/skills · Snapshot date: 2026-11-06

Method note: PR comment counts are unavailable in this dataset (Comments: undefined for all 50 PRs). Rankings below are therefore inferred from contemporaneity of updates, cross-linked issues, recurring contributors, and per-Skill PR clusters — not raw comment volume. Issue rankings use actual comment/👍 counts.

1. Top Skills Ranking (by attention signal)

# Skill / PR What it does Discussion highlights Status
1 skill-creator — #1298, #1997, #1681 Meta-skill for authoring, packaging, and evaluating Skills Largest PR cluster; three independent fixes (trigger-eval isolation + Windows pipes, YAML frontmatter scalar parsing, direct package_skill.py execution). Ties into issue #202 ("should be updated to best practice") — authoring tooling is the ecosystem's weakest link All OPEN
2 mcp-builder — #1742 Generates and evaluates MCP servers from specs Breaking rename in mcp>=2.0.0 (streamablehttp_client → streamable_http_client), plus custom headers now require create_mcp_http_client. Directly paired with issue #1390 (eval harness scores 0/N) — the skill's runtime and harness both need repair OPEN (cf. #1668)
3 webapp-testing — #1980, #1976 Browser-driven testing and element discovery Security-first framing: removal of shell=True (CWE-78 command injection) in with_server.py, plus correctness fix for textarea/select mislabeled as text Both OPEN
4 docx — #1792, #1734 Word document manipulation (revisions, comments) Silent-failure pattern dominates: LibreOffice timeout reported as success without verifying w:ins/w:del removal; request to detect orphaned comments. Mirrors issue #2018 (invalid XML on merge) — docx is the most bug-reported bundled skill Both OPEN

  4. #29879 — fix(core,cli,sdk): discard buffered tool calls on mid-stream error or retry Prevents partially-streamed ToolCallRequests from being executed after failure/retry — a correctness fix that avoids duplicate side effects.

  9. #30043 — feat(core): expose tool call ids to hooks Adds tool_call_id to hook inputs so integrations can pair before/after events — a small but high-leverage change for observability tooling.

  10. #30017 — fix(core): keep committed turns when cancelling a tool-result continuation Stops cancellation from rolling history back before the user prompt, which erased already-executed tool turns that may have modified files.

  • Context economics — Requests cluster around making the context window cheaper and cleaner: longer Claude prompt cache TTL (#5220), model-judged pruning of junk tool output (#5362), and implicit reliance on /compact as the only recovery path (#5367).

The common thread is that MCP connection state and the model's tool registry fall out of sync with no automatic reconciliation.
  2. OAuth token lifecycle is fragile. Both the Entra/remote-MCP path (#5366) and the ACP interactive path (#5350, #5229) show refresh-token grants not being attempted, or the code→token exchange not running at all. Only a server restart recovers.

  5. Sandbox policy is opaque. With duplicate read-write rules appearing unexplained in sandbox.decision (#5365) and enterprise-managed policies failing during option updates (#5360), admins lack the observability needed to debug policy in managed environments.

Long-running (opened 28 Oct), part of umbrella #40111, and references a cluster of prior issues (#23506, #14696, #26862, #1694) — clearly a sustained pain point.

  5. #60041 [OPEN] feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use — karup Stacked on #60039; adds the first-use TOFU flow for private-network MCP certs. Reviewers should treat #60039/#60041 as a pair — the second diff is small only once the first lands.

  6. #62226 [OPEN] fix(mcp): skip codemode query for LaunchDarkly — aNewMoose Adds mcp.launchdarkly.com to the rejectsUnknownQuery host list so OpenCode stops appending ?codemode=false, which LaunchDarkly rejects with HTTP 400. Small, surgical fix; the allowlist pattern suggests more hosts will need adding over time.

  7. #60895 [OPEN] feat(cli): add --all to session list — ColonelToad Currently opencode session list always filters to the current directory's project. --all exposes cross-project sessions. Low-risk ergonomics win for multi-repo users; closes #59004.

  8. #62227 [CLOSED] fix(core): do not spend the image budget on payload-free images — jimmyallinai boundImages was evicting remote images that carry no inline payload, wasting budget without reclaiming anything. Fix makes the eviction decision payload-aware. Contributor PR, already closed — likely merged or superseded.

  9. #61547 [OPEN] fix(tui,app): only apply extended 5min retry to ServiceUnavailableError location sync — cxxde Cold UNC workspace plugins caused slow startup and left a 5-minute retry blanket applied too broadly. Narrows the retry to the specific error class. Affects Windows/network-share users disproportionately.

  10. #61619 [OPEN] fix(cli): normalize Windows PWD in run command — zpzjzj Git Bash supplies /c/... for PWD; native process.chdir() needs C:\.... Routes through the existing FSUtil.windowsPath() before the noninteractive run path chdirs. Closes #61603.

Also worth a glance: #62235 [CLOSED, needs:compliance] — a full rebrand of the CLI/app/config paths to "harpcode" with a built-in local llama.cpp provider layer and default MCP servers; closed rather than reviewed, reinforcing that config-path and branding changes to a fork are out of scope upstream. #62067 [CLOSED] restored configured agent colors in Mini TUI; #61607 [OPEN] fixes the What's New popup for markdown-style Highlights changelogs; #57088 [OPEN] restores edge-snapped window bounds that resolveWindowState drops when Windows reports invisible resize borders.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Caveat: with zero issue and zero discussion activity in the window, these directions are inferred from PR intent and the issues those PRs cite — not from request volume.

  • Enterprise/private networking for MCP. Two stacked PRs (#60039, #60041) plus an umbrella issue (#40111) and four historical cross-references point squarely at self-signed certs and private CAs. Remote MCP adoption is being gated by TLS trust ergonomics, not by tooling capability.
  • Per-server MCP configurability in general. The TLS block and the host-specific rejectsUnknownQuery allowlist (#62226) both follow the same shape: move behavior from global heuristics to per-server config.
  • Multi-project session ergonomics. session list --all (#60895) is a request to stop assuming cwd == the only project a developer works in.
  • Local-model / offline-first defaults. The harpcode fork PR (#62235) proposed a built-in lowest-priority llama.cpp provider layer. Even though it was closed, it is the clearest recent artifact of demand for a zero-config local inference path.
  • Docs/site consolidation. #62209 → #62229 signals an internal direction (SolidStart + a single services/site worker) that will shape contributor workflow more than any user-facing feature this cycle.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows path semantics remain a recurring tax. Git Bash PWD normalization (#61619), cold UNC workspace startup (#61547), and window-bounds math against invisible resize borders (#57088) are three separate Windows-specific defects in the active set. Windows is over-represented relative to its share of the PR queue.
  • MCP servers are hostile to OpenCode's default request shaping. LaunchDarkly returning HTTP 400 on ?codemode=false (#62226) is a symptom of appending query params speculatively. The allowlist approach fixes one host, not the class of problem.
  • Resource budgeting is being spent on nothing. #62227 — evicting remote images that carry no inline payload burns the image budget without ever freeing memory. Budget accounting logic likely needs a broader audit beyond this one call site.
  • Deploy pipelines lacked a real smoke test. The 5 Nov release-page breakage that motivated #62230 shows site changes could reach cf deploy without ever booting the Worker. Build-time verification is now being added reactively.
  • TUI/desktop rendering parity drift. Mini TUI dropped configured agent colors (#62067) while the full TUI honored them; the desktop What's New popup failed on newer markdown changelogs (#61607). Both are "two code paths, one feature" failures.
  • Long-tail review latency on infrastructure PRs. #60039 and #60041 have sat open since 28 Oct while newer, smaller PRs merged — MCP networking changes are accumulating as a stack, which means the eventual review is larger and riskier than either diff alone.
  • Contributor signal on needs:compliance. #62235 shows a willingness to fork + rebrand rather than request a feature. Worth watching whether local-model defaults resurface as a legitimate config-layer proposal.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker and PR queue were unusually active. The long-running macOS CPU bug (#7730) continues to dominate engagement with 29 comments, while a bumper crop of fixes landed around Windows process handling, file encoding, tool-search schema refs, and MCP OAuth hangs. Discussion activity centered on session multiplexing and community-built tooling (Slack bot, CaseClip).

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. [#7730] High CPU usage on macOS with long sessions — 29 comments, 12 👍. The most-engaged open issue; users report CPU swinging between 50–110% and memory at 600–800MB, apparently correlated with context/session length. Still unresolved months after filing. Link
  2. [#7885] npm search not indexing new pi-packages — 19 comments. Closed, but notable: newly published pi-package keywords weren't discoverable, blocking the pi.dev/packages gallery (which mirrors npm search). Publication/discovery pipeline issue. Link
  3. [#10741] Groq Qwen3.8 27B fails with HTTP 400 (developer role) — Provider compatibility: Pi sends a developer role Groq's template rejects. Points to a broader need for provider-specific role mapping. Link
  4. [#10287] getContextUsage() overestimates massively after retryable network error — Jumped from ~42k to 330k tokens after a WebSocket failure. Corrupts context accounting and could trigger premature compaction. Link
  5. [#10846] pi-env: inject daemon process so client runs in Workers — Requests a startProcess callback to decouple Connection from node: imports, enabling Cloudflare Workers deployment. Important for portable SDK adoption. Link
  6. [#10616] pi.exec fails for .cmd commands on Windows — npm, npx, pnpm all fail via extension exec but work through the bash tool. In-progress; part of a wider Windows-support cluster. Link
  7. [#10015] bash truncation notice reports 0B for oversized last line ending in newline — Trailing newline resets the live byte counter, producing line is 0B. A fix PR (#11852) already merged. Link
  8. [#11317] Allow SDK users to customize identity preamble — Request to replace only sections.preamble while keeping default tools/rules/docs. Reflects growing SDK/embedded-agent use cases. Link
  9. [#11820] Submissions.wait leaks unhandled rejection in pi-durable 1.5.0 — Race in waiter registration inside readOnLine; failure before adoption leaks a promise rejection. Stability concern for durable sessions. Link
  10. [#11829] Let a session detach instead of dying on conversation switch — Currently /resume, /tree, and pickers tear down the running turn. This request directly motivated the parallel discussion (#11830) on juggling live conversations. Link

4. Key PR Progress

  1. [#11854] Kill whole process trees of bash commands on Windows — taskkill /T misses orphaned descendants whose parent exited; proposes a more robust tree kill. Directly addresses runaway background processes. Link
  2. [#11751] edit preserves line endings on untouched lines, diffs only around changes — Fixes CRLF churn (#8544) and avoids OOM on large-file diffs by scoping diffing to changed regions. Link
  3. [#11811] read/edit handle UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files without corruption — edit previously silently corrupted non-UTF-8 files; introduces a shared file-encoding.ts helper. Link
  4. [#11850] Follow local schema $refs in tool_search and codemode summaries — Fixes #11803; Pydantic/FastMCP servers using $defs now have discoverable tools. Merged. Link
  5. [#11857] Prompt cache warming in p2 — Anthropic's 5-minute cache was never refreshed; data shows 789 rewrites cost ~$1,430 (26% of p2 spend) over Oct 12–Nov 5. High-dollar-impact change. Link
  6. [#11855] Close remaining MCP OAuth connections on callback server close — Fixes the "stuck on Connecting…" hang after successful login by not awaiting http.Server.close() on lingering keep-alive sockets. Link
  7. [#11853] Remove all extension overlays on /reload and session switch — hideOverlay() only popped the topmost entry, leaving stacked overlays orphaned. Link
  8. [#11851 / #11848] ctx.ui.custom() overlays can report blocked program status — Extends the blocked option from inline components to overlays so agent dashboards (e.g. Herdr) see correct state. Closes #11816. Link
  9. [#11840] Add jitter to agent retries — Spreads concurrent retries, including at the delay ceiling, to avoid thundering-herd behavior in multi-subagent workflows. Link
  10. [#11696] Experimental session sync (pi-durable/sync) — Devices upload/pull session commits via an outbox + applyBatch; concurrent edits fork to a new session. Early but significant for multi-device workflows. Link

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • [#11830] How do you juggle two live conversations? — Friction when a long turn is running but you need to consult another conversation; every switch kills the session or forces a new terminal tab. Link

Q&A

  • [#11404] Official Pi code agent sandbox by Docker? — Four sbx/pi* Docker Hub images surfaced; community unsure whether these are official. 2 👍. Link

Show and tell

  • [#11860] CaseClip — save a Pi mistake as a reviewable case card — /case save captures the latest request, tool result, and correction for later review. Addresses the "agent said it worked but it 404'd" failure mode. Link
  • [#11844] pi-mom-slack — community Slack bot for pi 1.x — One pi session per Slack thread with persistent working directory via SessionManager.continueRecent; MIT licensed, npx pi-mom-slack. Link

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session lifecycle flexibility: Detach vs. teardown on conversation switch (#11829, #11830), session replication/sync across devices (#11696), and durable waits that survive restarts (#11846).
  • SDK/embedding customization: Granular prompt sections (#11317) and runtime-agnostic process injection for Workers (#10846) signal demand for embedding Pi outside the CLI.
  • Agent-state observability: Multiple issues (#11670, #11816/#11851) push toward standardizing state reporting (OSC 7501) so external dashboards can consume it.
  • Extension isolation/robustness: Requests to skip failing extensions instead of exiting (#11822) and to provide a sandboxed runtime.
  • Cross-platform correctness: Windows (process trees, .cmd exec, self-update) and Termux/Android (blocking spawnSync) parity requests keep appearing.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows support remains rough: .cmd-based tooling via pi.exec (#10616), orphaned process trees (#11854), /bin/sh spawn crashes on self-update (#11814).
  • Platform-sensitive helpers blocking in-process hosts: spawnSync in findExecutableOnPath/commandExists freezes in-process hosts like Termux/Android (#11809).
  • File fidelity: Silent corruption of non-UTF-8/UTF-16 files and line-ending churn from edit (#11751, #11811) erode trust in tool output.
  • TUI input fragility: Split kitty CSI-u sequences leaking into the composer (#11802), stale @-completion prefixes (#11823, #11825), and lost prompts when copying output (#11379).
  • State/accounting bugs: Context-usage overestimation after network errors (#10287), dropped full-output locators during compaction (#11845), and unhandled rejections in durable waits (#11820).
  • Cost visibility: Prompt-cache expiry silently multiplying Anthropic spend (#11857) highlights a class of invisible-cost bugs developers want surfaced.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-06

Generated: 2026-11-06 02:48 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report — AI CLI Developer Tools Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-06 · Tools covered: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tooling landscape is consolidating around three shared engineering problems: context economics (cache TTLs, pruning, token-frugal navigation), agent reliability signaling (subagents reporting false success, hangs, mid-stream tool-call corruption), and MCP operational maturity (OAuth lifecycle, TLS trust, schema drift across session resumes). Simultaneously, the maturity gap between tools is widening: Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI are shipping deep platform-level fixes (path traversal patches, ACP policy enforcement, retry correctness), while Claude Code's day was dominated by a trust incident rather than a feature race — a signal that privacy and safety defaults are now competitive differentiators, not just compliance checkboxes. Windows and cross-platform correctness (path semantics, process trees, libc/native addon compatibility) is an over-represented pain point across nearly every community. Meanwhile, several projects (Codex, Qwen Code) had no community signal today, and two tools (OpenCode, Codex) show PR- or release-only momentum with zero issue activity — evidence that community health is no longer uniform across the ecosystem.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (updated) PRs (updated) Discussions Release Status (24h)
Claude Code ~10 hot + honorable mentions (1 dominant: #107757, 172 👍) 1 N/A (not provided) No release
OpenAI Codex ⚠️ N/A (summary failed) ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ Unknown
Gemini CLI ~10 hot + 50 updated in window 10+ (security + correctness heavy) N/A (not provided) No release
GitHub Copilot CLI 22 updated (10 hot listed) 0 N/A (not provided) 2 releases (v1.0.106 + pre-release)
OpenCode 0 updated (reporting gap flagged) 10+ N/A (not provided) 1 release (process-daemon v0.5.0)
Pi 10 hot listed, tracker "unusually active" 10+ 1 Ideas + 1 Q&A + 2 Show-and-tell No release
Qwen Code ⚠️ N/A (summary failed) ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ N/A ⚠️ Unknown

Notes on data quality:

  • OpenAI Codex and Qwen Code summaries failed to generate — they are marked N/A, not "inactive." No inference should be drawn from their absence.
  • OpenCode reported literally zero issue updates; the digest itself flags this as "a reporting gap rather than a quiet codebase" and uses PR descriptions as a proxy. Treat as N/A for issue activity.
  • Discussions data was not provided by any source; where GitHub Discussions appear to be a primary channel (Pi, OpenCode), this should not be read as community silence.
  • Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Pi had no release in the window; Copilot CLI and OpenCode were the only shippers today.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Requirements appearing across two or more tool communities:

Direction Tools Specific Need
Context / cache economics Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Pi, Gemini CLI Longer Anthropic prompt-cache TTL (Copilot #5220), cache warming to stop 5-min expiry (Pi #11857 — 26% of p2 spend), model-judged pruning of junk tool output (Copilot #5362), token-frugal context management & "Tactful Extraction" (Gemini #19561), auto-memory overreach undermining user control (Claude #107555)
MCP reliability & lifecycle Claude Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi MCP servers killed after first turn in pre-warmed sessions (Claude #107179/#107060), tool schemas lost mid-session (Copilot #5367), stale OAuth "connected" state (Copilot #5366), OAuth hang on callback close (Pi #11855), per-server TLS trust for private CAs (OpenCode #60039/#60041)
Headless / automation & terminal-host integration Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Pi, Gemini CLI remote-control --headless (Claude #30447), OSC 7501 agent-status reporting for terminal hosts (Copilot #5320; Pi #11670/#11816), device-code sign-in without browser side effects (Copilot #5358), Workers-runtime process injection (Pi #10846)
Sandboxing + unsafe-command safety Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Copilot CLI Zero-dependency OS sandboxing to unlock native bash (Gemini #19873), stop destructive git reset --force/DB writes (Gemini #22672), pkill -f 'cat' SIGTERMing macOS apps (Claude #106029), Tab executing /clear data-loss (Claude #106074), opaque sandbox policy reporting (Copilot #5365/#5360)
Session persistence & multiplexing Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Pi Cross-surface shared session list (Claude #107611), trustworthy session resume (Copilot #5359/#5361), session detach instead of teardown on switch (Pi #11829/#11830), multi-device session sync (Pi #11696)
Subagent/skill reliability & observability Gemini CLI, Claude Code False-positive GOAL success after MAX_TURNS (Gemini #22323/#21983), under-triggered skills/subagents (Gemini #21968), settings.json overrides ignored by Browser Agent (Gemini #22267), permanent-memory overreach (Claude #107555)
Windows / cross-platform correctness OpenCode, Pi, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI Git Bash PWD normalization (OpenCode #61619), orphaned process trees (Pi #11854), .cmd exec failures (Pi #10616), multi-minute Windows turn stalls (Copilot #5356), Termux/Bionic broken 6 months (Copilot #3333), Windows dev: 0 stat fix (Gemini #30033)
Privacy & data hygiene defaults Claude Code, (Copilot implicitly) Remove email-in-User-Agent exposure entirely, not make it configurable (Claude #107757); open-sourcing the privacy mod (Claude #107768)
AST-aware / semantic code navigation Gemini CLI, Claude Code (implicitly) Three-issue EPIC on AST grep/mapping to cut misaligned reads and token noise (Gemini #22745/#22746/#22747)

Strongest cross-cutting theme: MCP is the new integration tax. Four of the six active communities independently filed MCP failures — this is now the single largest source of "works, then stops working" reports.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Feature focus

  • Claude Code — Agent autonomy depth (auto-memory, remote control, daemon mode) with the heaviest investment in behavioral correctness: memory overreach, destructive-action guards, desktop/session unification. Today's agenda was trust-centric (privacy leak, data-loss Tab bug).
  • Gemini CLI — Deep platform engineering: security hardening (path traversal), correctness of streaming/retry semantics, and a strategic bet on AST-aware navigation + native-bash sandboxing. The most architecturally forward-looking backlog.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI — Terminal-environment integration and editor handoff (/code, inline Kitty images, /settings dashboard) plus model-routing transparency (Fusion over ACP). Clearly targeting the VS Code / terminal-native enterprise developer.
  • OpenCode — Infrastructure and self-hosting: site/worker consolidation, per-server MCP networking, session ergonomics (--all). Positioning as a configurable, deployment-flexible CLI rather than a hosted-first product.
  • Pi — SDK/embedding and extensibility: Workers runtime support, custom identity preambles, session sync, extension sandboxing. The most library-like of the set — building a platform, not just a CLI.
  • Copilot CLI vs. Claude Code — Copilot leans into editor/terminal-host embedding and enterprise policy visibility; Claude leans into agent autonomy and desktop ergonomics.

Target users

Tool Primary user
Claude Code Power users running long, autonomous desktop/daemon sessions
Gemini CLI Engineering teams building on a model + agent platform; editor integrations (--acp)
Copilot CLI Enterprise VS Code / terminal developers; GitHub-centric workflows
OpenCode Self-hosters, infra-minded teams, private-network MCP users
Pi SDK integrators, extension authors, multi-device power users
Codex / Qwen Code ⚠️ Insufficient data today

Technical approach

  • Gemini CLI is the most defensive: p1 security patches, retry/discard correctness for streamed tool calls, hook policy enforcement in ACP.
  • Copilot CLI is the most release-driven: shipping directly without visible PR activity, iterating on ACP surface and auth ergonomics.
  • OpenCode is the most infrastructure-first: PTY protocol bump, build-time Worker smoke tests, deploy gating.
  • Pi is the most SDK/extension-oriented: prompt-section customization, runtime-agnostic process injection, durable session sync.
  • Claude Code is the most desktop-app-weighty alongside the strongest privacy/trust incident of the day.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Most active communities (today):

  1. Gemini CLI — Highest volume of substantive engineering (50 issues updated, 10+ PRs, multiple p1 security/correctness fixes). Momentum is high and directed.
  2. Pi — "Unusually active" tracker with 10+ PRs, a full editorial backlog (Windows process trees, file encoding, cache warming, OAuth), and organic community tooling (Slack bot, CaseClip). Strong ecosystem-building signal.
  3. GitHub Copilot CLI — 22 issue updates + 2 releases; high day-to-day friction surfaced (MCP state drift, session resume, Windows stalls) but also active shipping. Momentum high, maturity mid — reliability issues are the dominant theme.
  4. Claude Code — Dominated by a single high-engagement trust incident (172 👍) and a wave of desktop-app triage. High sentiment engagement, lower feature velocity today (no release, 1 PR).
  5. OpenCode — PR-only momentum today; infra consolidation and MCP networking. Community feedback signal is absent (0 issues) — maturity assessment is provisional.
  6. OpenAI Codex / Qwen Code — ⚠️ Insufficient data. Do not rank.

Rapidly iterating: Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI (Gemini through security/correctness patches, Copilot through releases). Maturing toward platform stability: OpenCode and Pi (protocol bumps, smoke tests, SDK surface). Trust-repair mode: Claude Code (privacy controversy) and Copilot CLI (MCP/OAuth/session-resume reliability cluster).

Maturity read: Copilot CLI shows the highest shipping cadence but the lowest reliability consistency (fragile MCP/OAuth/session state). Gemini CLI shows the strongest fix discipline but a backlog of false-positive success-signal bugs that erode automation trust. Neither Codex nor Qwen Code can be assessed today due to data gaps.

6. Trend Signals

  1. MCP operational maturity is the top reliability frontier. Across Claude Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Pi, the recurring failure pattern is state drift: connection state, tool registry, and auth tokens fall out of sync with no automatic reconciliation. Expect "MCP lifecycle management" (health checks, auto-restart, schema reconciliation) to become a first-class feature category. Action for developers: budget engineering time for MCP supervision; do not assume "connected" means "usable."

  2. Context economics is becoming a budget line item. Pi quantified Anthropic cache expiry at ~$1,430 / 26% of p2 spend in three weeks; Copilot is requesting longer cache TTLs and model-judged pruning; Gemini is designing AST tools to cut token noise. Action: treat prompt-cache configuration and context pruning as cost-engineering, not just UX.

  3. False-positive agent success is an emerging trust crisis. Gemini's subagents report GOAL/success after hitting MAX_TURNS or failing on Wayland; Claude's auto-memory promotes one-off corrections to permanent rules. Action: build external verification (tests, diffs, exit codes) around agent claims — do not trust the agent's own status field.

  4. Automation and headless operation are demanded across the board. remote-control --headless, Workers runtime support, OSC 7501 status reporting, device-code sign-in, and multi-device session sync all point the same direction: AI CLIs are becoming background services, not interactive toys. Action: design for TTY-free, daemonized, embeddable operation now.

  5. Windows and cross-platform correctness is a persistent tax. Six of the seven tools surfaced Windows-specific defects (path semantics, process trees, .cmd exec, multi-minute stalls, glibc/Bionic incompatibility). Action: if your team is Windows-heavy, weight platform-fix velocity heavily in tool selection — it lags across the board.

  6. Privacy and safety defaults are now competitive. The Claude Code User-Agent/email leak (172 👍, demand for removal not configurability) and the open-sourcing of the privacy mod show users treating data hygiene as non-negotiable. Action: audit what your CLI sends at the network boundary (headers, telemetry, query params) — this is now a procurement criterion.

  7. Sandboxing + native-bash is a deliberate design tension. Gemini's zero-dependency sandboxing proposal aims to unlock grep/sed/awk chaining without losing security. Action: watch this space — the winning approach to "agentic bash" will likely define the next generation of tool execution.

  8. Editor/terminal-host embedding is the next integration layer. ACP Fusion advertisement, /code handoff, OSC status protocols, and inline image rendering signal that CLIs are being absorbed into editors and terminal multiplexers rather than used standalone. Action: prioritize ACP/status-protocol support if you build editor or terminal tooling.

Methodology note: This report is synthesized from provided community digests only. OpenAI Codex and Qwen Code are marked N/A due to summary generation failure and are excluded from momentum rankings rather than treated as inactive. Issue/PR counts reflect the reporting window and are not normalized across repos.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Data source: github.com/anthropics/skills · Snapshot date: 2026-11-06

Method note: PR comment counts are unavailable in this dataset (Comments: undefined for all 50 PRs). Rankings below are therefore inferred from contemporaneity of updates, cross-linked issues, recurring contributors, and per-Skill PR clusters — not raw comment volume. Issue rankings use actual comment/👍 counts.

1. Top Skills Ranking (by attention signal)

# Skill / PR What it does Discussion highlights Status
1 skill-creator — #1298, #1997, #1681 Meta-skill for authoring, packaging, and evaluating Skills Largest PR cluster; three independent fixes (trigger-eval isolation + Windows pipes, YAML frontmatter scalar parsing, direct package_skill.py execution). Ties into issue #202 ("should be updated to best practice") — authoring tooling is the ecosystem's weakest link All OPEN
2 mcp-builder — #1742 Generates and evaluates MCP servers from specs Breaking rename in mcp>=2.0.0 (streamablehttp_client → streamable_http_client), plus custom headers now require create_mcp_http_client. Directly paired with issue #1390 (eval harness scores 0/N) — the skill's runtime and harness both need repair OPEN (cf. #1668)
3 webapp-testing — #1980, #1976 Browser-driven testing and element discovery Security-first framing: removal of shell=True (CWE-78 command injection) in with_server.py, plus correctness fix for textarea/select mislabeled as text Both OPEN
4 docx — #1792, #1734 Word document manipulation (revisions, comments) Silent-failure pattern dominates: LibreOffice timeout reported as success without verifying w:ins/w:del removal; request to detect orphaned comments. Mirrors issue #2018 (invalid XML on merge) — docx is the most bug-reported bundled skill Both OPEN
5 xlsx — #2019 Spreadsheet recalculation and external-link risk analysis Most recently updated substantive PR; fixes false negatives in external_links_at_risk for worksheet-scoped defined names and aliases. Fixes #2013 OPEN
6 pyxel — #525 Retro game development in Python Longest-lived high-visibility skill proposal (opened 2026-03-05, still active 2026-11-01). Scope covers headless input-driven runs, frame inspection, and evidence-based verification — an unusually rigorous test story OPEN
7 New Skill submissions — #1245, #1703, #1771, #1615 Notion spec→implementation + resume auditor; Markdown→MP4 video; smart-contract audit on TON; SCNet HPC/Slurm ops Net-new domain coverage: product ops, media generation, Web3, and scientific compute. None merged All OPEN
8 document-typography — #514 Typographic QC for generated docs (orphans, widows, numbering) Notable framing: "affects every document Claude generates, users rarely ask for it" — a proactive-quality skill archetype. Low activity since March OPEN

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

① Security, trust boundaries, and supply chain — the single loudest thread

  • #492 "Community skills distributed under anthropic/ namespace enable trust boundary abuse" — 46 comments, by far the most-discussed issue in the repo. Namespace impersonation lets community skills inherit official trust.
  • #1394 XSS in skill-creator's eval-viewer (innerHTML + non-attribute-safe escapeHtml).
  • #1980 command-injection class in webapp-testing.

② Skill evaluation and triggering is unreliable — the loudest technical complaint

  • #556 run_eval.py reports 0% trigger rate across all queries (13 comments, 7 👍).
  • #1390 mcp-builder evaluation scores 0/N against every real MCP server (TextContent not JSON-serializable, errors swallowed).
  • #1298 / #1997 attempt fixes in skill-creator itself. → Demand: a trustworthy, self-hosted regression harness for Skills.

  3. #5367 — Agent regularly loses MCP tool schemas A "every single day" report: returning to a session silently loses access to certain MCP tools, recoverable only via /compact. High-severity, low-workaround — this is the kind of state bug that erodes trust in long sessions.

  4. #5359 — Resumed session 400: "Tool reference not found in available tools" When an MCP server's tool set changes between launches, every request in the resumed session hard-fails with a 400. Pairs with #5367 into a coherent "MCP + session resume" reliability cluster.

  7. #5354 — ACP does not advertise Copilot Fusion or its tier configuration · 👍 2 Fusion works interactively but ACP reports the model as "Auto" with no tier selector, blocking clients like T3 Code. Directly tied to today's release work.

  • Context economics — Requests cluster around making the context window cheaper and cleaner: longer Claude prompt cache TTL (#5220), model-judged pruning of junk tool output (#5362), and implicit reliance on /compact as the only recovery path (#5367).
  • Terminal-host integration surface — Status protocols (OSC 7501), foreground-session change hooks (#5279), and inline image rendering all point to Copilot CLI being embedded in richer terminal environments rather than used standalone.
  • Model routing transparency — Fusion and tier configuration being invisible over ACP (#5354) and model/mode mismatches in session/new (#5363) suggest users want the routing layer to be inspectable and settable programmatically.

The common thread is that MCP connection state and the model's tool registry fall out of sync with no automatic reconciliation.
  2. OAuth token lifecycle is fragile. Both the Entra/remote-MCP path (#5366) and the ACP interactive path (#5350, #5229) show refresh-token grants not being attempted, or the code→token exchange not running at all. Only a server restart recovers.

  5. Sandbox policy is opaque. With duplicate read-write rules appearing unexplained in sandbox.decision (#5365) and enterprise-managed policies failing during option updates (#5360), admins lack the observability needed to debug policy in managed environments.

Also worth a glance: #62235 [CLOSED, needs:compliance] — a full rebrand of the CLI/app/config paths to "harpcode" with a built-in local llama.cpp provider layer and default MCP servers; closed rather than reviewed, reinforcing that config-path and branding changes to a fork are out of scope upstream. #62067 [CLOSED] restored configured agent colors in Mini TUI; #61607 [OPEN] fixes the What's New popup for markdown-style Highlights changelogs; #57088 [OPEN] restores edge-snapped window bounds that resolveWindowState drops when Windows reports invisible resize borders.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Caveat: with zero issue and zero discussion activity in the window, these directions are inferred from PR intent and the issues those PRs cite — not from request volume.

  • Enterprise/private networking for MCP. Two stacked PRs (#60039, #60041) plus an umbrella issue (#40111) and four historical cross-references point squarely at self-signed certs and private CAs. Remote MCP adoption is being gated by TLS trust ergonomics, not by tooling capability.
  • Per-server MCP configurability in general. The TLS block and the host-specific rejectsUnknownQuery allowlist (#62226) both follow the same shape: move behavior from global heuristics to per-server config.
  • Multi-project session ergonomics. session list --all (#60895) is a request to stop assuming cwd == the only project a developer works in.
  • Local-model / offline-first defaults. The harpcode fork PR (#62235) proposed a built-in lowest-priority llama.cpp provider layer. Even though it was closed, it is the clearest recent artifact of demand for a zero-config local inference path.
  • Docs/site consolidation. #62209 → #62229 signals an internal direction (SolidStart + a single services/site worker) that will shape contributor workflow more than any user-facing feature this cycle.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows path semantics remain a recurring tax. Git Bash PWD normalization (#61619), cold UNC workspace startup (#61547), and window-bounds math against invisible resize borders (#57088) are three separate Windows-specific defects in the active set. Windows is over-represented relative to its share of the PR queue.
  • MCP servers are hostile to OpenCode's default request shaping. LaunchDarkly returning HTTP 400 on ?codemode=false (#62226) is a symptom of appending query params speculatively. The allowlist approach fixes one host, not the class of problem.
  • Resource budgeting is being spent on nothing. #62227 — evicting remote images that carry no inline payload burns the image budget without ever freeing memory. Budget accounting logic likely needs a broader audit beyond this one call site.
  • Deploy pipelines lacked a real smoke test. The 5 Nov release-page breakage that motivated #62230 shows site changes could reach cf deploy without ever booting the Worker. Build-time verification is now being added reactively.
  • TUI/desktop rendering parity drift. Mini TUI dropped configured agent colors (#62067) while the full TUI honored them; the desktop What's New popup failed on newer markdown changelogs (#61607). Both are "two code paths, one feature" failures.
  • Long-tail review latency on infrastructure PRs. #60039 and #60041 have sat open since 28 Oct while newer, smaller PRs merged — MCP networking changes are accumulating as a stack, which means the eventual review is larger and riskier than either diff alone.
  • Contributor signal on needs:compliance. #62235 shows a willingness to fork + rebrand rather than request a feature. Worth watching whether local-model defaults resurface as a legitimate config-layer proposal.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker and PR queue were unusually active. The long-running macOS CPU bug (#7730) continues to dominate engagement with 29 comments, while a bumper crop of fixes landed around Windows process handling, file encoding, tool-search schema refs, and MCP OAuth hangs. Discussion activity centered on session multiplexing and community-built tooling (Slack bot, CaseClip).

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. [#7730] High CPU usage on macOS with long sessions — 29 comments, 12 👍. The most-engaged open issue; users report CPU swinging between 50–110% and memory at 600–800MB, apparently correlated with context/session length. Still unresolved months after filing. Link
  2. [#7885] npm search not indexing new pi-packages — 19 comments. Closed, but notable: newly published pi-package keywords weren't discoverable, blocking the pi.dev/packages gallery (which mirrors npm search). Publication/discovery pipeline issue. Link
  3. [#10741] Groq Qwen3.8 27B fails with HTTP 400 (developer role) — Provider compatibility: Pi sends a developer role Groq's template rejects. Points to a broader need for provider-specific role mapping. Link
  4. [#10287] getContextUsage() overestimates massively after retryable network error — Jumped from ~42k to 330k tokens after a WebSocket failure. Corrupts context accounting and could trigger premature compaction. Link
  5. [#10846] pi-env: inject daemon process so client runs in Workers — Requests a startProcess callback to decouple Connection from node: imports, enabling Cloudflare Workers deployment. Important for portable SDK adoption. Link
  6. [#10616] pi.exec fails for .cmd commands on Windows — npm, npx, pnpm all fail via extension exec but work through the bash tool. In-progress; part of a wider Windows-support cluster. Link
  7. [#10015] bash truncation notice reports 0B for oversized last line ending in newline — Trailing newline resets the live byte counter, producing line is 0B. A fix PR (#11852) already merged. Link
  8. [#11317] Allow SDK users to customize identity preamble — Request to replace only sections.preamble while keeping default tools/rules/docs. Reflects growing SDK/embedded-agent use cases. Link
  9. [#11820] Submissions.wait leaks unhandled rejection in pi-durable 1.5.0 — Race in waiter registration inside readOnLine; failure before adoption leaks a promise rejection. Stability concern for durable sessions. Link
  10. [#11829] Let a session detach instead of dying on conversation switch — Currently /resume, /tree, and pickers tear down the running turn. This request directly motivated the parallel discussion (#11830) on juggling live conversations. Link

4. Key PR Progress

  1. [#11854] Kill whole process trees of bash commands on Windows — taskkill /T misses orphaned descendants whose parent exited; proposes a more robust tree kill. Directly addresses runaway background processes. Link
  2. [#11751] edit preserves line endings on untouched lines, diffs only around changes — Fixes CRLF churn (#8544) and avoids OOM on large-file diffs by scoping diffing to changed regions. Link
  3. [#11811] read/edit handle UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files without corruption — edit previously silently corrupted non-UTF-8 files; introduces a shared file-encoding.ts helper. Link
  4. [#11850] Follow local schema $refs in tool_search and codemode summaries — Fixes #11803; Pydantic/FastMCP servers using $defs now have discoverable tools. Merged. Link
  5. [#11857] Prompt cache warming in p2 — Anthropic's 5-minute cache was never refreshed; data shows 789 rewrites cost ~$1,430 (26% of p2 spend) over Oct 12–Nov 5. High-dollar-impact change. Link
  6. [#11855] Close remaining MCP OAuth connections on callback server close — Fixes the "stuck on Connecting…" hang after successful login by not awaiting http.Server.close() on lingering keep-alive sockets. Link
  7. [#11853] Remove all extension overlays on /reload and session switch — hideOverlay() only popped the topmost entry, leaving stacked overlays orphaned. Link
  8. [#11851 / #11848] ctx.ui.custom() overlays can report blocked program status — Extends the blocked option from inline components to overlays so agent dashboards (e.g. Herdr) see correct state. Closes #11816. Link
  9. [#11840] Add jitter to agent retries — Spreads concurrent retries, including at the delay ceiling, to avoid thundering-herd behavior in multi-subagent workflows. Link
  10. [#11696] Experimental session sync (pi-durable/sync) — Devices upload/pull session commits via an outbox + applyBatch; concurrent edits fork to a new session. Early but significant for multi-device workflows. Link

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • [#11830] How do you juggle two live conversations? — Friction when a long turn is running but you need to consult another conversation; every switch kills the session or forces a new terminal tab. Link

Q&A

  • [#11404] Official Pi code agent sandbox by Docker? — Four sbx/pi* Docker Hub images surfaced; community unsure whether these are official. 2 👍. Link

Show and tell

  • [#11860] CaseClip — save a Pi mistake as a reviewable case card — /case save captures the latest request, tool result, and correction for later review. Addresses the "agent said it worked but it 404'd" failure mode. Link
  • [#11844] pi-mom-slack — community Slack bot for pi 1.x — One pi session per Slack thread with persistent working directory via SessionManager.continueRecent; MIT licensed, npx pi-mom-slack. Link

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session lifecycle flexibility: Detach vs. teardown on conversation switch (#11829, #11830), session replication/sync across devices (#11696), and durable waits that survive restarts (#11846).
  • SDK/embedding customization: Granular prompt sections (#11317) and runtime-agnostic process injection for Workers (#10846) signal demand for embedding Pi outside the CLI.
  • Agent-state observability: Multiple issues (#11670, #11816/#11851) push toward standardizing state reporting (OSC 7501) so external dashboards can consume it.
  • Extension isolation/robustness: Requests to skip failing extensions instead of exiting (#11822) and to provide a sandboxed runtime.
  • Cross-platform correctness: Windows (process trees, .cmd exec, self-update) and Termux/Android (blocking spawnSync) parity requests keep appearing.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows support remains rough: .cmd-based tooling via pi.exec (#10616), orphaned process trees (#11854), /bin/sh spawn crashes on self-update (#11814).
  • Platform-sensitive helpers blocking in-process hosts: spawnSync in findExecutableOnPath/commandExists freezes in-process hosts like Termux/Android (#11809).
  • File fidelity: Silent corruption of non-UTF-8/UTF-16 files and line-ending churn from edit (#11751, #11811) erode trust in tool output.
  • TUI input fragility: Split kitty CSI-u sequences leaking into the composer (#11802), stale @-completion prefixes (#11823, #11825), and lost prompts when copying output (#11379).
  • State/accounting bugs: Context-usage overestimation after network errors (#10287), dropped full-output locators during compaction (#11845), and unhandled rejections in durable waits (#11820).
  • Cost visibility: Prompt-cache expiry silently multiplying Anthropic spend (#11857) highlights a class of invisible-cost bugs developers want surfaced.
