item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-11-06

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-11-06 02:48 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity, high-pressure operating state: 500 issues and 500 PRs were touched in the last 24h, with 186 PRs merged/closed against 314 still open and 253 of 500 updated issues closed. Activity is dominated by maintainer-driven cleanup (steipete, vincentkoc, obviyus), security-adjacent work around access-policy and staged-commit authority, and a stream of CI/test hardening PRs. However, the issue tracker shows a persistent cluster of P0/P1 crash-loop and data-loss regressions tracking back to the 2026.9.x–2026.10.x line, several with 15–75 comments and no merged fix. One release shipped (v2026.11.1), but it is a small hardening patch rather than a regression-closing update. Overall: very active, but stability debt on long-lived regressions is accumulating and needs maintainer triage.

2. Releases

v2026.11.1 — small, safety-focused patch:

  • Safer Mac settings: failed config saves no longer overwrite secrets; disabling Tailscale exposure preserves Gateway authentication (#187734, #187664; fixes #187600, #187597; thanks @anmol0b).
  • More reliable channel replies: Telegram, Discord, and webhook delivery robustness improvements (release note truncated in source data — full changelog should be verified on the release page).

No breaking changes or migration notes are stated in the provided excerpt. Notably, none of the top P0 regressions below are fixed in this release (e.g., #160959, #166017, #191847), and #141474's fix is explicitly noted as shipping in v2026.11.5-beta.1, not stable v2026.11.1.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today show steady incremental hardening rather than headline features:

  • MCP App content durability: #193812 preserves saved MCP App display content after view expiry via session-owned custom-entry lane.
  • Recovery model selection: #193719 keeps recovery models selectable across providers when a personal-account pin is missing (closes #193770).
  • Memory-wiki correctness: #193469 (closed) stops wiki lint treating commented/escaped [[wikilinks]] as live links.
  • UI performance: #193479 (closed) reduces long-session streaming onset work by retaining prepared history in the bounded projection cache.
  • CI/test hygiene: #193887 (closed) retires a redundant Swift portability adapter; #193870, #193904 rework CI admission for historical runs and PostgreSQL conformance.
  • QA/test reliability: #193908 awaits Workshop enable before reload.

Feature work advancing in open PRs: access-policy revision publishing (#182383), staged PostgreSQL authority at physical commit (#193842), OpenClaw ID Gateway membership authority behind Labs flag (#192335), and an opt-in "portable research" tool (#173964).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Theme
#160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (P0) 75 Plugin capture regression from 2026.9.6 stalls the event loop
#177656 — Native host exec shared-state integrity-admission error (P1) 29 Authority/admission model breaking native exec
#170956 — Windows slow startup, unclean shutdown, schtasks EPERM (P0) 29 Windows managed-service reliability
#178359 — doctor --fix idles 15+ min (P1) 25 Doctor/repair-path hangs
#166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable 24 SQLite recovery leaves agents permanently UNAVAILABLE
#191944 — gateway stop fails: "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" (P2) 19 Process-census/service-inspection reliability
#40001 — write tool lacks append mode; cron destroys shared files (P0) 17 Silent data loss in isolated sessions

Underlying need: the community is converging on a single meta-theme — the shared-state/integrity-admission and service-child lifecycle model introduced around 2026.9.x is producing a long tail of hangs, permanent-unavailable states, and recovery dead-ends. Users are not asking for features; they are asking for deterministic recovery after crashes and restarts.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / crash-loop & data-loss (no fix PR confirmed merged):

  • #160959 — Gateway event-loop block for minutes on large plugin capture (75 comments, diamond-lobster rating). Highest-impact open issue.
  • #166017 — mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs default not applied; MCP runtimes never evicted, spawn broker hits 256-child cap, all exec/read/MCP start fails. (linked PR open.)
  • #170956 — Windows restart/update unreliability (schtasks permission + unclean plugin shutdown).
  • #40001 — write overwrites instead of appending; isolated cron causes silent shared-file data loss.
  • #161921 — post-state-migrated-no-rollback deadlock between doctor --fix and plugins update.
  • #70903 — persistent provider cooldown blocks users for hours after billing recovery.
  • #142821 — default-on transcript redaction poisons replayed agent context (security + data-loss).
  • #158912 — MEMORY.md no longer injected at bootstrap on 2026.9.6 (docs mismatch, session-state/security).

P1 regressions:

  • #191847 — 2026.10.10: 512 MB SQLite worker OOM kills every turn in large sessions ("admission is closed").
  • #155563 — service-child relay/anchor and MCP groups retained after successful turns (2026.9.5 regression).
  • #134993 — Gateway pegs one CPU core in filesystem discovery with large skill/agent fleets.
  • #162637 — native Codex completion handoff fails with SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED.
  • #182647 — cloud-worker turns fail with "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" (labeled queueable-fix).
  • #118793 — Claude CLI session-limit error bypasses model fallback chain.

Exceptionally long-lived: #40001 (#40001) has been open since 2026-03-08 — ~8 months — despite being P0 data-loss. #70903 since 2026-04-24.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Progress streaming for Feishu/Lark (#131457) — parity with Slack/Discord/Telegram/Matrix/Mattermost/Teams; likely candidate once channel-delivery hardening in v2026.11.1 settles.
  • Append mode for write tool (#40001) — arguably a bug fix, but explicitly a missing capability; high candidate for near-term.
  • --prompt-file for openclaw infer model run (#140244) — small, low-risk automation ergonomics.
  • Disable hosted plugin catalog feed (#164620) — privacy/air-gap demand.
  • Control UI: browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after /new (#158800) — UX continuity.
  • Failure-only notifyOnExit mode (#141973, closed stale) — noise reduction.
  • Session tool-set explainer (PR #192713, closes #192712) — strong debuggability signal; likely to land soon.
  • First-run provider→chat flow (PR #193892) — onboarding friction fix.

Prediction for v2026.11.x: expect the #141474 recovery fix (already in v2026.11.5-beta.1) to reach stable, plus CI/authority-model hardening and the Control UI onboarding/model-catalog fixes. Feishu streaming and write append mode are less certain for the immediate next tag.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Recovery is not trustworthy. Multiple users report that after a crash, restart, or update, the system lands in a state that requires the other subsystem to fix it first (doctor ↔ plugins update deadlock, permanent UNAVAILABLE agents, "admission is closed"). This is the dominant emotional theme in high-comment threads.
  • Windows is a second-class platform. schtasks EPERM, slow startup, unclean shutdown, and the fact that Windows CI covers only ~0.6% of test files (#126874, closed stale) are repeatedly cited.
  • Silent data loss is the most feared failure mode — cron overwriting shared memory files, transcript redaction propagating into commands/files/replies, and stale async results replaying into the wrong Discord channel (#135117).
  • Cost/caching surprises — Anthropic prompt cache stuck at ~46k prefix (#140129), cache never reused (#182891) — direct billing anxiety.

Satisfaction signals: users are actively filing highly detailed, reproducible reports with version pins and logs; several explicitly credit the team's responsiveness (e.g., #187468 confirmed update-failure report). The maintainers' clawsweeper triage labels (diamond lobster / gold shrimp ratings) show a maturing triage process that contributors respect.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention — high severity, low or stalled momentum:

  1. #40001 — P0 data-loss, open since 2026-03-08, no fix PR, needs product decision. Most overdue P0.
  2. #70903 — persistent provider cooldown blocks paying users post-billing-recovery; open since 2026-04-24, stale.
  3. #160959 — highest-comment P0 (75), needs maintainer review, no fix PR.
  4. #142821 — redaction poisoning agent context; security review requested, linked PR open since Sept.
  5. #134993 — CPU pegging with large fleets; open since 2026-09-01.
  6. #126874 — Windows CI coverage gap; closed stale but the underlying risk (unverified Windows path) remains and correlates with #170956.
  7. Stale-but-unresolved product decisions: #150743 (QQ channel long-term support after Tencent handoff stalled), #164620 (disable hosted catalog feed), #124306 (exec approval card doesn't flag mount-point targets before rm -rf — a safety gap worth prioritizing).
  8. PR risk: #173964 (portable research, XL, security-boundary, "needs proof") and #192335 (OpenClaw ID membership authority) are large security-boundary changes that need explicit review bandwidth; #191509 is an accidental empty placeholder that should be closed.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw, snapshot 2026-11-06. Comment/reaction counts and issue states are as reported in the provided dataset.

横向生态对比

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Agent / Assistant OSS Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-06 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, IronClaw Method note: Figures are single-day (24h) community digests. OpenClaw's "500/500" counts appear to be a dataset cap and should be read as ≥500, not a true ceiling. Counts measure items touched, not net-new work.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The ecosystem is converging from "chatbot with tools" to durable, multi-surface agent runtimes, and the current fault line is no longer model capability but session authority, migration integrity, and plugin isolation. Four of the five projects are simultaneously rebuilding their state layer — append-only session history, deterministic replay, and gateway-mediated session ownership appear independently in OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw. Release posture splits cleanly: Hermes is shipping from a large release train, OpenClaw is patching a mature but debt-laden core, and QwenPaw/ZeroClaw are pre-release, accumulating review-queue backlogs. The strongest cross-project user signal is not feature demand but trust in recovery and failure reporting — silent data loss and "success that did nothing" outrank missing features in every tracker.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Merge/Close Throughput Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw ~500 touched / 253 closed ~500 touched / 314 open 186 merged/closed (~37%) v2026.11.1 — small hardening patch; top P0s unfixed 6.4 / 10
Hermes Agent 50 (47 open / 3 closed) 50 (44 open / 6 merged) 6 merged (~12%) v0.23.0 "The Hearth" shipped Nov 5 (~1,950 PRs, 666 contributors) 8.0 / 10
QwenPaw 14 32 (20 open / 12 closed) ~12 closed/merged (~38%) None; public 2.2.2.post1 vs. beta 2.3.0b3 skew 5.5 / 10
ZeroClaw 30 (25 open / 5 closed) 50 (48 open / 2 merged) 2 merged (~4%) None; v0.9.0 staged but blocked 5.9 / 10
IronClaw 0 0 — None n/a (dormant)

Scoring rubric (composite, 0–10): activity/throughput 25% · release cadence 20% · stability & regression debt 35% · review throughput/maturity 20%. Scores are analyst judgment, not vendor metrics.

Reading the table: OpenClaw operates at roughly 10× the daily item volume of any peer. Hermes has the healthiest ratio (one large, coherent release with spin-out tracking issues). ZeroClaw's 2-of-50 merge rate is not low contribution — it is a review bottleneck with substantial PRs stacked behind do-not-merge/status:blocked dependencies (#12244 → #11964/#12232; #11126 → #10412).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers

  • Breadth of integration surface — the only project in the set with mature parity across Feishu/Lark, QQ, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Mattermost, Teams, and webhooks, plus MCP app content durability and a Control UI.
  • Operational depth — doctor --fix, managed Windows services (schtasks), macOS Tailscale/Gateway auth handling, process-census service inspection. Peers are still building desktop/serve entry points; OpenClaw already has repair tooling (that occasionally deadlocks).
  • Triage maturity — clawsweeper severity ratings (diamond lobster / gold shrimp) and reproducible, version-pinned reports. This is the most institutionally mature tracker in the set.

Technical approach differences

  • Monolithic gateway with an integrity-admission / shared-state authority model introduced around 2026.9.x. Where Hermes is consolidating into a unified gateway, OpenClaw is absorbing the cost of having done so earlier — the entire P0 cluster (#160959 event-loop stalls, #177656 admission errors, #166634 permanent UNAVAILABLE, #161921 migration deadlock) is downstream of this design.
  • Staged PostgreSQL commit authority (#193842) and access-policy revision publishing (#182383) show OpenClaw pushing further into transactional session authority than any peer.

Community size comparison

  • OpenClaw's top thread carries 75 comments; Hermes' 227; ZeroClaw's 16; QwenPaw's 8. OpenClaw dominates volume of distinct reporters, while Hermes dominates per-thread consensus-building.
  • Decisive gap: ~500 items/day vs. 30–50 for peers. OpenClaw is the de facto reference implementation by traffic, but that scale is precisely what exposes its stability debt — #40001 (P0 data loss) has been open since 2026-03-08, ~8 months, with no fix PR.

Positioning verdict: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's substrate and cautionary tale — highest capability and adoption, lowest marginal stability per shipped feature. Its competitive risk is not a feature gap but trust erosion on recovery paths while Hermes closes the integration gap at a healthier ratio.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific Needs Observed
Durable, append-only session state + deterministic replay All four active OpenClaw: session-owned custom-entry lanes (#193812), SQLite recovery dead-ends (#166634). Hermes: unified-gateway session authority (#145171), cron state → cron/runtime.db (#75833). QwenPaw: append-only per-session SQLite + paginated history + turn forks (#8532). ZeroClaw

同赛道项目详细报告

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

Date: 2026-11-06 Repository: github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Today's Overview

Hermes Agent shipped v0.23.0 "The Hearth Release" on November 5, 2026 — a massive cycle since v0.22.0 (~10,080 commits, ~1,950 merged PRs, ~850 issues closed, 666 contributors). Activity remains extremely high: 50 issues updated in 24h (47 open/active, 3 closed) and 50 PRs updated (44 open, 6 merged/closed), consistent with a large-scale, high-velocity open-source project in active maintenance. The dominant theme of ongoing work is stabilization of the unified gateway (#106742), which merged Oct 14 and continues to generate follow-up defects in session state, Desktop connection, and profile scoping. Community engagement is substantive — the top tracking issues carry 200+ and 40+ comments respectively — suggesting a mature user base running multi-profile, multi-surface deployments. Overall project health looks strong on throughput, with moderate risk in post-merge regressions around sessions and gateway routing.

2. Releases

v0.23.0 — "The Hearth Release" (released 2026-11-05)

Scope since v0.22.0:

  • ~10,080 commits · ~1,950 merged PRs
  • ~8,720 files changed (~725,200 insertions, ~201,400 deletions)
  • ~850 issues closed · 666 contributors

Notes:

  • The release framing ("Hermes kept the threshold…") suggests a gateway/entry-point consolidation theme, consistent with the unified gateway work landing in this cycle.
  • Breaking changes / migration notes: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt. Given the unified-gateway rollout (#106742), users with standalone hermes serve, Desktop URL/Cloud/SSH modes, and standalone profiles should expect migration behavior changes — see the migration command (hermes gateway migrate --multiplex) referenced in #149682. Treat this release as a protocol/plumbing transition release; verify Desktop remote connections and Group Chats after upgrade.
  • Tracked known post-release issues include profile-scoped auth (PR #149813) and local image upload regressions on Desktop v0.23.0 (#149770).

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed today (6 PRs / 3 issues), highlights via closed items and fix PRs in flight:

  • #134889 [CLOSED] — Tracking issue for unified gateway post-merge fixes (227 comments). Closure signals the primary stabilization wave for one-gateway-per-local-session is complete; remaining work has been spun out.
  • #139818 [CLOSED] — Remote-backend Desktop sessions unresumable (session.resume → not_found) is resolved; a notable Desktop remote-backend reliability win.
  • #149787 [CLOSED] — Desktop Scheduled view: script-only (no_agent) run rows now openable with real output preview.
  • PR #137942 [CLOSED] — Bot-mode turn subprocess now bounded by the 600s per-attempt deadline (was an unbounded subprocess.run holding the per-profile delivery lock). Prevents wedged-child deadlocks.
  • Follow-on work formalized: #143547 (open, 50 comments) now carries remaining unified-gateway problems; #145171 tracks the entry-point cutover of serve, remote Desktop, and web onto gateway session authority.

Feature work advancing (open PRs):

  • #149630 — /undo now cross-references /rollback for file restoration (checkpoint awareness).
  • #149786 / #149746 — CI cost reduction (same-runner job merging) and npm → pnpm 12.15.0 workspace migration.
  • #75833 — Cron scheduler state moved out of jobs.json into per-profile cron/runtime.db (long-running infra refactor).

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #134889 — Unified gateway post-merge tracking (CLOSED) 227 The defining workstream of this release cycle; massive coordination surface.
2 #143547 — Remaining unified-gateway problems 50 Continuation issue; still active the same day #134889 closed.
3 #139818 — Remote desktop session resume fails 41 (👍3) High user impact, now closed.
4 #97681 — Cross-gateway bot collaboration 40 (👍4) Strongest feature appetite signal: multi-agent, cross-machine, federated bots.
5 #105758 — Lifecycle guard false-positive on Node CLIs 25 Developer-workflow friction; scanner heuristics too broad.

Underlying needs: Users are running multi-profile, multi-surface setups (CLI + TUI + Desktop + messaging bots + cron) and want them to behave as one coherent system. The unified gateway pain is the cost of that consolidation. Separately, federation/collaboration between personal agents (#97681) is the clearest "next platform" demand.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / High severity (recent, tracked):

  • #149682 — Group Chats imported via hermes gateway migrate --multiplex fail first turn for every member with runtime_draining (room session title collides with standalone-era Group: <room> row). Migration-day blocker; no linked fix PR yet in provided data.
  • #149784 — Desktop sessions become permanently unrecoverable (admission_conflict) after 90-day pruning; routing entries never refreshed, restore won't self-heal. Data-availability risk; no fix PR shown.
  • #148742 — Legacy state.db without INTEGER PRIMARY KEY id accumulates NULL-id rows post-upgrade → compression fails with int(None), attempts_exhausted. Upgrade-path corruption risk; no fix PR shown.

P1 / P2 (open):

  • #149770 — Desktop local image uploads fail ("session not found") when a legacy remote profile overrides the negotiated wire. Regression in v0.23.0.
  • #148531 — owner-backfill 409s "Exclusive maintenance refused" on every desktop boot in split topology.
  • #147387 — Auth-gated dashboard rejects Desktop token-mode credentials (WebSocket upgrade always rejected).
  • #148389 — Kanban worker hangs at startup on Windows (never issues model request, zero TCP connections).
  • #132645 — Windows: hermes update leaves host gateway down when a named profile is sticky.
  • #135171 — macOS: update SIGTERMs launchd wrapper/helper processes as "manual gateways"; warning never clears.
  • #110374 (👍16, highest-reaction bug) — Slack status indicator silently broken with slack-sdk >= 3.44 (agents.sessions.setStatus rejects free-text/empty).
  • #148457 — browser.executable_path to a sandbox-capable Chromium still launched with --no-sandbox on AppArmor-userns hosts (security-relevant).

Fix PRs in flight:

  • #137562 — Desktop clarify-lock expiry.
  • #148265 — Matrix prose sanitizer deleting text resembling attributes.
  • #149802 — /stop-cancelled delegation incorrectly waking the parent session.
  • #149813 — Remote Config Nous token resolved under wrong (production) secret scope.
  • #117769 — Delayed process notifications conflicting with newer user instructions.

Pattern: Post-unified-gateway, the split-topology / legacy-DB / profile-scoping seams are the dominant defect class. Migration from standalone backends is the highest-risk path right now.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #97681 (40 comments, 👍4) — Bots collaborate across gateways (across machines now, across owners next). Strong candidate for the next platform milestone.
  • #102269 — Bot Marketplace: discover/review/install "bot packs" via profiles + distribution.yaml. Natural commercialization/ecosystem bet.
  • #98004 — Per-group auto-continue budget for Bot Mode rooms (item 4 of #89545) — safety-cap tuning.
  • #96906 — Delegation closeout: hold one terminal response until task-scoped background work finishes (default-off, awaiting maintainer decision; prior PR deferred for gateway reliability).
  • #145171 — Entry-point cutover of serve/remote Desktop/web onto gateway authority (security-tagged tracking issue).
  • Plugin ecosystem is visibly growing: new catalog submissions for PrintWatch (3D printers, LAN mode) #149803, qbo-ops (QuickBooks Online) #149801, and proofops (completion-claim verification) #149625.

Prediction for next release (v0.24.x): entry-point cutover completion, remote/Cloud/SSH Desktop onto gateway sessions, cross-gateway bot messaging foundation, and continued migration hardening (Group Chat imports, legacy state.db). Bot Marketplace likely remains a larger future milestone.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Migration/upgrade fragility dominates: legacy state.db corruption (#148742), unrecoverable pruned Desktop sessions (#149784), Group Chat import failures (#149682), split-topology 409s (#148531). Users with long-lived installs are bearing the transition cost.
  • Windows and macOS lifecycle/reliability issues around hermes update (#132645, #135171) are recurring.
  • Policy/heuristic false positives frustrate automation: terminal lifecycle guard (#105758), skill-security scanner deadlock (#94353).
  • Structured-output redaction breaks plugin parsing — shell.exec rewrites 32-hex tokens to abcd12...ef34 (#149778).

Use cases visible in the data: multi-profile gateways on macOS with 5 launchd-supervised instances (#135171); remote Desktop backends with basic auth (#139818, #147387); Bot Mode group rooms (#98004, #149682); cron-driven automation (#145314, #148389); messaging-bot integrations (Slack #110374, Matrix #148265); plugin-driven domain automation (3D printing, accounting).

Satisfaction: High engagement (666 contributors, 850 issues closed) and constructive, detailed bug reports reflect an invested community. Dissatisfaction concentrates on transitional regressions rather than core functionality; several high-visibility items were closed today, which should improve sentiment.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived/open items needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Why it matters
#75833 — Cron state out of jobs.json Since 2026-08-01 Large infra refactor; carries 6 risk labels (session-state, message-delivery, security-boundary, compatibility, Windows, blast-moderate). Long-running, high-blast-radius.
#94353 — Skill approval deadlock Since 2026-08-25 Scanner-refused writes can never be human-approved — a logic deadlock, not a preference issue.
#96906 — Delegation closeout Since 2026-08-28 Awaiting maintainer decision; prior PR deferred. Roadmap ambiguity.
#97681 — Cross-gateway bot collaboration Since 2026-08-29 Highest-demand feature; "current review queued" — needs prioritization signal.
#105758 — Lifecycle guard false-positive Since 2026-09-08 Dev-workflow blocker; needs-decision label outstanding.
#110374 — Slack status broken (👍16) Since 2026-09-13 Highest-reaction bug; simple dependency-surface fix with outsized user-visible impact.
#121796 — xAI grok-4.7 effort allowlist Since 2026-09-24 One-line allowlist extension; needs-repro despite trivial root cause.

Bottom line: Hermes Agent is a high-throughput, fast-moving platform in the middle of a major architectural consolidation (unified gateway). Release cadence and contributor base are strong; the primary health risk is migration-path regressions across legacy DBs, split topologies, and Desktop remote connections. Clearing the tagged fix PRs and completing the entry-point cutover (#145171) should be the maintainers' near-term focus, alongside the cheap-win Slack allowlist fix (#110374).

IronClaw — nearai/ironclaw

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw is in a high-velocity, release-quiet phase: 46 tracked items moved in the last 24h (14 issues, 32 PRs) with zero new releases, indicating the project is mid-cycle and accumulating fixes/features rather than shipping. Activity is strongly PR-weighted (32 PR updates vs. 14 issues, 20 open / 12 closed or merged), and roughly half of the visible PRs have already moved to Under Review. The work clusters around four themes: plugin ecosystem hardening (install, dependency checks, hook isolation, console routing), durable session storage and pagination, Matrix channel reliability, and Windows platform parity. Issue traffic is dominated by memory/retrieval correctness bugs (#8040, #8580, #8276) and a hard blocker in Creator review workflows (#8592). Overall health reads as actively maintained with a growing bug surface in secondary subsystems — no release pressure, but several multi-week-open defects are now recurring.

2. Releases

None. No new versions published in the last 24h, and the "Latest Releases" feed is empty.

Context inferred from issue reports: the most recent published build referenced by users is 2.2.2.post1, while testers are running Desktop 2.3.0b2 / 2.3.0b3 with a qwenpaw 2.4 backend package and reme_ai 0.4.2.0. This version skew between the release channel and the beta branch is itself a signal worth watching — several reports (e.g. #8585, #8580) were filed against beta/desktop builds that are ahead of the public release.

3. Project Progress

Of the 20 highest-signal PRs, 6 are closed/merged (the remaining 6 of the 12 closures fall outside the top-20 sample). Notable landings:

PR Change Impact
#7842 Isolate synchronous plugin hooks + event-loop lag watchdog (#7840) High — a blocking time.sleep/subprocess.run in any plugin previously froze the host's single-threaded asyncio loop; this is the most consequential stability fix in the batch
#6659 Model fallback with cooldown (fixes #2199, #1327, #2089) High — automatic failover on rate limits, timeouts, service errors
#6788 Shared root profile workspace for ACL store Fixes Telegram/ACP channels rejecting previously approved users on every new task
#7738 Filter unrecognized kwargs before OpenAI completions.create() Removes streamIdleTimeoutMs-class TypeError from proxy/middleware layers
#8558 Simplify Matrix legacy state migration and device locking Unblocks valid Matrix accounts; follow-up to #8187
#8597 view_audio tool catalog translations Console i18n completeness

In-flight majors: #8532 (XXXL: append-only per-session SQLite history, paginated history, native Turn forks), #8586 (XXXL: unify ACP and native session configuration), #8598 (XXL: plugin dependency-check refactor), #8472 (XL: reranker model center with multi-query precision history).

Engagement is concentrated on Issues; PR comment counts are unreported (undefined) in this dataset, so ranking below is issue-driven.

  1. #8040 — 8 comments (opened 2026-09-30, still open). Embedding reindex silently drops a whole batch when one CJK chunk exceeds the provider's per-item token limit, while the loop logs processed=126/126. Marked a recurrence of #5950. Underlying need: users need observability and atomicity in batch jobs — partial failures must not be reported as success, and index reconciliation must be trustworthy. The recurrence label suggests the first fix addressed the symptom, not the root batching contract.
  2. #7026 — 4 comments, CLOSED. chat_template_kwargs auto-injected without extra_body wrapping → openai SDK TypeError on all calls with deepseek-v4-pro. Underlying need: the provider compatibility layer must not leak raw kwargs into SDK calls; related to merged #7738.
  3. #8276 — 4 comments. ReMe reranker enablement accepts an empty api_key, surfacing only as "unexpected error". Underlying need: fail-fast config validation with actionable messages rather than generic error swallowing — the second ReMe memory-config defect this cycle.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, with fix-PR status:

Severity Issue Status / Fix
Critical #8040 embedding reindex drops batches silently (CJK token limit); recurrence of #5950 No linked fix PR. Open 37 days — highest-risk item

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows a high-velocity, security-hardening phase consistent with the run-up to the v0.9.0 release: of 30 issues touched in the last 24h, 25 remain open/active and 5 closed — three of which were priority:p1 / release:v0.9.0 identity-access security bugs (#11127, #11123, #12051, #12046). PR throughput is unusually high at 50 updated (48 open, only 2 merged/closed), indicating a review bottleneck: many substantial PRs (#11289, #11313, #12244, #11286) are marked do-not-merge or status:blocked and are stacking on dependencies. A large cluster of issues and PRs authored by JordanTheJet and Audacity88 (#12245–#12254, #12246, #12247, #12248, #12249) reveals a coordinated "scoped dashboard chat" + identity-access follow-up campaign in flight. No new releases were cut today.

2. Releases

None. No new releases were published in the last 24h. Note that multiple merged/closed items and open PRs carry the release:v0.9.0 label, suggesting the next cut is being staged but is not yet ready (several blockers below).

3. Project Progress

Only 2 PRs merged/closed in the window (both outside the top-20 shown), so concrete landing is light relative to activity. However, 5 issues closed, three of which are security-relevant:

  • #11127 [CLOSED] Session-data tools bypass principal ownership checks (S0 security)
  • #11123 [CLOSED] SOP execution accepts wildcard tool selectors without tools:execute (S0)
  • #12051 [CLOSED] sop_workshop apply scoped-principal privilege escalation
  • #12046 [CLOSED] Non-admin wildcard tool selectors retain operator-only tools
  • #10526 [CLOSED] RFC accepted/completed: append-only session event history + deterministic state replay

Notable PRs advancing features (open, not yet merged):

  • #12258 sessions_prompt tool for inter-agent prompting
  • #12259 scaffold for async sessions_message (RFC #11027 / #11119)
  • #12059 runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
  • #11194 Microsoft Teams channel
  • #11680 Firecrawl web search provider
  • #11744 reasoning streaming in Telegram/Slack drafts

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Signal Link
#10526 RFC: append-only session history / deterministic replay 16 comments (most discussed), now closed Issue #10526
#8132 Evaluate Rust/WASM web UI vs React/Vite 13 comments, 1 👍, still open since June Issue #8132
#10926 Matrix send_via treats peers as rooms 8 comments, priority:p2 Issue #10926
#9779 SOP sops_dir default silently ignored 7 comments, priority:p1 Issue #9779
#11703 Deferred tool activation busts prompt cache 5 comments, cost/perf Issue #11703

Underlying needs: The community is converging on durable, replayable, attributable session state (#10526, #9597) — the recurring theme across the most-discussed threads is that ZeroClaw's conversational state model is too mutable and fragmentation across logs/receipts/control-plane is causing observability and attribution gaps. The WASM web-UI debate (#8132) reflects a desire to eliminate the Node/Vite toolchain from the runtime for supply-chain and simplicity reasons.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (fix PR status noted):

S0 / p1 — Security (mostly resolved):

  • #11127, #11123, #12051, #12046 — closed today, but reviewers explicitly flag that #11126 (OPEN) is only partially addressed by PR #10412 and "landing that PR alone must not be treated as" full resolution. #11126
  • #11124 [OPEN] SOP decision gate ignores strict fallback — S0, no fix PR referenced #11124
  • #11126 [OPEN] Queued session ops retain revoked admin ownership — partial fix in #10412 #11126

S2 / degraded behavior:

  • #10926 Matrix send_via peer-vs-room misresolution #10926
  • #9572 Gateway WebSocket turn overflows Tokio worker stack (dev profile) #9572
  • #12145 Plugin store limiter leaves wasmtime default 10,000 memories/tables per store — memory budget bypass #12145
  • #12043 & #12225 glob_search silently drops authorized matches under allowed roots (two related defects, opposite directions) #12043, #12225
  • #12228 cron update --agent reports success but never reassigns #12228
  • #12194 Unknown model silently falls back to 32k context window, failing valid turns #12194
  • #12047 OIDC bearer verification has no attempt limiter/outbound cap (DoS/amplification) #12047
  • #12050 OIDC callback page has no browser binding (login CSRF) #12050

S3 / minor:

  • #11703 prompt cache bust on deferred tool activation #11703
  • #12236 cached HTTP clients shared across test runtimes → flaky "dispatch task is gone" #12236

Assessment: The S0 cluster closure is a genuine health win, but the security surface is still active — OIDC (CSRF, rate-limiting), WASM sandbox limits, and glob_search authorization semantics all have open, high-risk threads with v0.9.0 labels and no confirmed fix PRs.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Session durability & inter-agent messaging — #9597 (durable peer-agent turns), plus PRs #12258 (sessions_prompt) and #12259 (async sessions_message). Strongly points to a sessions/messaging subsystem landing in the next version.
  • Web-managed attachments — #12181 (dashboard document upload, first #9488 Phase 2 Web slice) #12181
  • Non-admin dashboard chat — #11984 & #12247 (scoped chat for signed-in non-admins) #11984
  • Provider breadth — Firecrawl web search (#11680), Microsoft Teams channel (#11194), OpenRouter balance (#11845/#11846)
  • Rust/WASM UI migration — #8132, still under evaluation

Prediction for next version (v0.9.0): session/messaging primitives, scoped dashboard chat, and identity-access hardening are the most likely headline features; provider integrations (Firecrawl, Teams) may slip unless review unblocks.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Cost & performance sensitivity: User Audacity88 repeatedly flags prompt-cache busting (#11703) and hidden 32k context fallback (#12194) — real production friction around token spend and silent degradation.
  • Silent-failure frustration: A recurring theme across #9779 (SOP never loads), #12228 (cron update false success), #12043/#12225 (glob_search silently drops files) — users are repeatedly burned by operations that report success but do nothing. This is the single strongest dissatisfaction signal in the data.
  • Security researcher engagement: IftekharUddin and Audacity88 are filing detailed, well-scoped S0/p1 reports, indicating active adversarial review — good for long-term health, but signals the authorization model needs a consolidation pass rather than point fixes.
  • Maintainer-load pressure: JordanTheJet's follow-up PRs suggest the team is doing disciplined post-review cleanup, but the volume of stacked do-not-merge/blocked PRs implies review capacity, not contribution, is the current bottleneck.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or blocked items warranting maintainer attention:

  • #8132 (open since 2026-06-22, 13 comments) — WASM UI evaluation, needs-author-action; decision debt accumulating for ~4.5 months. #8132
  • #9597 (open since 2026-07-31) — durable peer-agent turns, status:in-progress, no landing yet. #9597
  • #9779 / #9770 (open since early August) — SOP and cron silent-failure bugs, both priority:p1, both still open ~3 months. #9779, #9770
  • PR #11313 — config set/patch not published to running daemon; priority:p1, release-gate, needs-maintainer-review, open since 2026-10-01. Auth-policy staleness is a real operational risk. #11313
  • PR #11289 — stable RPC denial reason identifiers; open since 2026-09-30, do-not-merge, risk:high. #11289
  • PR #11286 — bind gateway pairing tokens to roster users; open since 2026-09-30, domain:security, priority:p2. #11286
  • PR #12244 — scoped dashboard chat; status:blocked on #11964 and #12232, do-not-merge, release:v0.9.0. This is the critical path for the dashboard-chat campaign. #12244

Bottom line: ZeroClaw is healthy on contribution volume and has clearly closed a meaningful security milestone today, but review throughput and stacked dependencies (esp. #12244 → #11964/#12232, and #11126 → #10412) are the gating factors for the v0.9.0 release. The most actionable health signal is the cluster of silent-failure bugs, which represent the clearest user-trust risk.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-06

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-06 02:48 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity, high-pressure operating state: 500 issues and 500 PRs were touched in the last 24h, with 186 PRs merged/closed against 314 still open and 253 of 500 updated issues closed. Activity is dominated by maintainer-driven cleanup (steipete, vincentkoc, obviyus), security-adjacent work around access-policy and staged-commit authority, and a stream of CI/test hardening PRs. However, the issue tracker shows a persistent cluster of P0/P1 crash-loop and data-loss regressions tracking back to the 2026.9.x–2026.10.x line, several with 15–75 comments and no merged fix. One release shipped (v2026.11.1), but it is a small hardening patch rather than a regression-closing update. Overall: very active, but stability debt on long-lived regressions is accumulating and needs maintainer triage.

2. Releases

v2026.11.1 — small, safety-focused patch:

  • Safer Mac settings: failed config saves no longer overwrite secrets; disabling Tailscale exposure preserves Gateway authentication (#187734, #187664; fixes #187600, #187597; thanks @anmol0b).
  • More reliable channel replies: Telegram, Discord, and webhook delivery robustness improvements (release note truncated in source data — full changelog should be verified on the release page).

No breaking changes or migration notes are stated in the provided excerpt. Notably, none of the top P0 regressions below are fixed in this release (e.g., #160959, #166017, #191847), and #141474's fix is explicitly noted as shipping in v2026.11.5-beta.1, not stable v2026.11.1.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today show steady incremental hardening rather than headline features:

  • MCP App content durability: #193812 preserves saved MCP App display content after view expiry via session-owned custom-entry lane.
  • Recovery model selection: #193719 keeps recovery models selectable across providers when a personal-account pin is missing (closes #193770).
  • Memory-wiki correctness: #193469 (closed) stops wiki lint treating commented/escaped [[wikilinks]] as live links.
  • UI performance: #193479 (closed) reduces long-session streaming onset work by retaining prepared history in the bounded projection cache.
  • CI/test hygiene: #193887 (closed) retires a redundant Swift portability adapter; #193870, #193904 rework CI admission for historical runs and PostgreSQL conformance.
  • QA/test reliability: #193908 awaits Workshop enable before reload.

Feature work advancing in open PRs: access-policy revision publishing (#182383), staged PostgreSQL authority at physical commit (#193842), OpenClaw ID Gateway membership authority behind Labs flag (#192335), and an opt-in "portable research" tool (#173964).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Theme
#160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (P0) 75 Plugin capture regression from 2026.9.6 stalls the event loop
#177656 — Native host exec shared-state integrity-admission error (P1) 29 Authority/admission model breaking native exec
#170956 — Windows slow startup, unclean shutdown, schtasks EPERM (P0) 29 Windows managed-service reliability
#178359 — doctor --fix idles 15+ min (P1) 25 Doctor/repair-path hangs
#166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable 24 SQLite recovery leaves agents permanently UNAVAILABLE
#191944 — gateway stop fails: "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" (P2) 19 Process-census/service-inspection reliability
#40001 — write tool lacks append mode; cron destroys shared files (P0) 17 Silent data loss in isolated sessions

Underlying need: the community is converging on a single meta-theme — the shared-state/integrity-admission and service-child lifecycle model introduced around 2026.9.x is producing a long tail of hangs, permanent-unavailable states, and recovery dead-ends. Users are not asking for features; they are asking for deterministic recovery after crashes and restarts.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / crash-loop & data-loss (no fix PR confirmed merged):

  • #160959 — Gateway event-loop block for minutes on large plugin capture (75 comments, diamond-lobster rating). Highest-impact open issue.
  • #166017 — mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs default not applied; MCP runtimes never evicted, spawn broker hits 256-child cap, all exec/read/MCP start fails. (linked PR open.)
  • #170956 — Windows restart/update unreliability (schtasks permission + unclean plugin shutdown).
  • #40001 — write overwrites instead of appending; isolated cron causes silent shared-file data loss.
  • #161921 — post-state-migrated-no-rollback deadlock between doctor --fix and plugins update.
  • #70903 — persistent provider cooldown blocks users for hours after billing recovery.
  • #142821 — default-on transcript redaction poisons replayed agent context (security + data-loss).
  • #158912 — MEMORY.md no longer injected at bootstrap on 2026.9.6 (docs mismatch, session-state/security).

P1 regressions:

  • #191847 — 2026.10.10: 512 MB SQLite worker OOM kills every turn in large sessions ("admission is closed").
  • #155563 — service-child relay/anchor and MCP groups retained after successful turns (2026.9.5 regression).
  • #134993 — Gateway pegs one CPU core in filesystem discovery with large skill/agent fleets.
  • #162637 — native Codex completion handoff fails with SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED.
  • #182647 — cloud-worker turns fail with "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" (labeled queueable-fix).
  • #118793 — Claude CLI session-limit error bypasses model fallback chain.

Exceptionally long-lived: #40001 (#40001) has been open since 2026-03-08 — ~8 months — despite being P0 data-loss. #70903 since 2026-04-24.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Progress streaming for Feishu/Lark (#131457) — parity with Slack/Discord/Telegram/Matrix/Mattermost/Teams; likely candidate once channel-delivery hardening in v2026.11.1 settles.
  • Append mode for write tool (#40001) — arguably a bug fix, but explicitly a missing capability; high candidate for near-term.
  • --prompt-file for openclaw infer model run (#140244) — small, low-risk automation ergonomics.
  • Disable hosted plugin catalog feed (#164620) — privacy/air-gap demand.
  • Control UI: browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after /new (#158800) — UX continuity.
  • Failure-only notifyOnExit mode (#141973, closed stale) — noise reduction.
  • Session tool-set explainer (PR #192713, closes #192712) — strong debuggability signal; likely to land soon.
  • First-run provider→chat flow (PR #193892) — onboarding friction fix.

Prediction for v2026.11.x: expect the #141474 recovery fix (already in v2026.11.5-beta.1) to reach stable, plus CI/authority-model hardening and the Control UI onboarding/model-catalog fixes. Feishu streaming and write append mode are less certain for the immediate next tag.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Recovery is not trustworthy. Multiple users report that after a crash, restart, or update, the system lands in a state that requires the other subsystem to fix it first (doctor ↔ plugins update deadlock, permanent UNAVAILABLE agents, "admission is closed"). This is the dominant emotional theme in high-comment threads.
  • Windows is a second-class platform. schtasks EPERM, slow startup, unclean shutdown, and the fact that Windows CI covers only ~0.6% of test files (#126874, closed stale) are repeatedly cited.
  • Silent data loss is the most feared failure mode — cron overwriting shared memory files, transcript redaction propagating into commands/files/replies, and stale async results replaying into the wrong Discord channel (#135117).
  • Cost/caching surprises — Anthropic prompt cache stuck at ~46k prefix (#140129), cache never reused (#182891) — direct billing anxiety.

Satisfaction signals: users are actively filing highly detailed, reproducible reports with version pins and logs; several explicitly credit the team's responsiveness (e.g., #187468 confirmed update-failure report). The maintainers' clawsweeper triage labels (diamond lobster / gold shrimp ratings) show a maturing triage process that contributors respect.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention — high severity, low or stalled momentum:

  1. #40001 — P0 data-loss, open since 2026-03-08, no fix PR, needs product decision. Most overdue P0.
  2. #70903 — persistent provider cooldown blocks paying users post-billing-recovery; open since 2026-04-24, stale.
  3. #160959 — highest-comment P0 (75), needs maintainer review, no fix PR.
  4. #142821 — redaction poisoning agent context; security review requested, linked PR open since Sept.
  5. #134993 — CPU pegging with large fleets; open since 2026-09-01.
  6. #126874 — Windows CI coverage gap; closed stale but the underlying risk (unverified Windows path) remains and correlates with #170956.
  7. Stale-but-unresolved product decisions: #150743 (QQ channel long-term support after Tencent handoff stalled), #164620 (disable hosted catalog feed), #124306 (exec approval card doesn't flag mount-point targets before rm -rf — a safety gap worth prioritizing).
  8. PR risk: #173964 (portable research, XL, security-boundary, "needs proof") and #192335 (OpenClaw ID membership authority) are large security-boundary changes that need explicit review bandwidth; #191509 is an accidental empty placeholder that should be closed.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw, snapshot 2026-11-06. Comment/reaction counts and issue states are as reported in the provided dataset.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Agent / Assistant OSS Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-06 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, IronClaw Method note: Figures are single-day (24h) community digests. OpenClaw's "500/500" counts appear to be a dataset cap and should be read as ≥500, not a true ceiling. Counts measure items touched, not net-new work.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The ecosystem is converging from "chatbot with tools" to durable, multi-surface agent runtimes, and the current fault line is no longer model capability but session authority, migration integrity, and plugin isolation. Four of the five projects are simultaneously rebuilding their state layer — append-only session history, deterministic replay, and gateway-mediated session ownership appear independently in OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw. Release posture splits cleanly: Hermes is shipping from a large release train, OpenClaw is patching a mature but debt-laden core, and QwenPaw/ZeroClaw are pre-release, accumulating review-queue backlogs. The strongest cross-project user signal is not feature demand but trust in recovery and failure reporting — silent data loss and "success that did nothing" outrank missing features in every tracker.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Merge/Close Throughput Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw ~500 touched / 253 closed ~500 touched / 314 open 186 merged/closed (~37%) v2026.11.1 — small hardening patch; top P0s unfixed 6.4 / 10
Hermes Agent 50 (47 open / 3 closed) 50 (44 open / 6 merged) 6 merged (~12%) v0.23.0 "The Hearth" shipped Nov 5 (~1,950 PRs, 666 contributors) 8.0 / 10
QwenPaw 14 32 (20 open / 12 closed) ~12 closed/merged (~38%) None; public 2.2.2.post1 vs. beta 2.3.0b3 skew 5.5 / 10
ZeroClaw 30 (25 open / 5 closed) 50 (48 open / 2 merged) 2 merged (~4%) None; v0.9.0 staged but blocked 5.9 / 10
IronClaw 0 0 — None n/a (dormant)

Scoring rubric (composite, 0–10): activity/throughput 25% · release cadence 20% · stability & regression debt 35% · review throughput/maturity 20%. Scores are analyst judgment, not vendor metrics.

Reading the table: OpenClaw operates at roughly 10× the daily item volume of any peer. Hermes has the healthiest ratio (one large, coherent release with spin-out tracking issues). ZeroClaw's 2-of-50 merge rate is not low contribution — it is a review bottleneck with substantial PRs stacked behind do-not-merge/status:blocked dependencies (#12244 → #11964/#12232; #11126 → #10412).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers

  • Breadth of integration surface — the only project in the set with mature parity across Feishu/Lark, QQ, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Mattermost, Teams, and webhooks, plus MCP app content durability and a Control UI.
  • Operational depth — doctor --fix, managed Windows services (schtasks), macOS Tailscale/Gateway auth handling, process-census service inspection. Peers are still building desktop/serve entry points; OpenClaw already has repair tooling (that occasionally deadlocks).
  • Triage maturity — clawsweeper severity ratings (diamond lobster / gold shrimp) and reproducible, version-pinned reports. This is the most institutionally mature tracker in the set.

Technical approach differences

  • Monolithic gateway with an integrity-admission / shared-state authority model introduced around 2026.9.x. Where Hermes is consolidating into a unified gateway, OpenClaw is absorbing the cost of having done so earlier — the entire P0 cluster (#160959 event-loop stalls, #177656 admission errors, #166634 permanent UNAVAILABLE, #161921 migration deadlock) is downstream of this design.
  • Staged PostgreSQL commit authority (#193842) and access-policy revision publishing (#182383) show OpenClaw pushing further into transactional session authority than any peer.

Community size comparison

  • OpenClaw's top thread carries 75 comments; Hermes' 227; ZeroClaw's 16; QwenPaw's 8. OpenClaw dominates volume of distinct reporters, while Hermes dominates per-thread consensus-building.
  • Decisive gap: ~500 items/day vs. 30–50 for peers. OpenClaw is the de facto reference implementation by traffic, but that scale is precisely what exposes its stability debt — #40001 (P0 data loss) has been open since 2026-03-08, ~8 months, with no fix PR.

Positioning verdict: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's substrate and cautionary tale — highest capability and adoption, lowest marginal stability per shipped feature. Its competitive risk is not a feature gap but trust erosion on recovery paths while Hermes closes the integration gap at a healthier ratio.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific Needs Observed
Durable, append-only session state + deterministic replay All four active OpenClaw: session-owned custom-entry lanes (#193812), SQLite recovery dead-ends (#166634). Hermes: unified-gateway session authority (#145171), cron state → cron/runtime.db (#75833). QwenPaw: append-only per-session SQLite + paginated history + turn forks (#8532). ZeroClaw

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

Date: 2026-11-06 Repository: github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Today's Overview

Hermes Agent shipped v0.23.0 "The Hearth Release" on November 5, 2026 — a massive cycle since v0.22.0 (~10,080 commits, ~1,950 merged PRs, ~850 issues closed, 666 contributors). Activity remains extremely high: 50 issues updated in 24h (47 open/active, 3 closed) and 50 PRs updated (44 open, 6 merged/closed), consistent with a large-scale, high-velocity open-source project in active maintenance. The dominant theme of ongoing work is stabilization of the unified gateway (#106742), which merged Oct 14 and continues to generate follow-up defects in session state, Desktop connection, and profile scoping. Community engagement is substantive — the top tracking issues carry 200+ and 40+ comments respectively — suggesting a mature user base running multi-profile, multi-surface deployments. Overall project health looks strong on throughput, with moderate risk in post-merge regressions around sessions and gateway routing.

2. Releases

v0.23.0 — "The Hearth Release" (released 2026-11-05)

Scope since v0.22.0:

  • ~10,080 commits · ~1,950 merged PRs
  • ~8,720 files changed (~725,200 insertions, ~201,400 deletions)
  • ~850 issues closed · 666 contributors

Notes:

  • The release framing ("Hermes kept the threshold…") suggests a gateway/entry-point consolidation theme, consistent with the unified gateway work landing in this cycle.
  • Breaking changes / migration notes: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt. Given the unified-gateway rollout (#106742), users with standalone hermes serve, Desktop URL/Cloud/SSH modes, and standalone profiles should expect migration behavior changes — see the migration command (hermes gateway migrate --multiplex) referenced in #149682. Treat this release as a protocol/plumbing transition release; verify Desktop remote connections and Group Chats after upgrade.
  • Tracked known post-release issues include profile-scoped auth (PR #149813) and local image upload regressions on Desktop v0.23.0 (#149770).

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed today (6 PRs / 3 issues), highlights via closed items and fix PRs in flight:

  • #134889 [CLOSED] — Tracking issue for unified gateway post-merge fixes (227 comments). Closure signals the primary stabilization wave for one-gateway-per-local-session is complete; remaining work has been spun out.
  • #139818 [CLOSED] — Remote-backend Desktop sessions unresumable (session.resume → not_found) is resolved; a notable Desktop remote-backend reliability win.
  • #149787 [CLOSED] — Desktop Scheduled view: script-only (no_agent) run rows now openable with real output preview.
  • PR #137942 [CLOSED] — Bot-mode turn subprocess now bounded by the 600s per-attempt deadline (was an unbounded subprocess.run holding the per-profile delivery lock). Prevents wedged-child deadlocks.
  • Follow-on work formalized: #143547 (open, 50 comments) now carries remaining unified-gateway problems; #145171 tracks the entry-point cutover of serve, remote Desktop, and web onto gateway session authority.

Feature work advancing (open PRs):

  • #149630 — /undo now cross-references /rollback for file restoration (checkpoint awareness).
  • #149786 / #149746 — CI cost reduction (same-runner job merging) and npm → pnpm 12.15.0 workspace migration.
  • #75833 — Cron scheduler state moved out of jobs.json into per-profile cron/runtime.db (long-running infra refactor).

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #134889 — Unified gateway post-merge tracking (CLOSED) 227 The defining workstream of this release cycle; massive coordination surface.
2 #143547 — Remaining unified-gateway problems 50 Continuation issue; still active the same day #134889 closed.
3 #139818 — Remote desktop session resume fails 41 (👍3) High user impact, now closed.

Underlying needs: Users are running multi-profile, multi-surface setups (CLI + TUI + Desktop + messaging bots + cron) and want them to behave as one coherent system. The unified gateway pain is the cost of that consolidation. Separately, federation/collaboration between personal agents (#97681) is the clearest "next platform" demand.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / High severity (recent, tracked):

  • #149682 — Group Chats imported via hermes gateway migrate --multiplex fail first turn for every member with runtime_draining (room session title collides with standalone-era Group: <room> row). Migration-day blocker; no linked fix PR yet in provided data.
  • #149784 — Desktop sessions become permanently unrecoverable (admission_conflict) after 90-day pruning; routing entries never refreshed, restore won't self-heal. Data-availability risk; no fix PR shown.
  • #148742 — Legacy state.db without INTEGER PRIMARY KEY id accumulates NULL-id rows post-upgrade → compression fails with int(None), attempts_exhausted. Upgrade-path corruption risk; no fix PR shown.

P1 / P2 (open):

  • #149770 — Desktop local image uploads fail ("session not found") when a legacy remote profile overrides the negotiated wire. Regression in v0.23.0.
  • #148531 — owner-backfill 409s "Exclusive maintenance refused" on every desktop boot in split topology.
  • #147387 — Auth-gated dashboard rejects Desktop token-mode credentials (WebSocket upgrade always rejected).
  • #148389 — Kanban worker hangs at startup on Windows (never issues model request, zero TCP connections).
  • #132645 — Windows: hermes update leaves host gateway down when a named profile is sticky.
  • #135171 — macOS: update SIGTERMs launchd wrapper/helper processes as "manual gateways"; warning never clears.
  • #110374 (👍16, highest-reaction bug) — Slack status indicator silently broken with slack-sdk >= 3.44 (agents.sessions.setStatus rejects free-text/empty).
  • #148457 — browser.executable_path to a sandbox-capable Chromium still launched with --no-sandbox on AppArmor-userns hosts (security-relevant).

Fix PRs in flight:

  • #137562 — Desktop clarify-lock expiry.
  • #148265 — Matrix prose sanitizer deleting text resembling attributes.
  • #149802 — /stop-cancelled delegation incorrectly waking the parent session.
  • #149813 — Remote Config Nous token resolved under wrong (production) secret scope.

Pattern: Post-unified-gateway, the split-topology / legacy-DB / profile-scoping seams are the dominant defect class. Migration from standalone backends is the highest-risk path right now.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #97681 (40 comments, 👍4) — Bots collaborate across gateways (across machines now, across owners next). Strong candidate for the next platform milestone.
  • #102269 — Bot Marketplace: discover/review/install "bot packs" via profiles + distribution.yaml. Natural commercialization/ecosystem bet.

  • Plugin ecosystem is visibly growing: new catalog submissions for PrintWatch (3D printers, LAN mode) #149803, qbo-ops (QuickBooks Online) #149801, and proofops (completion-claim verification) #149625.

Prediction for next release (v0.24.x): entry-point cutover completion, remote/Cloud/SSH Desktop onto gateway sessions, cross-gateway bot messaging foundation, and continued migration hardening (Group Chat imports, legacy state.db). Bot Marketplace likely remains a larger future milestone.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Migration/upgrade fragility dominates: legacy state.db corruption (#148742), unrecoverable pruned Desktop sessions (#149784), Group Chat import failures (#149682), split-topology 409s (#148531). Users with long-lived installs are bearing the transition cost.
  • Windows and macOS lifecycle/reliability issues around hermes update (#132645, #135171) are recurring.
  • Policy/heuristic false positives frustrate automation: terminal lifecycle guard (#105758), skill-security scanner deadlock (#94353).
  • Structured-output redaction breaks plugin parsing — shell.exec rewrites 32-hex tokens to abcd12...ef34 (#149778).

Use cases visible in the data: multi-profile gateways on macOS with 5 launchd-supervised instances (#135171); remote Desktop backends with basic auth (#139818, #147387); Bot Mode group rooms (#98004, #149682); cron-driven automation (#145314, #148389); messaging-bot integrations (Slack #110374, Matrix #148265); plugin-driven domain automation (3D printing, accounting).

Satisfaction: High engagement (666 contributors, 850 issues closed) and constructive, detailed bug reports reflect an invested community. Dissatisfaction concentrates on transitional regressions rather than core functionality; several high-visibility items were closed today, which should improve sentiment.

Item Age Why it matters

#121796 — xAI grok-4.7 effort allowlist Since 2026-09-24 One-line allowlist extension; needs-repro despite trivial root cause.

Bottom line: Hermes Agent is a high-throughput, fast-moving platform in the middle of a major architectural consolidation (unified gateway). Release cadence and contributor base are strong; the primary health risk is migration-path regressions across legacy DBs, split topologies, and Desktop remote connections. Clearing the tagged fix PRs and completing the entry-point cutover (#145171) should be the maintainers' near-term focus, alongside the cheap-win Slack allowlist fix (#110374).

8. Backlog Watch

Bottom line: ZeroClaw is healthy on contribution volume and has clearly closed a meaningful security milestone today, but review throughput and stacked dependencies (esp. #12244 → #11964/#12232, and #11126 → #10412) are the gating factors for the v0.9.0 release. The most actionable health signal is the cluster of silent-failure bugs, which represent the clearest user-trust risk.

AI 基础设施日报 2026-11-06

生成时间: 2026-11-06 02:48 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目 AI 基础设施对比 — 2026-11-06

1. 生态概览

活动集中在两个领域：服务栈加固和内存/量化效率。vLLM 正在处理高严重性的 v0.32.0 回归问题，同时推进分布式服务、Rust 前端对齐和 RL 权重重载工作流。llama.cpp 和 Ollama 继续在本地运行时内核、后端和内存方面的工作，而 LiteLLM 正在修复网关级流式传输、工具调用和速率限制的正确性问题。Unsloth 正在推进微调和扩散/视频内存效率。SGLang 的摘要生成失败，因此被排除在定性比较之外，但在活动表中有所记录。

2. 活动对比

仅在来源摘要提供数据时报告计数；n/r = 未报告。

项目 Issue 数量 PR 数量 发布状态
vLLM n/r；关联大量活跃 issue n/r；关联大量活跃 PR 过去 24 小时无发布；v0.32.0 已确认存在回归
SGLang n/a n/a 摘要生成失败
llama.cpp n/r n/r 滚动构建已发布：b12131–b12143
Ollama n/r n/r 无发布；稳定版 0.40.14，0.40.15-rc2 测试中
LiteLLM 95 个已更新 500 个已更新 v1.108.1 已发布，含 cosign Docker 签名验证
Unsloth n/r n/r 无发布；活跃 PR 队列涉及 Studio、扩散、视频、RAG

3. 模型支持竞赛

vLLM 在前沿 LLM 服务覆盖和分布式执行方面领先。 它正在推进 DeepSeek-V4.1 任意流水线阶段分区、MiniMax-M3 用于 prefill/decode 的上下文并行，以及 GB10/DGX Spark SM121 作为新兴目标。它还在跟踪 Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming，但这仍是一个请求。

llama.cpp 在本地/边缘架构和后端广度方面领先。 它新增了 xing4_0 架构支持、Blackwell MXFP4 W4A8 matmul、WebGPU MEAN、Vulkan IQ4_NL、Metal bf16 matmul 以及 Hexagon 后端工作。这是广泛的硬件/量化覆盖，而非数据中心服务。

Unsloth 在扩散/视频和微调硬件驻留方面领先。 它正在为 B200/GB200/B300 级显卡添加 NVFP4 步进保护、Lumina-Image-2.0 激活尺寸调整、面向 16 GiB L4 的 MiniMax-H3 slab 压缩、CUDA 13/cuDNN 选择、集成 GPU GGUF 加载以及 CPU 上下文并行。

LiteLLM 在提供商/API 规范化方面领先，而非模型内核。 它正在为 Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1/Sonnet 5/Haiku 5.5 添加 Bedrock 原生结构化输出、为 Seedance/MiniMax 添加 OpenRouter 视频字段、Vertex AI Cloud TTS 区域端点以及 Codex 特定版本的模型目录。

Ollama 目前在新区模型/硬件支持方面相对落后。 它有 Hindsight hs-decide-1-flash 请求/MLX PR、Qwen3.5 0.8B 量化请求以及 qwen35/qwen35moe 并行服务重新启用，但 Intel Arc 和 Arrow Lake Vulkan 支持仍是未解决的问题。

4. 性能前沿

优化工作按层次划分：

  • vLLM — KV 缓存、注意力、MoE、分布式服务。 工作包括 GDN prefill 原地 SSM 状态、Blackwell 上 TRT-LLM 单体 MoE 填充移除、通过 CUDA 复制引擎的 PP 交接、ROCm MXFP8 GEMM 重新调优、RoPE+KV 缓存融合、tokenizer 池浅拷贝以及 RL 的直接权重重载。
  • llama.cpp — 本地内核、内存映射、MoE 缓存。 Checkpoint 保存/恢复现在使用引用计数共享状态而非深拷贝；MoE 专家缓存报告 QFN 上解码 +6%、GLM 上 +7%、专家上传减少 8%；Vulkan/Metal/WebGPU 内核持续扩展。
  • Ollama — 本地运行时内存与调度。 MLX Qwen3.8 内存调优、Strix Halo/gfx1151 的统一内存 APU 调度以及应用启动的惰性语法高亮。一个 25–30% t/s 回归报告因需要更多信息而被关闭。
  • LiteLLM — 网关开销与路由效率。 流开销指标工作、调用方超时约束的重试、rpm/tpm 计数修复以避免过早 429、提示缓存亲和性用于

各项目详细报告

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 文摘 — 2026-11-06

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但项目在 Rust 前端对齐路线图、Q4 SIG 路线图以及一系列 Blackwell/ROCm 问题上有大量活动。今天最具影响力的信号是 v0.32.0 中影响 DeepSeek-V4.1 块大小选择的回归（修复跟踪于 #60762），以及 Qwen4Exp/Qwen3.8 在 262K 预填充边界处的崩溃，该问题出现在 v0.31.1 与 v0.32.0 之间。RL 训练直接权重重载（#54477 及后续 PR）的工作也明显在加速推进，有望成为默认方式。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内无新版本发布。

值得关注的迁移/配置说明：

  • v0.32.0 在 DeepSeek-V4.1 上的回归：发布标签上没有有效的块大小（64 和 128 均失败）。修复跟踪于 #60762；原始报告 #59203（已关闭）。
  • Rust 前端（VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1）仍为实验性，且相对于 Python API 服务器明确功能不完整。参见路线图 #44280。
  • 直接权重重载（VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct）正在向默认方式过渡；PR #66002 增加了模型选择加入机制并拒绝已知的静默路径，因此运维人员应预期在其变为隐式默认之前会有配置层面的门控变更。
  • XPU 分布式后端正在从 xccl → xccl2 迁移，旧版已弃用：#64818。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • DeepSeek-V4.1：任意流水线阶段分区支持正在推进（#63106）；允许在 KV 共享层组内部进行 PP 切分，而当前 NVIDIA 路径会拒绝此操作。
  • MiniMax-M3：单节点 NVLink TP2/TP4 上使用 FlashInfer CAKE 的预填充和解码索引器上下文并行（CP）（#61929）。
  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming（0.6B 多语言流式 ASR）已请求支持：#47455。
  • Rust 前端即插即用 API 服务器持续向对齐推进 — 跟踪：#44280。
  • GB10 / DGX Spark（SM121） 正在成为受支持的目标，但存在已知的逐张量 H2D 权重加载开销（#58726）以及 FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4 元数据崩溃（#50774）。

4. 性能与优化

已合入 / 审查中：

  • Qwen3.5/3.8 和 Qwen3-Next 线性注意力的 GDN 预填充原地 SSM 状态 — 当预填充行是全新的或完全缓存时，每层减少 4–5 个 gather/mask/cast/scatter 内核（#64498）。
  • TRT-LLM 单体 MoE：在 Blackwell 上为 block-FP8/MXFP8 将 DP 填充行排除在专家计算之外（#65972）。
  • 通过 CUDA 复制引擎进行 PP 交接（仅限 NVLink） — 0-SM 复制以减少流水线并行步骤中的 SM 争用（#65896）。
  • Tokenizer 池现在仅对 Rust 后端进行浅拷贝，而非对整个 tokenizer 执行 deepcopy（#65674）。
  • ROCm MXFP8 dot_scaled GEMM 重新调优，针对 gfx950 上 MiniMax-M3.1 TP4 线性层；M=17–256 瓦片重塑（#65530）。
  • RoPE + KV-cache 融合现在可通过显式请求或文档化的选择加入在 ROCm/AITER 上使用（#57900）。

回归 / 未解决的性能问题：

  • MiniMax-M2.7 TP4+EP 吞吐量回归，跨越 0.29、0.31、0.32：#63705。
  • Qwen3.5 397B NVFP4 DEP8：在 8×B200 上混合预填充-解码步骤比仅解码慢约 6 倍：#44806。
  • ROCm / MI355X 性能跟踪，针对 Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B（#57149）和 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next（#59575）。
  • GB10 权重加载因从 safetensors mmap 视图进行逐张量 H2D 而缓慢（#58726）。
  • 异步 KV 拉取在完成拉取后出现 1.0–1.8 秒的重新排队停顿；RFC 提议进行队首重新准入（#62532）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. v0.32.0 在 DeepSeek-V4.1 上的块大小回归 — 发布标签上没有可用的块大小（64 和 128 均失败）。修复跟踪于 #60762；原始：#59203。
  2. Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GPU 崩溃 — 当单次预填充跨越 262,144 原生边界时出现 CUDA 非法内存访问。在 v0.31.1 上正常，在 v0.32.0 上损坏：#62383。
  3. NixlConnector KV 损坏 — 远程 READ 正在进行时，KV 块在租约到期时被释放；解码可能静默消费被覆盖的 KV。正确性 bug，未引用可见修复 PR：#61229。
  4. DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE 置换索引 bug — 存储在权重池中的置换索引在二级睡眠下被清零，导致重载时每一行都变成第 0 行的副本。修复：#66010。
  5. 二级睡眠 + 排队请求 — 如果在 reload_weights 完成之前触发 wake_up()，在 L2 睡眠期间排队的请求可能在已丢弃的权重上运行。修复：#65326。
  6. FlashInfer 采样器 JIT 在默认 wheel 安装中无法发现 nvcc 时导致引擎启动崩溃（无原生采样器回退）：#49497。
  7. SM120 自适应验证门控 — enable_adaptive_verification 在 SM120 上被拒绝（设备查询透镜门控为 SM90/SM100）：#63343。
  8. Qwen3.5-9B 混合 GDN + 动态 LoRA 在长序列上出现 NaN（punica Triton 内核）：#52568。
  9. int8_per_token_head KV 正确性 — 开启前缀缓存时损坏输出（池被钉在 100%）：#50702；禁用前缀缓存时损坏首批生成的 token：#50749。
  10. ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash "Workspace is locked" 在高解码并发下 rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits 中出现 AssertionError：#64874。
  11. EngineCore 断言 在 _update_from_kv_xfer_finished 中，当异步 KV 连接器报告已中止/已释放请求的传输完成时：#43226。
  12. ROCm AITER FA 跳过 1 token bug — CK 路径上的 min_seqlen_q=1 丢弃单 token 提示。修复 PR（已关闭/已合并跟踪）：#65722。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 谨慎固定版本。 v0.32.0 有两个已确认的回归（DeepSeek-V4.1 块大小、Qwen3.8/4Exp 262K 预填充崩溃）。如果你使用这些模型，请留在 v0.31.1，直到 #60762 和 #62383 解决。在生产中采用 v0.32.x 之前请跟踪这两个问题。
  • KV 连接器用户（P/D 分离）： NixlConnector 租约到期 bug 是静默的 — 你可能看到看似合理但错误的输出，而非崩溃。如果你依赖去中心化服务，请关注 #61229，并考虑固定到已知良好的连接器版本，直到修复落地。
  • 共享集群上的睡眠/唤醒（L2）： L2 睡眠 + 排队请求路径可能在过期权重上提供服务。#65326 中的修复尚未合并；如果你使用睡眠模式进行 RL/评估交换，请在编排中将 wake_up() 门控在权重重载完成之后。
  • 混合 + 量化 KV 用户： 如果你在 Gemma-4 或类似模型上运行 int8-per-token head KV 并开启前缀缓存，请注意两个正确性 bug（#50702、#50749）。作为安全网，在解决之前请禁用前缀缓存。
  • Linux/ROCm 用户： 若干 AITER 和 workspace-lock 问题（#64874、#65722）影响多租户解码工作负载；如果你在 ROCm 上服务 GLM-5.3-Flash 或单 token 提示，请在高负载下显式测试。#65530 中的 M=17–256 MXFP8 重新调优可能会显著改善 MiniMax-M3.1 TP4 吞吐量（>仅瓦片选择变更，但值得基准测试）。
  • 跨越 262K 的长上下文智能体： Qwen4Exp 崩溃在预填充边界处可精确复现 — 如果你构建具有超大工具/系统提示的智能体，要么在单次预填充中保持在 262,144 token 以下，要么固定到 v0.31.1。
  • RL / 微调团队： 直接权重重载工作（#54477、#64352、#66002）正在快速收敛；预计近期会切换为默认，现在就开始审计自定义加载器 — 新的选择加入模型将拒绝之前静默不正确的路径（参见 #66010 了解正在捕获的此类 bug）。
  • Rust 前端： 尚未准备好用于生产 — 在 #44280 的对齐检查清单关闭之前，将 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 视为实验性。
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

⚠️ 摘要生成失败。

llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp 摘要 — 2026-11-06

今日亮点

llama-server 落地了一项以内存为重点的变更，用引用计数的共享状态替代深拷贝的检查点（b12141），同时还伴有 Vulkan 和 Metal 内核方面的工作（b12143、b12138）。在 PR 方面，Blackwell 借助 mxf8f6f4 MMA 获得了 MXFP4 W4A8 路径（#31747），而一种混合 MoE 专家缓存报告了可测量的解码收益（#31233）。稳定性仍是主导主题：量化目标上的投机解码正确性（#25618）以及与 MTP 相关的崩溃（#31077、#30698）仍处于开启状态。

发布与破坏性变更

无公开 API 破坏。值得注意的行为变更：

  • b12137 — 服务器拒绝非对象的实时会话更新。 此前格式错误的负载会抛出未捕获异常并终止服务器；现在发送无效会话 JSON 的客户端将收到错误响应，而不再是崩溃。请审查任何自定义的 Realtime 兼容客户端。
  • b12140 — YaRN 的 truncate=false。 长上下文 RoPE 缩放现在可以避免将校正间隔边界舍入为整数；需主动启用，且向后兼容。
  • b12131 / b12132 — server/common 中移除 u8path()，改用 generic_string()。属于内部清理，但值得在 Windows 上对非 ASCII 模型路径做回归测试。

新模型与硬件支持

  • Blackwell MXFP4 W4A8 matmul — 使用 kind::mxf8f6f4（m16n8k32、scale_vec::1X）的 mul_mat 路径，激活量化为 e4m3，每 32 个值使用 ue8m0 缩放，对应 e2m1 权重（#31747）。
  • xing4_0 架构 — 完整注册、张量加载、HF→GGUF 转换，以及 mHC/MLA/MoE/MTP 的计算图；无新增 ggml 算子（#31589）。
  • WebGPU：MEAN 算子已落地（b12135）；COUNT_EQUAL 正在评审中，用于 ggml-opt 的 token 准确率统计，目前回退到 CPU（#31578）。
  • Vulkan IQ4_NL 标量 MMQ 整数点积着色器，面向不支持 coopmat 的 GPU，沿用 IQ4_XS 的先例（#31764）。
  • Metal bf16×bf16 matmul 内核已添加，同时将 mul_mm 扩展到 32 <= K < 64（b12138）。
  • Hexagon：set_tensor_n 后端 API，以及重打包/分块稳健性修复（#31744）。
  • OpenAI 兼容的 /v1/audio/speech 端点正在评审中，基于已关闭的 mtmd 音频输出设计 issue 构建（#31763、#21956）。

性能与优化

  • 检查点内存开销降低 — 在槽位保存/恢复中，用引用计数的 shared_ptr 检查点列表和 common_state_data 缓冲区替代深拷贝（b12141）。
  • MoE 专家缓存（ClassLRU） — 类 LRFU/MQ 的混合方案，报告称在热缓存下相比 SLRU 达到 QFN 上解码 +6%、GLM 上 +7%、专家上传减少 8%（#31233）。
  • Vulkan FWHT 内核扩展到块宽度 > 512，且现在可直接接受 F16 源，覆盖子组和共享内存两条路径（b12143）。
  • Vulkan flash-attention 行分块将验证 token 和 GQA 头打包进一个 tile，以共享 K/V 读取（WIP/RFC）（#30190）。
  • Linux mmap：提议移除 MAP_POPULATE，该选项目前会阻塞直到整个模型被换入（#28055）。
  • WASM relaxed SIMD 点积实现，用于浏览器构建（#19590）。
  • Qualcomm Adreno Vulkan 变通方案正在进行中：为 rms_norm 添加运行时循环次数，以避免展开变体被错误编译（[#30824](https://github

Unsloth Digest — 2026-11-06

1. Today's Highlights

No releases landed in the last 24h, but the PR queue is very active on two fronts: Studio desktop/chat UI polish and lag fixes (glass theme, long-chat scrolling, floating browser), and serious perf/memory work on the diffusion and video paths (Lumina-Image-2.0, MiniMax-H3, NVFP4 step protection). A notable correctness/performance item surfaced in RAG ingestion: embeddings run at batch-of-1 per document (~99 ms/chunk vs 2.07 ms batched).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24h. However, a forward-compat break is flagged:

  • transformers 5.23 renames gradient checkpointing → activation checkpointing, with 4 behavior-changing spots in Unsloth. Old names remain as aliases until v6, but Trainer reads only new names. (#16667)

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • NVFP4 diffusion on sm_100-class cards (B200/GB200/B300): W4A16 step-protect schedule auto now default, protecting first/last NVFP4 steps. (#16759)
  • Lumina-Image-2.0: added measured activation sizes, improving int8 residency on 16–24 GB cards. (#16808)
  • MiniMax-H3: host-reserve-aware slab compaction to avoid OOM on 16 GiB L4. (#16849)
  • CUDA 13 / cuDNN selection fix for stable-diffusion.cpp builds (reads CUDA major from DT_NEEDED). (#16789)
  • Integrated GPU GGUF loading: memory-map oversized models and read lookup tables from disk. (#16857)
  • CPU backend: context parallelism now engages (or refuses explicitly) instead of silently falling back to DDP. (#16802)

4. Performance & Optimization

  • RAG ingest batching gap: _embed_all is called per document; small-file corpora hit the batch-of-1 path at ~99 ms/chunk vs 2.07 ms batched (~48×). (#16715)
  • Diffusion LoRA training: removed per-micro-step host syncs, single decode per cached image, streamed int8 base load — bit-identical numerics. (#16763)
  • Video memory planning: forward headroom now counted before keeping whole-module offload, preventing first-forward OOMs. (#16805)
  • Long-chat UI lag on Linux: offscreen message bodies parked behind measured placeholders to unblock WebKitGTK style/layout. (#16854)
  • Pipeline parallel on CPU: chunked cross entropy now runs on last stage instead of silently falling back to full [rows, vocab] logits. (#16846)
  • sd.cpp installer: retries transient downloads before stepping down to CPU build. (#16788)

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  • High — RAG throughput regression: ~48× slower ingest for multi-document corpora. (#16715)
  • High — Image generation falls back to CPU/RAM on Windows 11 / RTX 3060 while text gen correctly uses GPU. (#16803)
  • Medium — Studio fine-tuning job list drops cancelled queued jobs when a newer job starts (multi-LoRA interaction); CLOSED. (#16632)
  • Medium — Fine-tuning pagination can skip a job when Multi-LoRA batches start out of order; open follow-up. (#16720)
  • Medium — Cursor invalidation race when Multi-LoRA batch starts during a list request. (#16719)
  • Medium — Download never resumes on Windows (v0.1.915-beta). (#16810)
  • Low/Medium — Long-conversation UI lag on web + desktop; fix PR exists. (#16603, #16854)
  • Low — Glass theme inconsistencies and full-background blur; several reports. (#16770, #16820)
  • Low — search_conversation tool disappearance (3rd recurrence). (#16706)
  • Low — AppImage startup failure on Slackware64 (GLib/AppIndicator symbol); CLOSED. (#16605)
  • Low — Homebrew cask unsloth unavailable despite docs; CLOSED. (#16672)
  • Tool-calling correctness: GLM/MiniMax/Kimi/DeepSeek/Seed-OSS in-process routes return tool calls as plain text (finish_reason: "stop") — fix PR open. (#16824)

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • RAG builders: until batching is fixed, chunk aggregation across documents is your only lever — the per-document embed call dominates ingest cost.
  • Tool-using agents: validate finish_reason and parse embedded <tool_call> blocks if you run GLM/MiniMax/Kimi/DeepSeek/Seed-OSS in-process; the fix is in flight but not merged.
  • Windows + NVIDIA users: verify image-gen actually lands on GPU — silent CPU fallback is reported on RTX 3060.
  • Multi-LoRA fine-tuning pipelines: pagination and job-list consistency issues exist; treat queue listings as eventually-consistent and reconcile by job ID.
  • Frontier stack (transformers 5.x): pin or prepare for the checkpointing API rename; behavior changes in 4 spots even with aliases present.
  • Serverless/small-GPU diffusion: NVFP4 step protection and measured activation tables materially change residency on B200-class and 16–24 GB cards — good time to re-run memory plans.
